title: The chain
line: A chain of about √x theta lifts
summary: Each lift adds a layer of divisibility. The chain’s length, between √x and 2√x lifts, balances cost against error at the square root.
story: The GUIDE’s size table fixes the number of lifts m between √x and 2√x. That is the square root Alpöge singles out in his note: he says Claude suggested the chain’s length.

`UpperBound` builds the chain. Source forms are lifted m times between definite hermitian spaces X₀ → X_m and restricted to Y_m: the composite lift. The seesaw identity (`Seesaw/SeesawIdentity`) says that the lower chain applied to Poincaré series is a constant times this composite lift. `UpperBound/Divisibility` and `UpperBound/Size` then show the lifts are highly divisible and not too big.

That gives Theorem A (`Reduction/ShortAndEnough`): a multiple of the projected Poincaré series has short lifts and small index. `Spanning` proves Theorem B with a second-moment argument (Bessel functions, unfolding): a few translates span almost all of the target forms. Together they are the upper half of the main inequality.

modules.title: Theorem A (short forms) and Theorem B (enough forms)
modules.group: Three theorems and the main inequality
modules.note:
The source is the space `ramifiedSourceForms` of ramified source forms. It lies in the space
`SourceForm` of all source forms, whose dimension is written `D_X`. The target is the space
`targetForms`, whose dimension `D.targetDim` is written `d_T`. We define the translates `s 𝔭` of the
map `𝔭` from the source to the target and prove Theorems A and B: the source is spanned by integral
forms `φ` whose images `s 𝔭 φ` have short lifts `Θ₁ s 𝔭 φ`, these images have small index, and the
images of few translates span almost all of the target.

Notions from other files:
* `D.poincare` is the Poincaré map `𝒫` from source forms to the forms on `Y₀`, without the factor
  `poincareScale`, which the number `c_ss` (`D.seesawConst`, entering as its inverse in
  `D.scaledInclusion`) absorbs. `D.chosenGL` is the finite group `Ḡ` acting on the forms on `Y₀`,
  with the central projection `e₀` to the good part.
* `D.Θ ϑ` is the chain of lifts `Θ_ϑ` of target forms for the twist `ϑ`.
* `D.targetLattice` records which target forms are integral at each `ι`, and its `IndexLe y δ` says
  that at every `ι ∣ l` the family `y` becomes integral with loss `δ_l`, where `∑ δ_l log l ≤ δ`.
* `D.gain l` is the divisibility asked of the chain at `l`; `D.errorUnit` is `f a log³ b`, with
  `D.logB` standing for `log b`.
role: Theorem A: a multiple of the projected Poincaré series has short lifts and small index.
Theorem B: few translates span almost all of the target forms.

modules.title: Galois conjugates of jets of theta functions and archimedean bounds for jets
modules.note:
An automorphism `σ` of `ℂ` over `K = ℚ(√-d)` acts on the jets of theta functions. This action is
realized as a `σ`-semilinear map `L` on `𝒮 V`, whose laws hold on `V.finitePart`. We then prove
archimedean bounds for the conjugates of the jets of admissible combinations of the operators
`New.Space.finHeisenbergOp` applied to the integral vacuum, moved by finite points of a pair of
groups.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Parameters.exists_isJetConjugation`: existence of `L`;
  `New.Parameters.IsJetConjugation.exists_map_schrodingerOp`: its action on the vacuum `vacElem` and
  on the data `Ψ ⊗ vacElem` for Schwartz–Bruhat functions `Ψ`;
  `New.Parameters.IsJetConjugation.norm_map_intVacuum_le`: a bound, with constant `P.constantBound`,
  for the images of the translates of `ω g (intVacuum V)`; it rests on
  `New.Parameters.norm_omega_vac_le`.
* `New.Parameters.norm_jet_le_of_isVacuumCombination` and
  `New.Parameters.sqrt_weylNormSq_schurJet_le_of_isVacuumCombination`: archimedean bounds for the
  conjugates by `σ ∈ Aut ℂ` of the jets, and for their Schur matrices;
  `New.Parameters.isVacuumCombination_of_isAdmissibleCombination` makes them apply to admissible
  combinations.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters.E`: The field `P.E s = K(ζ)`, for a primitive root of unity `ζ` of order
  `P.q₁ s`; `P.Φ s` is the set of its infinite places, a group isomorphic to `Gal(E/K)`.
* `New.Parameters.jetScale`: A nonzero complex number, the period factor times the area scale over
  the period `Ω₀`, at which Taylor series of theta functions are scaled.
* `New.Parameters.bigOmega`: The real number Ω = exp(γ − Re L′/L(1, χ_K))·2π/rd_E, with γ Euler's
  constant and rd_E the root discriminant of E.
* `New.Parameters.intVacuum`: The vacuum of rank n multiplied by the n-th power of a fixed number
  that makes its values at finite vectors integral.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.𝒮`: For a space V of rank n, a Banach space of integrable functions on 𝔸^n on which the
  Heisenberg and Weil representations act. Applied to an adelic vector, `f : 𝒮 V` gives the value
  of its theta function.
modules.literature:
Related work: Bannai–Kobayashi, Algebraic theta functions and the p-adic interpolation of
Eisenstein–Kronecker numbers, 2010; Kings–Sprang, Eisenstein–Kronecker classes and integrality of
critical values, 2019; Katz, p-adic L-functions for CM fields, 1978.

The Galois action on theta functions with complex multiplication and on the finite Weil
representation is known; see `Lib.Weil.DualPair.KernelLaws` for sources.

modules.title: p-adic gauge bounds for one theta lift and data from functions modulo an ideal
modules.note:
This file derives `p`-adic bounds for one theta lift between the definite spaces with index types
`n` and `n'` from bounds on jets. A function `Ψ` on `n' × n` matrices modulo a modulus `𝔪`, put at
the places dividing `𝔪` with the integral vacuum elsewhere, gives a datum. If the values of `Ψ` are
integral away from `q`, an integer multiple of this datum is a standard datum at the primes not
dividing `q`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Kernel.raises`: the additive monoid of data that multiply gauges by at most `max c 0`.
* `New.Parameters.omega_mem_raises_of_schurJet_le`: a standard datum translated by `(1, x * d * y)`,
  with `d` diagonal at the places above `p` that define the gauge and `x`, `y` integral above `p`,
  raises gauges by at most `max B 0` for any bound `B` on the weighted entries of the jet matrices.
* `New.Parameters.mem_raises_of_standardData`: an explicit bound for a standard datum itself.
* `New.Parameters.smul_mem_raises_of_dvd`: if a multiple of a datum is standard and the scale is
  `p`-integral, an explicit larger multiple of the datum does not increase the gauges.
* `New.Parameters.smul_vacuumDatum_mem_standardData`: if `q * N` lies in `𝔪` and the values of `Ψ`
  are integral away from `q`, an explicit integer multiple of the datum is a standard datum at every
  prime `l` prime to `q`.
* `New.Parameters.isVacuumCombination_vacuumDatum`: the datum is a combination of translates of the
  scaled vacuum by finite adelic vectors, with coefficients of controlled size.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Kernel`: an abstract theta kernel, that is, a representation `ω` of the finite points of the
  two unitary groups on data and an equivariant map `jetMap` from data to linear maps.
* `New.thetaKernel`: the theta kernel of the definite pair `stdSpace E n`, `stdSpace E n'`; its jet
  matrix is `schurJet κ (jetSeries _ c f)`, with derivatives scaled by `c`.
* `New.weylGauge`: the `p`-adic sup norm of `g⁻¹` applied to `ιₚ ∘ ξ`, where `ιₚ : ℂ →+* ℂ_[p]` is
  the chosen `p`-adic place.
* `New.Parameters.standardData`: the span, over the ring of the complex `z` with `‖ιₚ z‖ ≤ 1`, of
  the translates of the integral vacuum `intVacuum V = vacuumScale ^ card n • V.vacElem` by the
  vectors that `δ` makes integral above `p`.
* `New.Seesaw.IsAdmissibleCombination`: a finite linear combination with conditions on the support,
  the denominators and the size of the conjugates of its coefficients.

modules.title: Rational equivariance, integrality and size of definite theta kernels
modules.note:
This file studies the theta kernels `New.modKernelStdSpace` of a pair of standard definite spaces
`I_L`, `I_N`, whose real datum is determined by a polynomial `Q`. The kernels are evaluated at
finite points. Moving these points by rational elements acts through the two-sided substitutions
`New.Rows.twoSidedSubst`. Here `p` is a number whose prime divisors in `E` are the places at which
integrality is asked. The file builds the normalising constant `New.Rows.modKernelScale` and bounds
the conjugates of a polynomial `Q` homogeneous of degree `d` on polydiscs.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.modKernelStdSpace_embFin_mul`: moving the points by rational elements substitutes the
  variables of `Q` (`New.Rows.twoSidedSubst`) and multiplies by determinants.
* `New.Rows.IsModKernelScale`, `New.Rows.exists_ne_zero_isModKernelScale`: after one
  normalising constant, kernels with `p`-integral input are `p`-integral and, under bounds on the
  sizes of the input, their conjugates are bounded.

Notions from other files:
* `New.stdSpace`: the definite space `I_n`, the sum of `n` norms with its standard lattice.
* `New.Gf`, `New.integralAbove`: the finite adelic unitary group, and its subgroup of points whose
  components at all primes above `p` are integral invertible matrices.
* `New.modKernelStdSpace`: the theta kernel of the datum made of a function `Ψ` on matrices modulo
  `𝔪` and the Fock vector of a polynomial `Q`, for the Weil action twisted by two characters of
  `U(1)`.
* `New.Space.jetSeries`, `New.jet`: the Taylor series of a theta function in Fock's coordinates, and
  the pairing `P(∂) F (0)` of a polynomial `P` with a power series `F`.
* `New.Rows.twoSidedSubst`: the substitution `x_τ ↦ c_τᵀ x_τ g_τᵀ` on complex polynomials in the
  entries of `N × L` matrices `x_τ`.

modules.title: Inserting a block into a parameter
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
The parameters of all chains and grids of spaces are built in one way. There are a stem and a finite
set C of centres, each with a length and a kind, down or up. For B ⊆ C the vector λ⁺_B consists of
the stem and the blocks c + [l_c], c ∈ B, and the sign of an entry is −1 to the power of the number
of centres outside B that are down and above it or up and below it. The parameter λ_B is λ⁺_B
lowered by ½ or by 0, as the parity of the rank requires. Everything is at one infinite place, and
entries are doubled.

* `New.CentreSystem`, `New.CentreSystem.IsSeparated`, `New.CentreSystem.IsParam`: the data, the
  conditions on parities and distances, and the parameter λ_B on a space with these signs, up to a
  common sign σ.
* `New.CentreSystem.IsParam.isBlockRule_insert_of_down`,
  `New.CentreSystem.IsParam.isBlockRule_neg_insert_of_up`: the parameters before and after the
  insertion of a block correspond (`New.IsBlockRule`): the parameters themselves for a down centre,
  their negatives for an up centre.

Notions from other files:
* `HCParam s`: integer vectors l = 2λ indexed by the coordinates of a space with signs s.
* `HCParam.HasGap l h`: the entries of λ are distinct and lie in (n − 1)/2 + ℤ, n the rank, and
  entries at coordinates of opposite signs are at least h apart.
* `centredBlock e d`: the doubled entries of e + [d], where [d] = ((d−1)/2, (d−3)/2, …, (1−d)/2).
* `IsBlockRule γ γ' l l'`, for spaces of ranks n, n': both parameters have a large gap; after
  shifting λ by n'/2 − γ' and λ' by n/2 − γ, the longer one is the shorter one together with a block
  centred at 0; and the two coordinates of a common shifted entry have equal signs if the entry is
  positive and opposite signs if it is negative.

modules.title: Direct and mirror data modulo `N`, and the operator `Up`
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
Let `P` contain one place of each conjugate pair above the split prime `N` of the CM field `E`. A
marked lattice at `P` is a lattice `L` with a vector `ε` of `L / N L` that is non-zero at every
place. Everything here is written in a basis of `L` whose last vector lifts `ε`, at all places of
`P` at once:
* the stabiliser of `(L, ε)` is `mirabolic`, and `diagNInv` takes `L` to `L⁺ = L + 𝒪 ε / N`;
* the direct datum `1[S L ⊆ L', S ε = ε']` is `directDatum`; in bases of `L⁺` and `L'⁺` it is
  `lastRowDatum`;
* the mirror datum `1[S L ⊆ L'⁺] ψ_N (u' (S ε))`, where `u'` is the linear form on `L'⁺` with kernel
  `L'` and `u' (ε' / N) = 1`, is `mirrorDatum` in bases of `L` and `L'⁺`;
* the operator `Up`, which replaces `L` by `L⁺` and sums against `ψ_N` over the primitive vectors
  with unit last entry, is `upOperator`.

A `LiftLaw` records how a lift depends on its datum. On ramified vectors the following hold. A
mirror lift, moved by `diagNInv`, is `Up` after a direct lift, and `Up` moves through a direct lift
up to the factor `γ` of its law. A glued double lift is the number of primitive vectors times a
mirror lift after a direct lift; hence, moved by `diagNInv`, it is a scalar times two direct lifts
after `Up`. So a chain of glued double lifts is a scalar times a chain of direct lifts after a power
of `Up`.

Notions from other files:
* `FinPlace E` is the set of finite places of `E`, `star w` the conjugate place, `LocField w` the
  completion `E_w` with valuation `v` (integral means `v x ≤ 1`) and `ResField w` its residue field.
* `LocProd P` is the product of the `E_w` over `w ∈ P`, and `O` is its ring of integers.
* `stdLattice.selfDualAddChar E` is the additive character of the finite adeles `𝔸f E` fixed by the
  Weil data.
* `liftIntegralFn r f` is `S ↦ f (r S)` on integral matrices `S` and zero elsewhere.
* `compUpTo f j` is the composite `f (j - 1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ f 0` of a chain of linear maps.

modules.title: Descent pairs: descent data for theta lifts to definite unitary groups
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file sets up the theta lift from U(W), with W of rank r, to the definite group U(V), with
V = `New.stdSpace` of rank n > r, and the descent from V to W. One structure, `New.DescentPair`,
holds the data: the places of the level, the space W, an embedding of the indices of its basis into
those of V, a numbering of its basis vectors, the numbers of columns k⁺ and k⁻, and a character of
U(1)(𝔸) with its weight and tame part. The level sits at two finite families of split places
(`New.LevelPlaces`): M, the chosen places `chosenPlace`, and Q, the places `twistPlace` of the
twist. The residue field at w is k_w = `New.ResField w`. The finite datum Ψ_bl ⊗ vac is a vector of
the Weil representation `New.pairWeil` on `Hom(W, V)`: the block datum Ψ_bl, a function of the
reductions of a matrix at M and Q, with the vacuum at the other finite places.

For a descent pair `O`, the character of the descent datum is `O.u1Char`, with weight `O.weight` and
tame part `O.tamePart`. The highest weight of the forms on V is `(O.columnCount, O.detExp)`, given
by numbers of columns. Vectors of the representation of this weight are written ξ, and forms on V
are written Ξ.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DescentPair`: the data of a descent pair; `New.DescentPair.FormV`: its forms on V, with the
  action `New.DescentPair.formAction` of ∏_M GL_r and the Hecke polynomial
  `New.DescentPair.heckePolyOnForms`.
* `New.DescentPair.fockPoly`, `New.DescentPair.blockDatum`, `New.DescentPair.conjKernel`,
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`: the Fock polynomial of a vector, the finite datum Ψ_bl ⊗ vac,
  the conjugate theta kernel as a linear form on weight vectors, and the normalized descent from
  forms on V to functions on U(W)(𝔸).
* `New.DescentPair.blockDatum_eq_sum_modDatum`: Ψ_bl ⊗ vac is the sum of the translates of Ψ¹ ⊗ vac,
  with Ψ¹ = `New.DescentPair.identityBlockIndicator`, by lifts (`New.LevelPlaces.twistResidueLift`)
  of the inverses of the elements of `∏ GL(k_w)` over `Q` (`New.LevelPlaces.TwistGL`).
* `New.DescentPair.paramV`, `New.DescentPair.isHCParam_paramV`: the doubled parameter `l'` of the
  weight of forms on `V`.
* `New.DescentPair.FitsParams`: the data of a descent pair `O` are those of a parameter `l` on `W`
  and `l'` on `V`.
* `New.DescentPair.FitsParams.exists_isJointHarmonic`, `New.DescentPair.FitsParams.isEdge`: then the
  polynomial of the highest vector is a product of joint harmonics (staircases of minors), so it is
  an edge from `l` to `l'`.
* `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent_eq_smul_star_lift_swap`: the normalized descent
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`, defined by a class sum, is a multiple of the descent by the
  datum of the highest vector, the conjugate of the transposed lift (`New.Space.lift` from `V` to
  `W`) of the conjugate form.

Notions from other files:
* `New.levelOf w H`: the subgroup of K₀ = `New.stdLevel` of the elements whose reductions at the
  places `w i` form an element of H.
* `New.levelSpace π K χ`: the vectors on which each k in K acts through π by the scalar χ(k).
* `New.HasHeckePolynomial π hw p y`: y is spherical at the split place w, and the Hecke polynomial
  at T acts on it by p(T).
* `New.IsJointHarmonic`: a nonzero polynomial that is highest, of the lowest K-types, for the row
  and the column actions and harmonic in both directions.

modules.title: Good labels, index types of hermitian spaces, the group 𝖦 and idempotent e₀
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file introduces primitive polynomials and good tuples of labels at one prime. Then, for
admissible data D, it introduces the index types and signs for the bases of the hermitian spaces
X_j, Y_j and W_j.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsPrimitivePolynomial`: irreducible labels with a root of order |k|^r − 1. They are stable
  under scaling the roots by an M-th root of unity if M² ∣ |k| − 1
  (`New.IsPrimitivePolynomial.scaleRoots`). The product of their roots has order |k| − 1
  (`New.IsPrimitivePolynomial.isPrimitiveRoot_prod_aroots_and_exists_pow_eq`).
* `New.goodTuples`: tuples of labels, each without roots among the M-th roots of unity of its base
  field, of which at least one is primitive.
* `New.Data.X`, `New.Data.RowIndex`, `New.Data.Y`: the basis indices of X_j (rank `New.Data.n`), of
  Y_0 (rank r, `New.Data.card_rowIndex`) and of Y_j (`New.Data.RowIndex` and j blocks of size
  `New.Data.t`).
* `New.Data.chosenGL`, `New.Data.e₀`: the product of the groups GL_r over the residue fields at the
  chosen places above p₀, p₁, and the good idempotent in its group algebra. The idempotent is the
  sum of the idempotents `New.tupleIdem` over `New.Data.goodTupleFamilies`.
* `New.Data.isCentralProj_e₀`: `e₀` is a central idempotent.
* `New.Data.hyperplaneSum_mul_e₀`: `e₀` kills pure tensors with a factor `New.hyperplaneSum χ l`,
  `l ≠ 0`, `χ ^ q₂ = 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the data D, with m lifts, block size t and ranks k, n_j = k + j (t + 1) and
  r = k + m − 1; s is its parameter `D.towerExp`, and q₂ = q₂(s) the integer `New.Parameters.q₂`.
* `New.Data.ChosenPlace`: the chosen places above the level prime p_i (i = 0, 1), the finite places
  of E that divide both p_i and the conjugate `D.piM` of an integer of K of norm p₀p₁.
* `New.IsLabel`: a label of degree r is a monic squarefree polynomial c of degree r with c(0) ≠ 0.
* `New.tupleIdem`: the tensor product of the label idempotents e_c of a tuple of polynomials.
* `New.piTensorElem`: the pure tensor ⊗ x_i in ℂ[∏ G_i] of elements x_i of ℂ[G_i].

modules.title: Harish-Chandra parameters, weights and lift diagrams of the definite spaces
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
A weight is given by its last entry and by the number of columns of each height of its Young diagram
at each infinite place of `E`. This file fixes the weights on the spaces `X_j` and `Y_m`. It defines
the Harish-Chandra parameters of the `X_j` and of `Y_m` in decreasing order, the highest weights
`μ(X_j)` and `μ(Y_m)`, and the diagrams of the lifts between the `X_j`. It computes the columns and
bounds the rows of these diagrams, and it shows that `μ(X_m)` and `μ(Y_m)` interlace. It also
computes `n_τ = |μ(X_m)_τ| - |μ(Y_m)_τ|`, where `|·|` is the sum of the entries.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.columnCount`, `New.Data.lastEntry`: the columns and the last entry of the weight on
  `X_j`.
* `New.Data.keptColumns`, `New.Data.columnsY`: the columns of the weight on `Y_m`, obtained by
  branching.
* `New.Data.paramX`, `New.Data.weightX`, `New.Data.liftDiagram`: the doubled parameters and the
  weights of the `X_j`, and the diagrams of the lifts.
* `New.Data.weightX_eq`, `New.Data.weightY_eq`: the weights in terms of their columns.
* `New.Data.branchExponent_eq`: the formula for `n_τ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: data `D` for parameters `P : New.Parameters`. They give a CM field `E`, the number
  `m = D.m` of lifts and a rank `r = D.r`. From these come `k = D.k = r + 1 - m`, `t = D.t = 5 r`,
  the ranks `n_j = D.n j = k + j (t + 1)` and the gap `Δ = D.gap = 2 * D.halfGap = 2 r ^ 8`.
* `X_j`, `Y_m`: the standard definite hermitian spaces over `E` of ranks `n_j` and `n_m - 1`. Lift
  `j + 1` is the theta lift from forms on `U(X_j)` to forms on `U(X_{j+1})`. Branching is the
  restriction of representations from `U(X_m)` to `U(Y_m)`. This file has only their weights.
* `New.Data.Φ`: the set of infinite places of `E`.
* `New.Data.a`, `New.Data.aPlaces`: the integer `a = x b`, for the scales `x` and `b` of the data,
  and the set of `a`-places, the places `≡ 1` modulo `P.q₀`.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the weight `κ_j(σ) = κ(σ) + (j + 1/2) Δ` at `σ`, with `κ = D.weight`. It is
  not to be confused with the column count `New.Data.columnCount`.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: the sequence `λ^Y = (k/2 - 1, …, 1 - k/2; -κ_{1/2}, -κ_{3/2}, …)` at a
  place, where `κ_{i - 1/2} = κ_i - Δ / 2`.

modules.title: Chains of theta lifts, jointly invariant combinations, and free levels
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file treats chains of theta lifts and their jointly invariant combinations for a general
tower of finite adelic unitary groups joined by theta kernels. It shows that, in bounded rank, the
levels that reduce to `1` at the chosen places are free, that is, that they have trivial
stabilisers `New.classAut`. The chosen places of `E = D.E` are the prime divisors of
`New.Data.piM`; `D.f` is the number of infinite places of `E`. For every integral level in bounded
rank, the orders of the stabilisers divide `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.chain`: the composite of the first `j` lifts. It is equivariant (`New.chain_equivariant`),
  and its values are linear in the pure tensor of the data
  (`New.exists_linearMap_chain_eq_apply_pure`).
* `New.IsJointlyInvariant.sum_chain_mem_nsmul`: at free levels, a jointly invariant combination of
  chains is a sum with one term for each tuple of double cosets, with no denominators.
* `New.Data.principalLevel_le_chosenLevel`, `New.Data.classAut_eq_bot_of_le_chosenLevel`: in bounded
  rank, levels that reduce to `1` at the chosen places are free.
* `New.Data.card_classAut_dvd_chosenGroupOrder`: in rank at most `2 * D.n D.m` and for every
  integral level the stabilisers have order dividing `chosenGroupOrder`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.TensorChain`: The complex tensor product S_{j−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ S_0, equal to ℂ for j = 0.
* `New.classAut`: `classAut Γ K g` is Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹, the stabiliser in Γ of the coset gK; here
  Γ = `stdRatPoints` is the rational unitary group of the standard definite space `New.stdSpace`,
  inside the finite adelic group.
* `New.Data.n`: The rank 𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1) of X_j.

modules.title: Index sets, signs and parameters of the grids; the parameters of every step correspond
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
Two grids of unitary groups, `Y` and `Ỹ`, with nodes `(i, j)`, are treated together by a flag `z`
(`false` for `Y`, `true` for `Ỹ`). A node has a base block of `r` (in `Ỹ`, `r + 1`) indices, `i`
added blocks of one kind and `j` of another (`New.BlockIndex`). For `z = false` the node `(i, j)` is
`Y^i_j` with its parameter. For `z = true` it is `Ỹ^j_i` with the negative of its parameter, so that
one formula serves both grids. An offset `o` shifts the second kind of block; the grids have
`o = 0`, and the nodes with `i = 0` are the intervals `[o + 1, o + j]` of the triangles.

* `New.Data.GridIndex`, `New.Data.gridSigns`, `New.Data.gridParam`: index set, signs and doubled
  parameter of a node.
* `New.Data.gridDiagEquiv`: at `(j, j)`, `j ≤ m`, `Ỹ` is `Y` plus one vector of sign `(-1)^j`.
* `New.Data.gridParam_interlace`: at the node `(m, m)` the parameter of `Y` and that of `Ỹ`
  (`-gridParam true`) interlace.
* `New.Data.gridCentres`, `New.Data.isParam_gridParam`: the parameter of a node consists of a stem
  and the blocks of a set of centres (`New.CentreSystem`).
* `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_grid_succ_left`, `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_grid_succ_right`,
  `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_leftPair`: each step inserts a block, so the parameters correspond
  (`New.ParamsCorrespond`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the admissible data `D`, with `m` (even) lifts, the rank `r` (odd), `k = r + 1 - m`,
  `t = 5 r`, the gap `Δ = D.gap = 2 halfGap` and the set `D.Φ` of infinite places.
* `New.Data.RowIndex`: an index set with `r` elements, numbered by `New.Data.basisNumber`.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the centre `w_j = κ_j = κ + (j + 1/2) Δ` at an infinite place, with
  `κ = D.weight`, the gap `Δ = D.gap` and `Δ / 2 = D.halfGap`.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: the target parameter, the vector
  `λ^Y = ([k - 1]; -κ_{1/2}, -κ_{3/2}, …)`, with entries numbered from `0`; the entry `r` is
  `-κ_{m+1/2}`.
* `New.ParamsCorrespond γ γ' l l' s s'`: at each infinite place, the doubled parameters `l` (signs
  `s`) and `l'` (signs `s'`) satisfy the block rule (`New.IsBlockRule`) for the weights `γ`, `γ'`.

modules.title: Levels of the chain, chain data, and the composite lift
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
The map `New.Data.compositeLift` on source forms is built from chains of `m` theta lifts
`X_0 → X_1 → ⋯ → X_m` between definite unitary groups, followed by restriction to the block `Y_m` of
one rank less. Here `X_j` is an index set of `𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1)` elements. The weight at stage `j`
is given by the column numbers `New.Data.columnCount` and the determinant exponents
`New.Data.lastEntry`. This file defines the levels and spaces of forms of the stages, the
restriction from `X_m` to `Y_m`, the kernels of the lifts, the glued datum at `N` in the
Schrödinger model, and chain data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.restrictedChain`: ∑_x Ψ(x) · (chain with the data of x), then `New.Data.restrictToY`.
* `New.Data.IsChainDatum`, `New.Data.compositeLift`: chain data, and the same map for the data glued
  above `N` in each double lift.

Notions from other files:
* `New.classAut`: `classAut Γ K g` is Γ ∩ gKg⁻¹, the stabiliser in Γ of the coset gK; here
  Γ = `stdRatPoints` is the rational unitary group of the standard definite space `New.stdSpace`,
  inside the finite adelic group.
* `New.Data.n`: The rank 𝗇_j = k + j(t + 1) of X_j.
* `New.Data.columnCount`: The number of columns of height h < 𝗇_j at the infinite place τ in the
  weight on X_j; it does not depend on j. For h = 1 it is `D.a` at the places in `New.Data.aPlaces`
  and 0 elsewhere; for h = k ≠ 1 it is κ_1(τ) − ⌊𝗇_1 / 2⌋, with κ_j = `D.liftWeight j`; for h > k
  with h ≡ k mod t + 1 it is `D.gap` − (t + 1); otherwise it is 0.
* `New.chain` (in `New.UpperBound.Objects.LiftChains`): the composite of the first `j` theta lifts.
* `New.Data.chosenLevel` (in `New.UpperBound.Objects.LiftChains`): the integral elements that
  reduce to `1` at every chosen place, that is, at every prime divisor of `D.piM`.
modules.literature:
This file sets up the objects of the upper bound. Related work is listed with the results on them,
in `New.UpperBound.Divisibility.LocalDivisibility`, `New.UpperBound.Seesaw.SeesawIdentity` and
`New.UpperBound.Divisibility.ValuationAtLevel`.

modules.title: Spaces Y_j and W_j, the forms on them, and the target parameter
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file treats the hermitian spaces Y_j and W_j and the forms on them, for admissible data
`New.Data` and a tame character ϑ with modulus Q. The chosen places are the prime divisors of
`New.Data.piM`, written π̄₀π̄₁ as one symbol, with conjugate `New.Data.piMBar` written π₀π₁. These
are one half of the places above M = p₀p₁, and N = ππ̄ is the level. The target parameter ς
(`New.Data.targetParameter`) is a staircase whose lower steps are at least the gap h = 2h₂ apart, so
the spaces of forms `New.Data.principalForms` are finite-dimensional. This file also sets up the
levels and Weil representation data along the spaces Y_j, the gaps of the target parameter, and the
Harish-Chandra parameters on the descent pairs (W_j, V_j).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.spaceY`: the spaces Y_j with their lattices; `New.Data.spaceW`: the diagonal spaces W_j.
* `New.Data.goodForms`: the image of the idempotent e₀ on forms of principal level at the chosen
  places.
* `New.Data.isCuspKernel_typeKernel_paramW`: for signs such that entries of ς at indices of opposite
  sign differ by at least h, the kernel of this parameter (`New.Data.paramW` = 2ς) is a cusp kernel
  of order h₂.
* `New.Data.paramsCorrespond_descentPair`, `New.Data.fitsParams_descentPair`: the parameters on W_j
  and V_j correspond, by insertion of the block of the centre −w_j, and the descent pair (W_j, V_j)
  satisfies `New.DescentPair.FitsParams`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.Data.TameChar`: a character of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 with tame part supported on a finite set Q
  of places of norm prime to MN, Q disjoint from its conjugate.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the weight w_j = κ(σ) + j·h + h₂ at the infinite place σ, with
  κ = `New.Data.weight`, h the gap and h₂ half the gap.

modules.title: The chain of theta lifts ι_μ along the spaces Y_j: level, character and 𝖦-equivariance
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file defines the theta lifts `New.Data.liftY` from forms on Y_j to forms on Y_{j+1} and their
composite, the chain ι_μ = `New.Data.lowerChain`, for a tame character ϑ with modulus Q. It
determines the level and character of the image on Y_m and shows that the chain commutes with
𝖦 = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w). The basis of Y_j is indexed by `New.BlockIndex`, a block 0 of size r followed by
j blocks of size t; `New.blockNumber` is the number of the block.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.lowerChain`, `New.Data.lowerChainAtLevel`: the chain; it lands in the level
  `New.Data.lastLevel`, cut out by `New.Data.lastResidueLevel`, with the character
  `New.Data.lastLevelChar`.
* `New.Data.algFormRep_lowerChain`: how block triangular elements act on the image;
  `New.Data.lowerChain_principalRep`: the chain commutes with 𝖦 = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w) (`New.Data.chosenGL`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.TameChar`: a character of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 with tame part supported on a finite set Q
  of places of norm prime to MN, Q disjoint from its conjugate.
* `New.algFormRep`: right translation by the finite adelic unitary group on algebraic forms of a
  given weight; the weight λ° on Y_m has column numbers `New.Data.columnsY` and determinant exponent
  `New.Data.lastEntry` m.
* `New.Data.spaceY`: the hermitian space Y_j with its lattice 𝖬_j.
* `New.Data.levelPlaces`: the chosen places above p₀, p₁ and the places of the modulus Q of ϑ.
* `New.Data.pointDatumY`: the finite datum on Hom(Y_j, Y_{j+1}), the indicator of the inclusion
  modulo the level places and the vacuum elsewhere.

modules.title: The Poincaré map
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
The Poincaré map `𝒫 = D.poincareAt g t : 𝒜(X₀) → 𝒜(Y₀)` sends a source form `φ` to the form that
represents the Bessel period of `φ` in the Petersson inner product.

Notions from other files:
* `V.Form e`: the automorphic forms of archimedean type `e` on the adelic unitary group
  `G E s = GInf E s × Gf E n` of `V`; `V.quotMeasure` integrates over the quotient by the rational
  points, and `HasLevel z J` says that `z` is right invariant under `J ⊆ Gf E n`.
* `D.SourceForm` is the space `𝒜(X₀)` of algebraic forms on the definite unitary group of `X₀`,
  with values in a Weyl module and of level `D.levelX 0`. `D.principalForms (D.spaceY 0)` is the
  space `𝒜(Y₀)` of forms on the group `G₀` of `Y₀` whose archimedean type is the discrete series of
  doubled parameter `D.paramW` and whose level is `J_M = D.chosenLevel`, the group of integral
  finite adelic points that reduce to `1` at every prime divisor of `D.piM`.
* `Y.besselGroup` is the adelic Bessel subgroup `R(𝔸)` of a grading `Y`, and `Y.besselMeasure`
  integrates over `[R] = R(F) \ R(𝔸)`. For `Y = D.gradingY 0` the group is written `R₀`.
* `Y.sourceFn t φ` is the function `𝒲_φ (u h) = ψ_U (u) · t (ρ (h_∞⁻¹) φ (h_f))` on `R(𝔸)`. Here
  `u` is unipotent, `h` lies in the unitary group of `X`, `ψ_U` is the generic character,
  `ρ = conjWeylRep` is the action on the values of `φ`, and `t` is a linear form on these values.

modules.title: Characters of the lifts of the chain above the level N
modules.group: Source forms, target forms and chains of lifts
modules.note:
This file shows that the characters of the lifts of the chain are unramified above the level `N`.
It identifies the character given by `New.rankTwist` and `New.AutChar.spaceChar` with a base
change. It also moves scalings at the primes dividing π, which lie above `N`, through chains of
lifts. A chain whose data at one lift are fixed by such a scaling annihilates the forms `ψ - z ψ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.spaceChar_rankTwist`: `New.rankTwist` followed by `New.AutChar.spaceChar` gives the base
  change of the character of a lift.
* `New.Data.tensorChainLift_eq_zero_of_ramified`: for the chosen scaling `z_w` at a prime `w`
  dividing `π` and a tensor `t` of the data of the first `m` lifts, take `j < m` such that
  `ω(1, z_w)` on the factor of the lift from stage `j` to stage `j + 1` fixes `t`. Then the chain
  with the data `t` vanishes on the ramified source forms (`New.Data.ramifiedSourceForms`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.N`: The level: a chosen prime N ≡ 1 mod q₂² with log N ∈ [λ, λ + √(log b)], where
  λ = `New.Data.logLevelTarget`.
* `New.Data.liftKernel`: The theta kernel of the lift from forms on X_j (`New.Data.FormX`) to forms
  on X_{j+1}. The finite unitary groups of X_j and X_{j+1} act on its data by ω.
* `New.chain`, `New.doubleLiftChain`, `New.TensorChain.lift`: The chain of theta lifts with data
  Φ_0, Φ_1, …, the same chain taken in pairs with data in S_{2i} ⊗ S_{2i+1}, and the chain with a
  tensor of data.

modules.title: Integrals over a quotient as finite sums over cosets with controlled multiplicity
modules.note:
A finite set of cosets serves as a weighted fundamental domain. For subgroups `S`, `A`, `J` of `H`
and a finite `T ⊆ H ⧸ J`:
* `New.Seesaw.coverMultiplicity`: the number of classes in `S ⧸ (S ⊓ A)` that have a
  representative `r` with `t ∈ r • T` (zero if infinite).
* `New.Seesaw.exists_finset_coverMultiplicity_dvd_pow`: for `H = New.Gf E ι`, levels `J ≤ A` and a
  compact `D` on which the `q ^ n`-th powers of conjugates of `J` fall into `A`, a `T` stable under
  `S ⊓ A` whose multiplicities divide powers of `q` at the points of `T` and at the points with a
  given property that forces their `S`-orbit to meet `D`.
* `New.Grading.exists_integral_eq_sum_over_cut`: if the periods of a function over the Bessel
  subgroup factor over `T` and the multiplicities are non-zero on its support, its integral over the
  quotient of the adelic group `New.G E ε` by the rational points of `New.Grading.besselGroup` is a
  constant times a sum over `T` weighted by the inverse multiplicities.

In these names, a "cut" is such a finite set `T` of cosets.

Notions from other files:
* `New.G E ε = New.GInf E ε × New.Gf E ι`: the adelic unitary group, with its infinite and finite
  parts.
* `New.IsLevel J`: `J` is an open subgroup of the compact open subgroup `New.stdLevel E ι` of
  integral points of `New.Gf E ι`; its index there is `New.stdLevelIndex J`.
* `New.Grading.besselGroup`: the Bessel (Fourier–Jacobi) subgroup of `New.G E ε` attached to a
  grading, with finite part `New.Grading.besselFin` and rational points `New.Grading.ratBessel`.
* `Subgroup.quotMeasure`: the measure on a group that computes integrals over the quotient by a
  subgroup acting on the left; `New.Grading.besselMeasure` is this measure for the quotient of the
  Bessel subgroup by its rational points.

modules.title: Graded lattices, integrality away from q and admissible combinations of translates
modules.note:
This file provides tools for the computations at the finite places of the seesaw. A grading
(`New.Grading`) presents a hermitian space `V` as `X` plus a string of `s` basis vectors, and
`New.gradedLatticeBasis` is an explicit basis of a lattice in it, unimodular when `N = π π̄`.
Integrality lemmas handle numbers integral away from `q` and `l`-adic units.
`New.Seesaw.IsAdmissibleCombination v A n d p B z` says that `z = ∑ r(x) v(x)` with `r` finitely
supported in `A`, denominator `d` away from `n`, and size `B` when `p` holds. Moved vacua
(translates of the vacuum vector of the Weil representation, moved by a finite unitary element) and
the values of the operators `V.schrodingerOp` attached to functions modulo `𝔪` are such
combinations of translates.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Seesaw.integralAway`, `New.Seesaw.IsAdmissibleCoeffs`: complex numbers integral away from
  `n`, and finite families of coefficients with bounded denominator and, on demand, bounded size.
* `New.Seesaw.weightedTranslations`, `New.Seesaw.translations`: finite adelic vectors with given
  denominators away from `q`. They index the translates that may occur in a combination.
* `New.Seesaw.isUnimodular_gradedLatticeBasis_gram`: if `N = π π̄`, the Gram matrix of
  `New.gradedLatticeBasis` is hermitian and invertible over every subring.
* `New.Seesaw.exists_conjTranspose_mul_gradedGram_mul_eq_signMatrix`: for `N > 0` the form is
  congruent over `ℂ` to a diagonal of signs, `(s + 1) / 2` of them negative.
* `New.Seesaw.IsAdmissibleCombination.bind`: substitution; denominators and sizes multiply. The
  rules for scalars, bilinear maps and pure tensors follow from it.
* `New.Seesaw.isAdmissibleCombination_weil_vacElem`,
  `New.Seesaw.isAdmissibleCombination_schrodingerOp`: moved vacua and the values of
  `V.schrodingerOp` are admissible combinations of translates.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with
  xᴴJx equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.gradedGram e N`: the Gram matrix of X plus a string of length s: the identity on X; string
  vectors a, b with a + b = s − 1 pair to 1, or to −N if a = b.
* `New.finMultiplier`: for g in the finite adelic unitary group `New.Gf`,
  Δ_f(g) = υ(det u)|det u|^(−1/2), with υ the splitting character of the Weil data and u a chosen
  invertible matrix with uÔⁿ = Ôⁿ ∩ g⁻¹Ôⁿ.
* `New.AutChar.HasWeight`: μ has weight e and tame part ψ: almost all residue characters ψ_w are
  trivial, and μ(u) = ∏_v u_v^{e(v)} · ∏_w ψ_w(u mod w) whenever u has integral finite part.
modules.literature:
See `New.UpperBound.Seesaw.SeesawIdentity` for related work. See
`Lib.ClassField.Global.CMSplittingCharacters` for sources.

modules.title: The standard lattice of a graded space, line by line
modules.note:
Let `Y` grade the hermitian space `V` by an index set `X ⊕ Unit` of grade `0` and a string of `s`
basis vectors, and let the finite frame of `V` span the same lattice `Λ` as the standard basis
`New.gradedLatticeBasis`. The intersection `Λ⁻` of `Λ` with the span of the string and its
projection `Λ⁺` to this span are sums of lines.

* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.isGraded`: `Λ` is graded.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.mem_latticeMinus_iff`, `New.Grading.SpansLattice.mem_latticePlus_iff`:
  the generators of the lines; they differ only by `N⁻¹` at the middle vector of the string.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.mem_lattice_and_stringProj_eq_zero_iff`: for odd `s`, the
  intersection of `Λ` with the span of `X ⊕ Unit`.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.stringSum_mem_latticeMinus_iff`,
  `New.Grading.SpansLattice.stringSum_mem_latticePlus_iff`: the generators on the lines of the
  vectors `𝔢 ^ i`, for the scale `u = (a / ā) ^ ⌊(s + 2) / 2⌋` and when the constant `c` of `Y`
  has the valuations of `a ā`.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.map_stringMapFin_latticePlus`: under the same conditions, the shift to
  a space with a string of `s - 1` vectors and the same constant `c` takes `Λ⁺` onto `a Λ'⁻`.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.odd_of_notMem_latticeMinus`: a vector of `Λ⁺` outside `Λ⁻` exists
  only for odd `s`.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.exists_place_generates_of_notMem_latticeMinus`: such a vector
  generates `Λ⁺` over `Λ⁻` at some place above `N`.

The results on `Λ⁺` and on the span of `X ⊕ Unit` assume that `N` is split and squarefree
(`IsSplitSquarefree P N π`).

Notions from other files:
* `Y.SpansLattice a π u`: the lattice `Λ = V.lattice 1` has the standard basis
  `New.gradedLatticeBasis Y.indexEquiv a π u` over the integral finite adeles `Ô E`. This basis
  consists of the vectors of `X`, the multiples of the string vectors `b` by `lineIdele a u b`, and
  the last vector `e₀` of `X ⊕ Unit`, replaced for odd `s` by `e₀ / π̄ + u z / (π π̄)`, where `z`
  is the middle vector of the string.
* `IsSplitSquarefree P N π`: `N = π π̄`, where `π` is a uniformiser at the places of `P`, a unit
  elsewhere, and no place of `P` has its conjugate in `P`.
* `Y.stringSum t`: the vector `∑ t i • 𝔢 ^ i`, where `𝔢 ^ i = Y.stringPower i` is a multiple of
  the string vector `i` by an element of `E`.
* `Y.genericConst`: the constant `c` of the grading, a nonzero element of `E` fixed by conjugation.

modules.title: Congruence levels inside the stabilizer of a glued lattice
modules.note:
A grading `Y` of a hermitian space `V` (a choice of basis vectors with a fixed Gram matrix) embeds
the finite adelic unitary group on `X ⊕ Unit` into that of `V`. When the lattice of `V` is the glued
lattice of `Y`, this file gives congruences on an element of the small group that put its image
into the stabilizer of the lattice, or into a congruence level of it.

Notions from other files:
* `Grading V N (X ⊕ Unit) s` splits the index set `ι` of the basis of `V` into `X ⊕ Unit`, on
  which the Gram matrix is `1`, and a string of `s` vectors, orthogonal to it and with a fixed Gram
  matrix that depends on `N`; `Y.inclXFin` is the resulting map on finite adelic unitary groups.
* The glued lattice of `Y` is the `Ô`-span of the columns of
  `gradedLatticeBasis Y.indexEquiv a π u`. For odd `s` it glues the last vector of `X ⊕ Unit` to
  the middle vector of the string.
* `Y.SpansLattice a π u`: the frame `V.xFin` of `V` spans the glued lattice. So in coordinates of
  this frame the glued lattice is the standard lattice `Ô^ι`.
* `IsSplitSquarefree P N π`: `N = π π̄`, the idele `π` is a uniformizer at the places in `P` and a
  unit elsewhere, and `P` contains no place together with its conjugate.
* `congruenceGL M e`: the integral invertible matrices whose rows `e i` agree with those of `1`
  modulo `M`.
* `stdLevel E ι` is the stabilizer of `Ô^ι` in the finite adelic unitary group `Gf E ι`, and
  `levelOf w ⊥` is the subgroup of its elements congruent to `1` at every place `w i`.
modules.literature:
Related work: `Grading.inclXFin_mem_stdLevel` is related to Nikulin's criterion for extending
isometries to an overlattice: the congruence on `h` plays the part of the condition that an isometry
preserve the gluing.

modules.title: Bounds for the lattices of points on graded spaces
modules.note:
Let `Λ'` be the lattice `V.lattice x` of a finite point `x` of a graded space and `Λ` the lattice
of the point `1`. The file proves lattice steps of the induction for the bounds
`Q̄ ^ k Λ⁻ ⊆ Λ'⁻ ⊆ Q ^ (-k) Λ⁻`, where `q` generates `Q`.

* `New.Grading.smul_latticeMinus_le_of_map_latticePlus`: if `sh Λ⁺` is `a` times the `Λ⁻` of the
  next space, then the upper bound on one space and an inclusion `(q̄ / a) sh Λ'⁺ ⊆ Λ''⁻`, with
  `Λ''` the lattice of a point on the next space, give the lower bound on the next space.
* `New.Grading.SpansLattice.hasLatticeBounds_or_latticeSplitsAt`: for a grading over `X ⊕ Unit`,
  duality turns the lower bound into both bounds, unless `s` is odd and `Λ'` splits along `X ⊕ Unit`
  at a place above `N`.
* `New.Grading.LatticeSplitsAt.conj_scalarFin_mem`: if `Λ'` splits along `X` at a place `w ≠ w̄`,
  then the integral scalings of `X` supported at `w` and `w̄` preserve `Λ'`.

Notions from other files:

* `Gf E ι`: the finite adelic unitary group in the variables `ι`, whose elements are the finite
  points. The lattice `V.lattice x` is spanned over `Ô E` by the columns of `V.xFin * x`, where
  `V.xFin` is the finite frame of the hermitian space `V`.
* `New.Grading V N X s`: a splitting of the basis `ι` of `V` into an orthonormal part `X` of grade
  `0` and a string of `s` vectors, where vector `i` pairs only with vector `s - 1 - i`, to `1`,
  except that the middle vector (for odd `s`) pairs with itself to `-N`.
* `Y.latticePlus x`, `Y.latticeMinus x`: the projection `Λ'⁺` of the lattice of `x` to `X^⊥` and
  its intersection `Λ'⁻` with `X^⊥`, the span of the string.
* `Y.stringMapFin Y'`: the shift `sh` from the vectors of one graded space to those of the next.

modules.title: Finite zero terms and the evaluation of pairs of edges in the tower of spaces `Y_k`
modules.note:
For a splitting `D` of a hermitian space `V`, the zero term `D.zeroTerm` along its isotropic frame
is split into a real and a finite part, `New.Seesaw.zeroTermFin D`. For spaces presented by
`New.Grading` as a definite part plus a string of basis vectors, the part of grade zero gives
splittings. On `V⁻ ⊕ V''` this leads to a splitting down to `Hom (X', X⁻ ⊕ X'')` and an evaluation
of finite data, and both are equivariant for `New.Seesaw.tripleWeil`. This evaluation is then
applied to the tower `New.Data.spaceY k`, `k ≤ m = 2 ϱ + 2`, two lifts at a time; here `m` and `ϱ`
are the natural numbers `New.Data.m` and `New.Data.ϱ`.

## Main definitions and results

Throughout, a *string* of a grading is the block of basis vectors outside the definite part, and
`DoubleLiftData` records two successive steps `Y → Y' → Y''` where the first step makes the string
one shorter and the second, unless the string is already empty, makes it shorter by one.

* `New.Seesaw.zeroTermFin`: the finite part of the zero term. It obeys the law of the zero term for
  finite points of the parabolic subgroup (`New.Seesaw.zeroTermFin_omega`) and is not zero at the
  vacuum (`New.Seesaw.zeroTermFin_vacElem_ne_zero`).
* `New.Seesaw.GradeZeroPart`, `New.Seesaw.GradeZeroPart.splitting`: the part of grade zero, and the

modules.title: The neighbour lattice of a pair of edges
modules.note:
Take definite spaces with bases indexed by `X ⊕ Unit`, `X'` and `X'' ⊕ Unit`, written `X`, `X'`,
`X''` for short, and let `e` and `e''` be the last basis vectors of the first and of the third. An
explicit unitary carries the standard lattice of `Hom (X', X⁻ ⊕ X'')` to `neighbourLattice`. Away
from `N` this lattice is the standard one with scaled rows. Above `N` it is a neighbour of the
standard lattice, and the translations `neighbourTranslation` represent it modulo its integral
points. The sums `neighbourCosetRep` of these and of scaled rows away from `N` represent the whole
lattice modulo its integral points.

Notions from other files:
* `𝔸f E` is the ring of finite adeles of the CM field `E` and `Ô E` its subring of integral adeles;
  `star` is complex conjugation and `idem S` is the adele that is `1` on `S` and `0` off it.
* `IsSplitLevel P N`: the places above the prime `N` are those in `P` and their conjugates, all
  split of degree one and unramified.
* `IsSplitSquarefree P N π`: the idele `π` is a uniformiser on `P` and a unit elsewhere,
  `N = π π̄`, and `P` does not meet its conjugate.
* `stdLattice E ι` consists of the vectors with integral entries, `integralBox ι S` of those whose
  entries are integral at the places of `S`; `S.conjClosure` is `S` with its conjugate places.
* `residueOverN y` is the adele `y / N` at `P`, for residues `y` modulo `N` at the places of `P`.
* `Gf E ι` is the group of unitary matrices over `𝔸f E` with rows and columns indexed by `ι`.

modules.title: The vacuum of the neighbour lattice
modules.note:
The sum of the translates of the vacuum by the representatives of the neighbour lattice is computed
on the two edges of the pair. A representative is `neighbourTranslation X X'' y + t`, for residues
`y` and a vector `t` that vanishes above `N`. The translations by the `neighbourTranslation X X'' y`
add up to `doubleLiftGluing`, and they commute with the translations that vanish above `N`. So a
translate of the sum by such a vector is a sum of roots of unity times vectors `gluedTranslate`,
one for each class of the `t`. The result is
`isAdmissibleCombination_finHeisenbergOp_sum_neighbourCosetRep`.

Notions from other files:
* `PairIndex X X''`: the indices of a basis of `X⁻ ⊕ X''`, where each of the two definite spaces
  has a last basis vector.
* `neighbourTranslation X X'' y`: the matrix attached to residues `y` modulo `N` at the places of
  `P`, with `η ȳ / N` (`η` the unit of norm `-1`) in the row of the last basis vector of `X`,
  `-ȳ / N` in that of `X''`, and zero elsewhere. It is supported at the places conjugate to `P`.
* `vanishingAbove ι P`: the vectors that vanish at the places of `P` and their conjugates (for
  split `N`, the places above `N`).
* `AwayLatticeQuotient`, `neighbourCosetRep`: the classes, modulo the integral ones, of the
  elements of the neighbour lattice that vanish above `N`, and the sum
  `neighbourTranslation X X'' y + t` for a chosen representative `t` of such a class.
* `Z.finHeisenbergOp x`, `Z.vacElem`: the translation by a finite adelic vector `x` and the vacuum
  in the space `𝒮 Z`.
* `IsAdmissibleCombination v A n d p B z`: `z` is a finite combination of the `v x` with `x ∈ A`,
  whose coefficients times `d` are integral away from `n` and, if `p` holds, have absolute sum at
  most `B` under every automorphism of `ℂ`.
* `arrowTensor`: the map that joins data on `Hom(V, V')` and `Hom(V', V'')` to one datum on
  `Hom(V', V⁻ ⊕ V'')`.

modules.title: Finite evaluation of edge pairs takes translates of the vacuum to admissible combinations
modules.note:
This file proves that the finite evaluation of a pair of edges takes translates of the vacuum to
admissible combinations. It first gives a test for membership in the lattice of a graded space whose
string has odd length. For a pair of edges it then builds an integral matrix `latticeLift`, whose
adjoint kills the shift and keeps denominators, and uses it to identify the image `L'` of `L ∩ I^⊥`
in `I^⊥ / I` with the neighbour lattice. Here `L` is the lattice of the vacuum and `I` is the
isotropic subspace of the splitting. It follows that the evaluation of a translate of the vacuum is
`0` or a root of unity times a translate of the zero term of the vacuum, and that this zero term is
a nonzero multiple of the sum of the translates of the vacuum by representatives of `L'`. The two
conditions `LiftsNeighbours` and `MatchesDenominators` are checked for the middle double lift and
for the last double lift.

Notions from other files:
* A `Space` is a hermitian space over `E` with a point, an adelic basis that is orthonormal at the
  finite places; the columns of its finite part `V.xFin` span the lattice of `V`. The space `V⁻` is
  `V` with the form negated, and `flipSum V V''` is `V⁻ ⊕ V''`.
* `Grading V N (X ⊕ Unit) m` presents `V` as the orthonormal vectors `X ⊕ Unit` plus a string of `m`
  basis vectors, in which vector `i` pairs only with vector `m - 1 - i`, to `1`, or to `-N` if it is
  the middle vector; `Grading.SpansLattice` says that the point of `V` spans the lattice of the
  basis `gradedLatticeBasis`, in which, for odd `m`, the last vector of `X ⊕ Unit` is glued to the
  middle vector of the string.
* `DoubleLiftData`, called a pair of edges `Y → Y' → Y''`, is the data of two consecutive lifts
  between graded spaces `V`, `V'`, `V''`. It identifies the part of grade zero of `V⁻ ⊕ V''` with
  `(X ⊕ Unit)⁻ ⊕ (X'' ⊕ Unit)` plus hyperbolic planes.
* `IsNeighbourVector π δ c x` lists the congruences that glue the last entries of a vector `x`
  indexed by `PairIndex X X'' = (X ⊕ Unit) ⊕ (X'' ⊕ Unit)` to the coefficient `c`.
* `selfOrConj β` is the allowed denominator: `β` on the first block of indices, `β̄` on the second.
* `IsScalingAtM N β δ κ` says that each factor of `κ` is `1` or `δ`, that `δ` has norm one and is
  `1` above `N`, that `β` is a unit above `N`, and that the denominators of `κ` are bounded by `β`
  and `β̄`.

modules.title: Unfolding the chain of lifts: double lifts and the functions of the unfolding
modules.note:
A double theta integral over two definite unitary groups is a coefficient of the composite of two
lifts. Two unfolding steps give the double lift of the finite evaluation. Starting from `𝒲_φ`, each
unfolding step then gives an equivariant function on the next group `R_j`. Their supports are
bounded when the source form is ramified.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Seesaw.DoubleLiftData.exists_integral_constTermAtStringMap_mul_eq`: take the product of two
  constant terms. Integrate it over the Bessel subgroup `New.Grading.besselGroup` of `Y'`, and over
  that of `Y` against an equivariant function `W`. The result is an integral over the unitary group
  of `X`. Its integrand is `W` times a constant times a theta integral over the unitary group of
  `X'`. The theta integral is of the datum translated by `New.Seesaw.stackedStringMap` and cut down
  along `New.Seesaw.DoubleLiftData.splitting`.
* `New.Data.unfoldStage`: the function `𝒲_{k+1}` that the first `k + 1` unfolding steps leave;
  `New.Data.exists_unfoldStage_eq_algFormCoeff` evaluates it after each double lift.
* `New.Data.hasLatticeBounds_of_unfoldStage_ne_zero`: the support lemma, in terms of graded
  lattices.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Grading`: A presentation of a hermitian space as a definite part `X` (grade 0) plus a string
  of `s` graded basis vectors; `Y.inclX` embeds the unitary group of `X`.
* `New.Seesaw.DoubleLiftData`: For gradings `Y, Y', Y''` of `V, V', V''`, it identifies the
  grade-zero part of V⁻ ⊕ V'' with X⁻ ⊕ X'' plus hyperbolic planes.
* `New.Space.Splitting.zeroTerm`: For a splitting with frames `i`, `k`, the map that sends a datum f
  to y ↦ the mean of f(i y + k b) over adelic vectors b modulo rational ones.
* `New.Seesaw.flipSum`: For hermitian spaces V and V'', the orthogonal sum V⁻ ⊕ V'' of V with its
  form negated and V''.
* `New.Seesaw.stackedStringMap`: The adelic map (T*, T') from V' to V⁻ ⊕ V'', where
  `T = Y.stringMap Y'` and `T' = Y'.stringMap Y''`.

modules.title: The outer variables: finitely many classes, with weights
modules.note:
Let `G_j = Gf D.E (D.Y j)` be the finite adelic unitary group of the hermitian space `Y_j` over the
CM field `D.E`. For each `j ≤ 2ϱ + 1` and each tame character `ϑ` we choose a finite set `Ω_j` of
classes of `G_j` modulo the level `levelY ϑ j`, with multiplicities that divide a power of
`q = ϑ.normQ`. The file defines the weighted sum of a function over `Ω_0 × ⋯ × Ω_{k-1}` and proves
that it is invariant under the levels `D.levelX j` and has coefficients integral away from `q`.

Notions from other files:
* A tame character `ϑ` is an automorphic character of `U(1)` of weight `0` with a finite set `ϑ.Q`
  of places as modulus, and `ϑ.normQ` is the product of the norms of these places.
* The chosen places are the prime divisors of `D.piM`; they lie above the primes `p₀` and `p₁` of
  the data `D`.
* `stdLevel D.E (D.Y j)` is the stabiliser in `G_j` of the standard lattice, and `levelY ϑ j` its
  subgroup of elements that reduce to `1` at the chosen places and at the places of `ϑ.Q`.
* `localLevel n S` is the group of points that are integral at every place in `S`.

modules.title: The seesaw identity and the top of the chain
modules.note:
On the definite space `Y_m`, the integral of a matrix coefficient of a form on `X_m` against a form
on `Y_m` is a multiple of the inner product with the restricted form. To prove the seesaw identity,
we pair `Θ_ξ 𝒫 φ` with a form on `Y_m` and move the Bessel period up the lower chain, one lift at a
time. Each outer integral is a real integral times a weighted sum over the classes `Ω_j`. What
remains is the upper chain for the tensor `φ_ξ`, a multiple of which is the glued tensor of a chain
datum.

Notions from other files:
* `D.spaceY j`, `D.FormY j`: the space `Y_j` of the lower chain and the forms on its unitary group.
* `liftY ϑ j`, `lowerChainUpTo ϑ j`: the theta lift from `Y_j` to `Y_(j+1)` with twist `ϑ`,
  normalised by the index of its level, and the composite of the first `j` lifts.
* `D.poincareAt g t`: the Poincaré map `𝒫` from forms on `X_0` to forms on `Y_0`.
* `Grading`, `unfoldStage`: a grading of a space, with its Bessel group `R`, and the function `𝒲`
  that is left after some steps of unfolding.
* `cutPoints ϑ j`, `cutSum`: the classes `Ω_j` of the finite variables and the weighted sum over
  them.

In the notation of the comments the subscript `ξ` of `Θ_ξ`, `J_ξ` and `φ_ξ` stands for the twist
`ϑ`: `Θ_ξ = lowerChainUpTo ϑ`, `J_ξ(Y_j) = levelY ϑ j`. A `ξ` by itself is the tuple of real parts
of the outer variables. The lattice stabiliser `stdLevel` is written `J°`, and the index
`stdLevelIndex J` is `[J° : J]`. A tame character `ϑ` is an automorphic character of `U(1)` of
weight `0` with a finite set `ϑ.Q` of places (its modulus) outside which its tame part is trivial;
it is a twist if the tame part is nontrivial at every place of `ϑ.Q`. The chosen places, those
dividing `D.piM`, are fixed by the data `D` and do not depend on `ϑ`.
modules.literature:
For ramified source forms φ and every twist, the restricted definite chain of lifts of φ, with data
of controlled support and denominators, is a non-zero constant, free of φ and the twist, times the
indefinite chain of lifts of the Poincaré series of φ. The transfer of a Bessel or Fourier–Jacobi
period under one theta lift is known, locally and globally. Related work: B. Wang, Global theta
lifting and periods associated to nilpotent orbits, 2025; Gomez–Zhu, Local theta lifting of
generalized Whittaker models, 2014; Gan–Ichino, The Gross–Prasad conjecture and local theta
correspondence, 2016.

Each period in the seesaw unfolding is a constant times a finite sum over cosets of a small level,
weighted by reciprocals of stabiliser indices that divide powers of the norm of the twist's
conductor. So the coefficients of the definite chain get no new denominators away from the
conductor. Related work: Gross, Algebraic modular forms, 1999; Hsieh–Namikawa, Bessel periods and
non-vanishing of Yoshida lifts modulo a prime, 2015; X. Zhang, Non-vanishing mod p of theta lifts
for (O(2n+1), Mp(4n)), 2022.

modules.title: A lower bound for the divisibility bound by the gain
modules.note:
Fix a prime `p`. The divisibility bound of stage `j` at `p` measures the `p`-divisibility of a lift;
it depends on a set `S` (also written `ev`) of places whose long rows are removed.

This file defines it and bounds it from below by the gain at `p` when `p < x₁` is non-split. Apart
from an error term, only collisions lose; a collision is a pair `(τ, e)` with `e ∈ I_p` (`e` odd, or
`p = d`) such that `τ` and `(-p ^ e) τ` are `a`-places outside `ev`. In `lowColumns` and `lowBoxes`
a column is a column of a diagram; they count the columns of height below `n_{j+1}` and different
from `1`, and the boxes in them.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.divisibilityBound`: the divisibility bound at `p` of stage `j`, for a set `S` of places.
* `New.Data.le_divisibilityBound`: the lower bound for the divisibility bound by the gain at `p`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.aPlaces`: The `a`-places: the infinite places of `E` whose class in `(ℤ/q₁)ˣ` is `1`
  modulo `q₀`.
* `New.Data.IsExceptional`, `New.Data.ceilLogLifts`: A condition on `p` alone: `(p/d) = -1`,
  `p ≢ ±1` modulo `m`, and the order `o₀` of `-p` modulo `q₀` is odd and at most `𝔯`, the least
  natural number with `m ≤ p^𝔯`.
* `New.Data.placeOfInt`: The infinite place of E named by the class of the integer ν modulo q₁ if ν
  is prime to q₁, and the identity place otherwise.

modules.title: Marked primes above `p`, full marks and the scaled Hecke operator
modules.note:
Fix a prime `p` and an embedding `ι : ℂ → ℂ_[p]`. Each infinite place of `E` then induces a prime
above `p`. A finite set `Λ` of such primes is marked if it is disjoint from its conjugate and each
member is induced by an a-place; the definition also asks that `p` be exceptional and below `x₁`.
A *full mark* is a marked set that contains, for each a-place, the prime it induces or the
conjugate of that prime.
This file shows that a full mark exists and defines, with `A_𝔩` the number
`New.Data.heckeScalingExponent` of a prime `𝔩`, a scaled Hecke operator on the space
`D.SourceForm` of source forms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.IsFullMark`: a marked set that meets each pair of a prime induced by an a-place and its
  conjugate.
* `New.Data.exists_isFullMark`: a full mark exists for every exceptional `p < x₁`.
* `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator`: the operator `p ^ A_𝔩 • T_{𝔩,𝔯}` at a marked prime, on
  the space of source forms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.aPlaces`: The `a`-places: the infinite places of `E` whose class in `(ℤ/q₁)ˣ` is `1`
  modulo `q₀`.
* `New.Data.IsExceptional`, `New.Data.ceilLogLifts`: A condition on `p` alone: `(p/d) = -1`,
  `p ≢ ±1` modulo `m`, and the order `o₀` of `-p` modulo `q₀` is odd and at most `𝔯`, the least
  natural number with `m ≤ p^𝔯`.
* `New.placeOfEmb`: The prime of `E` induced by an embedding `σ : E →+* F` into an ultrametric
  normed field over `ℚ_p`: the centre on the integers of `E` of the valuation ring
  `{x : E | ‖σ x‖ ≤ 1}`.
* `New.Data.placeOfInt`: The infinite place of E named by the class of the integer ν modulo q₁ if ν
  is prime to q₁, and the identity place otherwise.
* `New.Data.lowColumns`: the number of columns at `τ` of height below `n_{j+1}` and different
  from `1`.

modules.title: p-adic gauge bounds for chains of theta lifts and restrictions to `Y_m`
modules.note:
This file proves that the value of a chain of theta lifts is a sum over classes. It deduces a
general p-adic gauge bound for the chain. It then gives gauge and norm bounds for the restriction
`New.Data.restrictToY` to `Y_m`, and describes the values of source forms. `New.weylGauge` is the
gauge of a vector at a finite point `g`: a maximum of p-adic absolute values read through the
embedding ι of `[PadicPlace p]`. `New.GaugeLe d c φ` says that `φ g` has gauge at most `c` at
`g * d` for all `g`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.chainCombination_eq_sum`: take a chain that is jointly invariant for the kernels
  `D.liftKernel ϑ`. Its value at `g D.m` is a sum over tuples of classes for the levels
  `D.levelX j`, `j < D.m`, and over the tuples x in the support of Ψ. The terms are the kernel
  products times Ψ x.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.gaugeLe_chain`: let `Ψ` be a weak chain datum for the twist `ϑ`, and
  let the places of `ϑ` have norm prime to `p`. Suppose every datum of the chain, changed by an
  operator `t j` that commutes with the levels, multiplies gauges by at most `p ^ r j` from the base
  point `d j` to `d (j + 1)`. Then the `Ψ`-combination of the chains sends a source form of gauge at
  most 1 at `d 0` to a form of gauge at most `p ^ ∑ r j` at `d D.m`.

Throughout, `D : Data P` fixes a CM field `E = D.E`, primes `p₀`, `p₁`, `N = D.N`, an integer
`π = D.piN` of `E` with `π π̄ = N`, and a length `m = D.m`. The type `D.X j` indexes a basis of a
definite hermitian space `X_j` over `E`, and `Gf D.E (D.X j)` is the group of finite adelic points
of its unitary group. Forms on `X_j` (`D.FormX j`) are algebraic automorphic forms on this group.
The level of `X_j` is `D.levelX j`, the elements of the integral subgroup `D.chosenLevel` whose last
row is `(0, …, 0, 1)` modulo `π`. Source forms are the forms on `X_0` fixed by `D.levelX 0`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.Twist`: A twist: a tame character (`New.Data.TameChar`) whose tame part is non-trivial
  at every place of its set Q.
* `New.Data.Translations`: Tuples (x_j) of finite adelic matrices with rows X_{j+1} and columns X_j,
  the translations that define the data of a chain.
* `New.IsJointlyInvariant`: the tensor ∑_x L_x ⊗ Φ_{x,m−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ Φ_{x,0} is unchanged by the joint
  action of the levels K_j, j < m.
* `New.Data.translateDatum`: The j-th datum of the tuple x: the normalised vacuum of Hom(X_j,
  X_{j+1}) translated by the finite Heisenberg operator of x_j.
* `New.Data.piNPlaces`: the set of primes dividing `π`, where `π π̄ = N`.

modules.title: Valuations of lifts at non-split primes
modules.note:
This file concerns a non-split prime `p`, for a p-adic place of ℂ. Fix a marked set `Λ` of primes
of `D.E` above `p` (`New.Data.IsMarked`), and write 𝔯 = `D.ceilLogLifts p`. For a weak chain datum
`Ψ` for a twist `ϑ` of level prime to `p`, this file moves Hecke operators at `Λ` from the source
onto the data of the lifts, where each term is a lift evaluated at a neighbor. It then bounds the
gauge of the restricted chain on the image of powers of the scaled Hecke operators.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.IsMarked.ω_ofSplitPlaces_mem_raises`: the bound for one lift evaluated at a neighbor.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.exists_sum_heckeSplit_lift_eq_smul`: at a prime of `Λ` of norm
  `q = z ^ 2`, with t = `D.t`, the operator `z ^ ((t + 1) i) * q ^ i.choose 2 • T_i` passes through
  one lift as an integral combination of the Hecke operators `T_{i'}` with i' ≤ i.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.exists_sum_heckeSplit_lift_eq_pow_smul`: so for i ≤ 𝔯 the same holds
  with the factor `p ^ (f 𝔯 t)`, where f = `D.f`.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.exists_sum_heckeSplit_chain_eq_pow_smul`: the iteration of this over
  the lifts of the chain.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.exists_lift_eq_chain_scaledHeckeOperator`: the operators
  `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator` are moved onto the data of the lifts, with a bound on the
  changed data that involves `New.Data.liftLoss`.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.gaugeLe_scaledHeckeOperator_pow`: the bound on the gauge of
  `New.Data.restrictedChain` on the image of the `m`-th power of the product of the operators
  `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.N`: The level: a chosen prime N ≡ 1 mod q₂² with log N ∈ [λ, λ + √(log b)], where
  λ = `New.Data.logLevelTarget`.
* `New.Data.liftKernel`: The theta kernel of the lift from forms on X_j (`New.Data.FormX`) to forms
  on X_{j+1}. The finite unitary groups of X_j and X_{j+1} act on its data by ω.
* `New.chain`, `New.doubleLiftChain`, `New.TensorChain.lift`: The chain of theta lifts with data
  Φ_0, Φ_1, …, the same chain taken in pairs with data in S_{2i} ⊗ S_{2i+1}, and the chain with a
  tensor of data.
* `New.Data.IsMarked`: Λ is disjoint from its conjugate, each prime of Λ is induced by an a-place,
  and p is an exceptional non-split prime below the bound x₁.

modules.title: Elementary divisor bound for the scaled Hecke operator via edges
modules.note:
Let `l` be a place of a marked set `Λ` above a prime `p`. This file carries the theorem on
elementary divisors, `New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors`, for the edge Hecke operator over
to the normalised Hecke operator `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator` at `l`. It assumes a
Frobenius cycle that matches the places above `l`. The proof identifies the two operators in
four steps:
* The edges: the cosets of the Hecke operator at `l` are indexed by edges. An edge is determined
  by its origin and its basis change there, because the rational points act freely on the cosets
  of the level (`New.Columns.HeckeEdges.eq_of_origin_eq_of_mem_parahoric`).
* The variables: at an a-place that induces `l` or its conjugate, an edge acts by letter matrices
  and powers of `p` (`New.Columns.kroneckerPi_symPowMatrix_eq_letterRep`).
* The weight space splits into monomials at these a-places and a factor on which the edges act
  integrally (`New.Columns.exists_weylIndex_equiv`, `New.Columns.exists_schur_eq_map`).
* The module: integral source forms are families of integral vectors indexed by the classes
  (`New.Columns.range_sourceFormOfValues`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Columns.isOntoUpToColength_scaledHeckeOperator_of_frobeniusCycle`: given a Frobenius cycle
  that matches the places above `l`, the operator is an edge Hecke operator, so the bound of the
  theorem holds for it.
* `New.Columns.HeckeEdges.heckeSplit_apply_rep`: The Hecke operator as a sum over edges.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsOntoUpToColength`: The endomorphism `y` keeps `M`, and for some natural number `i ≤ c` the
  sum `y (M) + p ^ j₀ • M` has index dividing `p ^ i` in `M` (in the sense of `New.ColengthDvd`):
  `y` is onto on `M` modulo `p ^ j₀` up to an index `p ^ i`.
* `New.Data.IsMarked`: a marked set `Λ` of primes of `E` is disjoint from its complex conjugate,
  each of its primes is induced by an a-place (an element of `D.aPlaces`), `p` is exceptional
  (`New.Data.IsExceptional`), and `p` is below `D.x₁` and not split in the imaginary quadratic
  field.
* `New.Data.integralSourceForms`: the module of the elements of `D.SourceForm` of gauge at most `1`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle`: ring maps `ι s : W → R` for `s` in `ℤ/N`, alternately even and odd, with
  `ι (s + 1) ≡ ι s ^ P` modulo `p`, where `P = p ^ frobExp` and the residue field of `W` has
  `P ^ N` elements.

modules.title: Elementary divisors of one scaled Hecke operator on the integral source forms
modules.note:
Let `l` be a place of a marked set `Λ` above a prime `p`, and write `o₀ = D.o₀ p`. This file
applies the theorem on elementary divisors, `New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors`, to the
normalised Hecke operator `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator` at `l`, acting on the integral
source forms `New.Data.integralSourceForms`. The a-places that induce `l` or its conjugate form one
orbit under the place named by `-p ^ o₀` (`New.Data.exists_orbit_of_mem_aPlaces`), where the place
named by an integer acts on infinite places by multiplication. This orbit gives a Frobenius cycle.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.IsMarked.exists_frobeniusCycle`: such a Frobenius cycle exists.
* `New.Data.IsMarked.isOntoUpToColength_scaledHeckeOperator`: the operator keeps the integral source
  forms and is onto modulo `p ^ j₀` up to a bounded colength.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsOntoUpToColength`: The endomorphism `y` keeps `M`, and for some natural number `i ≤ c` the
  sum `y (M) + p ^ j₀ • M` has index dividing `p ^ i` in `M` (in the sense of `New.ColengthDvd`):
  `y` is onto on `M` modulo `p ^ j₀` up to an index `p ^ i`.
* `New.Data.IsMarked`: a marked set `Λ` of primes of `E` is disjoint from its complex conjugate,
  each of its primes is induced by an a-place (an element of `D.aPlaces`), `p` is exceptional
  (`New.Data.IsExceptional`), and `p` is below `D.x₁` and not split in the imaginary quadratic
  field.
* `New.Data.integralSourceForms`: the module of the elements of `D.SourceForm` of gauge at most `1`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle`: ring maps `T.embedding i : W → R` for `i` in `ℤ/N`, alternately even and
  odd, with `T.embedding (i + 1) ≡ T.embedding i ^ P` modulo `p`, where `P = p ^ frobExp` and the
  residue field of `W` has `P ^ N` elements.
modules.literature:
An integrally scaled Hecke operator above p, acting on forms at a-places linked in a circle by
Frobenius and conjugation, has elementary divisors of small mean exponent outside a small share. So
using it once per theta lift, to keep divisibility when the partner of an a-place is an a-place,
costs little colength. Slopes of T_p of at most about k/(p+1) for GL(2) over Q and regular p, and
integral scalings of Hecke operators, are known. Related work: Arsovski, Limiting measures of
supersingularities, 2019; Liu–Truong–Xiao–Zhao, Slopes of modular forms and geometry of eigencurves,
2023; Fakhruddin–Pilloni, Hecke operators and the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties, 2021.

modules.title: The places `Σ_N` above N and the set-up at p = N
modules.note:
This file sets up the case `p = N`. It defines the set `Σ_N` of the conjugates of the places above
`N` that `ιₚ` induces, and shows that it is a split level for `N`. Levels, forms and the operator
`Up` are described at the places of `Σ_N`, in bases of the lattices `L_j` (see
`New.Data.diagPointN`). The file ends with the module `𝒜'` of forms that `Up ^ (ϱ + 1)` sends to
source forms with values integral for `L_0`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.nonInducedPlaces`, `New.Data.upIntegralForms`: the places `Σ_N` and the module `𝒜'`.
* `New.Data.upOperator_mem_sourceForm`: the operator `Up = upOperator (D.formRepAtN 0)` preserves
  the source forms `D.SourceForm`, the forms on `X_0` fixed by its level.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.piNPlaces`: the set of primes dividing `π`, where `π π̄ = N`.

modules.title: Two invariant sums of translates attached to a chain datum
modules.note:
A chain datum `Ψ` has a plain tensor `φ♭` and a glued tensor `Glue φ♭`, and the latter is jointly
invariant. Expanding the gluing writes `Glue φ♭` as a double sum of translates of the vacuum
(`IsChainDatum.gluedTensor_eq_sum_translates`), and collecting its terms gives a weak chain datum
(`IsChainDatum.exists_isWeakChainDatum_compositeLift_eq`); this serves for sums of norms and for the
primes `p ≠ N`. The projection on vacua above `N` takes `Glue φ♭` to `φ♭`, so `φ♭` is jointly
invariant too (`IsChainDatum.isWeakChainDatum`); this serves for `p = N`.

Notions from other files:
* `D : Data P`: a CM field `E` with `f` infinite places, spaces `X_0, …, X_m` over it in a chain of
  `m` theta lifts, `X_j` of rank `n_j`, and a prime level `N = π π̄` with `π = D.piN`.
* `D.piNPlaces`: the places `w ∣ π`.
* `D.X j = D.InitIndex j ⊕ Unit`: the basis indices of `X_j`; the last one is the `Unit` summand.
* A tuple of translations `t`: a finite adelic matrix `t j` for each `j`, with rows indexed by
  `X_{j+1}` and columns by `X_j`. It is admissible for `q` if each `t j`, times the conjugate of
  `D.piM`, is integral at the places prime to `q`.
* `D.translateDatum t j`: the integral vacuum of `Hom(X_j, X_{j+1})` translated by the matrix `t j`.
* `D.gluedDoubleLiftDatum v i`: the gluing, the sum over `y` modulo `N` of the translates of
  `v (2 i) ⊗ v (2 i + 1)` by the last column `-y / N` and the last row `-ȳ / N`.
* `plainTensor Ψ`, `gluedTensor Ψ`: the tensors `φ♭ = ∑ x, Ψ x • ⊗ⱼ translateDatum x j` and
  `Glue φ♭`.
* `IsAdmissibleCombination v A q d p B z`: `z = ∑ x, r x • v x` with `r` supported in `A`, each
  `d * r x` integral away from `q` and, if `p` holds, all conjugates of `r` of `ℓ¹`-norm at most
  `B`.
* `IsChainDatum ϑ Ψ`, `IsWeakChainDatum ϑ Ψ`: admissible coefficients whose glued, respectively
  plain, tensor is jointly invariant under the levels `D.levelX j`; the conditions on support and
  sum of norms are weaker for a weak chain datum.

modules.title: N-adic valuation of the lifts between the X_j at the level prime N
modules.note:
This file bounds how many powers of `N` the lifts between the `X_j` lose at the level prime `p = N`.
It first bounds the values of the lift characters at `N` and the loss of the direct datum on the
standard lattices. The lifts with data at `Σ_N` obey the rules of `IsSplitLevel.LiftLaw`. So on
ramified source forms the chain of glued double lifts is a scalar of bounded valuation times the
chain of direct lifts after `Up ^ (m / 2)`. Each direct lift loses at most `f b` powers of `N`. The
main result is that on ramified source forms `φ` with `Up ^ (m / 2) φ` integral for `L_0`, the
composite lift loses at most `2 m f b` powers of `N`.

Notions from other files:
* `Σ_N` is `D.nonInducedPlaces`, the places above `N` conjugate to the induced places;
* `diagN n S` is `diag (1, …, 1, N)` at the places in `S` and `1` at the others, and
  `δ_j = D.diagPointN j` is this matrix on `X_j` for `S` the set `D.piNPlaces` of places dividing
  `π`. It takes the standard lattice to `L_j` at `Σ_N`: if `e` is the last standard basis vector,
  the last vector of the basis of `L_j` is `N e` or `e` at each place, a unit times `π e`. The unit
  is the same for all `j`, and the direct datum and `Up` do not depend on it;
* `ιₚ` is the chosen embedding of `ℂ` into `ℂ_N`, and `D.chainChar ϑ i` is the character of lift
  `i`, from `X_{i-1}` to `X_i`;
* `schrodingerOpAt Ψ v` puts the function `Ψ` of matrices at `Σ_N` on the finite datum `v` of a
  lift;
* `directDatum` is the indicator of the integral matrices whose last column is the last basis vector
  modulo `N`, and `Up` is the operator `upOperator`;
* the data in `k.raises d d' C` give lifts that raise gauges from `d` to `d'` by a factor at most
  `C`.
modules.literature:
Denominators at the level prime N are traded for the operator `Up`. Related work: Z. Liu, Test
Schwartz functions at p for theta lifts of Hida families, arXiv 2510.21644, 2025; S. Rallis,
Langlands' functoriality and the Weil representation, 1982.

modules.title: The colength of source forms at p = N
modules.note:
This file compares three modules of source forms, `𝒜_ι`, `𝒜^L` and `𝒜^∨`, with values integral
for the standard lattice, for `L_0` and for `L_0^∨` at `Σ_N`. These are
`integralFormsAt D.SourceForm d` for `d = 1`, `diagPointN 0` and `dualPointN 0`. The comparison
shows that `𝒜' ∩ 𝒜_ι` has colength at most `m f b D_X` in `𝒜_ι`, where `D_X` is the dimension of
the space of source forms. It bounds a colength by a mean degree. The case of monomials, which is
not used later, comes first as a model.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_colengthDvd_upIntegralForms_pow`: `𝒜'` has colength at most `m f b D_X`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.nonInducedPlaces`: the set `Σ_N` of the conjugates of the places above `N` that `ιₚ`
  induces.
* `New.Data.diagPointN`: the point `δ_j`, which takes the standard lattice at `Σ_N` to `L_j`.
* `New.Data.upIntegralForms`: the module `𝒜'`, the preimage of `𝒜^L` under `Up ^ (m / 2)`.

modules.title: The divisibility of the composite lift at each prime
modules.note:
This file bounds the gauge of the composite lift `New.Data.compositeLift` at a prime p, for a fixed
embedding ι : ℂ → ℂ_p; for p ≠ N it does so through the expansion `New.Data.restrictedChain` into
chains of `m` lifts. At the exceptional primes it uses the bound of
`New.Data.IsMarked.isOntoUpToColength_scaledHeckeOperator` for the elementary divisors of the
