normalised Hecke operators `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator`.

A form *has valuation at least* `v` if its gauge at the base point `1` is at most `p ^ (-v)`. The
*a-places* (`New.Data.aPlaces`) are the infinite places ≡ 1 modulo q₀. At a non-split prime `p < x₁`
that is not *exceptional* (`New.Data.IsExceptional`), the loss pays for all collisions between
a-places. For an exceptional prime `p < x₁`, a *full mark* is a choice `Λ` of one prime from each
conjugate pair induced by the a-places; the places *inducing* `Λ` are those that induce a prime of
`Λ`, the *odd* places those that induce the conjugate of one.

With `m` the number of lifts, `f` the number of infinite places of `E` and `a` the length of a long
row, the exponents below are built from the following numbers.

* `D.heckeScalingExponent l` is `a` times the number of a-places that induce the prime `l`.
* `D.collisionExponent p`, written `j_p`, is the ceiling of `2 m f a / p`.
* `D.collisionSum p ev` is the sum of `a / p ^ e` over the collisions `(τ, e)` outside the set of
  places `ev` (`New.Data.IsCollision`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.gaugeLe_restrictedChain_one`: for p different from N and d, the chain
  of lifts keeps integrality.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.gaugeLe_restrictedChain_collisionSum`: at a non-split prime `p < x₁`
  the bounds for single lifts add up to the gain, less the loss and `m` times the collision sum.
* `New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum.gaugeLe_restrictedChain_of_isFullMark`: for a full mark Λ, the bound
  for `New.Data.restrictedChain` on the image of the m-th power of the product of the operators
  `New.Data.IsMarked.scaledHeckeOperator`.
* `New.Data.IsMarked.isOntoUpToColength_prod_scaledHeckeOperator_pow`: this power keeps the integral
  source forms and is onto modulo `p ^ j_p` up to a small colength.
* `New.Data.exists_colengthDvd_gaugeLe_compositeLift`: there is a module of source forms whose
  integral members have colength at most l in the integral source forms, with
  l ≤ allowedLoss(p) · dim (source forms), and on whose ramified members the composite lift of a
  chain datum has valuation at least gain(p) − allowedLoss(p).
* `New.Data.exists_err_gaugeLe_compositeLift`: the same bound for all primes p, on a submodule of
  the integral ramified source forms, with losses err(p) such that every finite sum ∑ err(p) log p
  is at most `New.Data.errorUnit`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.GaugeLe d c φ`: for every `g`, the p-adic gauge of the value `φ g` at `g * d` is at most `c`.
* `New.ColengthDvd M N z`: the index of `N` in `M` divides `z`, that is, each finite family in `M`
  has combinations in `N` by a matrix whose determinant divides `z`.
* `New.IsOntoUpToColength p M n y c`: the endomorphism `y` keeps `M`, and `y (M) + p ^ n • M` has
  index dividing `p ^ l` in `M` for some natural number `l ≤ c`.
* `New.Data.allowedLoss`: 2·loss(p) for a non-split prime p < x₁ (`New.Data.loss`); otherwise 2mfb
  if p = N, and 0 if not.
* `New.Data.gain`: the divisibility asked of the chain of lifts at p.
modules.literature:
For each prime p and twist of conductor prime to p, the chain of theta lifts is divisible by the
predicted power of p, less an error, on a submodule of the ramified source forms whose colength per
dimension is at most that error. The errors times log p have a small sum, which gives the
divisibility side of the bound. p-integrality of single theta lifts is known in the literature.
Related work: X. Zhang, Non-vanishing mod p of theta lifts for (O(2n+1),Mp(4n)), 2022; Berger,
Arithmetic properties of similitude theta lifts, 2009; Prasanna, Integrality of a ratio of Petersson
norms, 2006.

At an inert prime p pairing two a-places, each lift may lose divisibility. Outside a sparse set of
such p, the chain regains the predicted power of p, up to about one lift's loss, on the image of
scaled Hecke operators above p applied once per lift. Once enlarged by a p-power multiple of all
source forms, this image has small colength. Hecke operators passing through theta lifts, p-power
scaling by weight and p-adapted lifts at ordinary p are known in the literature. Related work:
Rallis, Langlands' functoriality and the Weil representation, 1982; V. Lafforgue, Estimées pour les
valuations p-adiques des valeurs propres des opérateurs de Hecke, 2011; Z. Liu, Test Schwartz
functions at p for theta lifts of Hida families, arXiv 2510.21644, 2025.

modules.title: Prime-by-prime divisibility measures; short forms span the ramified source forms
modules.group: Size of the composite lift; short source forms
modules.note:
This file defines numbers that measure, prime by prime, how divisible the chain of theta lifts on
source forms must be, and shows that short algebraic forms span. `New.AlgForm` is the space of
algebraic forms of weight (κ, e) on the definite unitary group of `New.stdSpace`, with right
translation `New.algFormRep`. The source forms `New.Data.SourceForm` form its subspace fixed by
`New.Data.levelX` 0. `New.Data.piNPlaces` is the set of the f primes dividing π, where ππ̄ = N and f
is the number of infinite places of E. Short forms span at a free level.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.localPrimeSum`: the exponent asked at p for a height y at an infinite place σ.
* `New.Data.localPrimeSumTotal`, `New.Data.gain`: the sum of these exponents over all infinite
  places, and the total exponent asked of the m lifts.
* `New.IsShort`: the values of a form are p-adically integral, and their conjugates under Aut(ℂ)
  have squared norm at most B.
* `New.span_isShort_eq_top`: at a free level K ≤ `New.stdLevel` the short forms span, for an
  explicit B.
* `New.Data.scalingGenerator`: for w ∣ π a scaling z_w at w (`New.Data.IsScalingAt`) of order N − 1
  modulo w.
* `New.Data.ramifiedSourceForms`: the source forms whose translates by the powers of each z_w have
  mean 0; `New.Data.ramifiedSourceForms_eq_range`: they are the image of ∏_{w∣π} (1 − z_w).
* `New.Data.span_isShort_ramifiedSourceForms_eq_top`: the short ramified source forms span the
  ramified source forms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: The fixed parameters: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a
  prime `d` with `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`.
* `New.weylGauge`: The gauge of ξ at g: the largest p-adic absolute value of a coordinate of
  g⁻¹·ι(ξ), with g⁻¹ acting in weight (κ, e).
* `New.weylNormSq`: The squared norm ξ* G ξ for the integer Gram matrix G = `New.weylGram`.
* `New.Data.chosenLevel`: The principal congruence subgroup of level `New.Data.piM`, whose prime
  divisors are the chosen places.

## Role in the proof

The exponents are used in `New.UpperBound.Divisibility.LocalDivisibility`, the short forms in
`New.Reduction.ShortAndEnough` and `New.Determinant.AuxiliaryForms.SpanningForms`.

modules.title: Explicit bound for the number of classes in the genus
modules.group: Size of the composite lift; short source forms
modules.note:
This file gives a crude explicit bound `New.Space.card_stdClasses_le` for the number of classes
`New.StdClasses (New.stdLevel E n)` in the genus of the standard lattice. A class is determined
by the Gram matrix `G` of a short basis of its lattice and a rational approximation `X` of the
change of basis. Both `G` and `G X` have integral entries of bounded size, and such matrices are
counted.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Space.card_stdClasses_le`: an explicit bound for the number of classes
  `New.StdClasses (New.stdLevel E n)`, for a CM field `E` with `f` infinite places and a natural
  number `N ≠ 0` in the different of `E`.
* `New.Space.stdClasses_eq_of_gram_eq`: two classes `g`, `g'` in `Γ \ G_f / K₀` are equal if
  there are `Y`, `Y'` in `GL n E` with the same Gram matrix such that `A' A⁻¹` has entries in
  `Ô E`, where `A = g.out⁻¹ Y` and `A' = g'.out⁻¹ Y'`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.StdClasses K`: the double cosets `Γ \ G_f / K` of the finite adelic unitary group `G_f` of
  the form `∑ x_i \bar x_i` by its rational points `Γ` and a subgroup `K`.
* `New.stdLevel`: the subgroup `K₀ = G_f ∩ GL_n(Ô)`, the stabiliser of the standard lattice `Ô^n`.

modules.title: Numerical inequalities between the parameters of the data
modules.group: Size of the composite lift; short source forms
modules.note:
This file proves explicit identities and inequalities between the parameters of the data `D`,
which are used to bound heights and indices. It groups the von Mangoldt sum prime by prime,
bounds the rows of the diagrams and the size of jets, computes the norm of `D.piMBar`, bounds the
number of classes at levels that contain a principal level, and bounds the sum of the allowed
losses. Here `s_p(y, σ)` is `New.Data.localPrimeSum p y σ`, and `κ(τ)` is the weight `D.weight τ`
of an infinite place `τ` (not the column count `D.columnCount τ h`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.localPrimeSum_eq_tsum`, `New.Data.primeSum_eq_sum_localPrimeSum`: the local sum at `p`
  as a sum over the powers of `p`, and the von Mangoldt sum `New.Data.primeSum` grouped prime by
  prime.
* `New.Data.card_stdClasses_le_exp_mul_log`, `New.Data.card_stdClasses_le_exp`: bounds for the
  number of classes of the definite unitary group at a level `K` that contains a given principal
  level.
* `New.Data.sum_allowedLoss_mul_log_le`: the losses `New.Data.allowedLoss p`, weighted by `log p`,
  add up to at most `New.Data.errorUnit`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.StdClasses K`: the double cosets `Γ \ G_f / K` of the finite adelic unitary group `G_f` of
  the form `∑ x_i \bar x_i` by its rational points `Γ` and a subgroup `K`.
* `New.Data`: the parameters `x`, `x₁`, `a`, `b`, `m`, `N`, … of the construction; `D.E` is its CM
  field, which contains `P.K = ℚ(√-d)` and has `D.f` infinite places.
* `New.Data.loss`: `f a (log b)² / p`, times `m` if `p ≡ ±1` mod `m`.
modules.literature:
See `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.FiniteVolume` for sources. See
`New.UpperBound.Divisibility.LocalDivisibility` for related work.

modules.title: Archimedean size of the composite lift, and passage to target forms by the good projection
modules.group: Size of the composite lift; short source forms
modules.note:
The composite lift of a chain datum is `New.Data.restrictedChain` of the expansion of its glued
tensor, so its size (`New.Data.weylNormSq_compositeLift_le`) follows from the bound for
`New.Data.restrictedChain`. This map sends source forms (algebraic forms on `X_0`) to forms on
`Y_m`. Separately, a form `z` of principal level on `Y₀` (the side of the target forms) is replaced
by its good part `|𝖦| e₀ s z`. For the lift to `Y_m` (`lowerChainAtLevel`), this replacement keeps
integrality of any scalar multiple `c •` of it, and it enlarges the bound `exp B` on its values to a
bound `exp (x ^ 99 + B)` on the class sum.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.rowSizeSum`, `New.Data.chainSize`: the size of the rows of one lift diagram, and the
  main term of the size of the chain.
* `New.Data.weylNormSq_restrictedChain_le`, `New.Data.weylNormSq_compositeLift_le`: the size bounds
  for the restricted chain and for the composite lift.
* `New.Data.lowerChain_goodProjTranslate_apply`: the lift of `|𝖦| e₀ s z` is a combination of right
  translates of the lift of `z`, with the coefficients of `|𝖦| e₀`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.jetSize`: The size `s_∞(j) = log j! + j log (M / Ω)` of a derivative of order `j`.
* `New.Data.restrictedChain`: For coefficients `Ψ` on translations of the integral vacuum, the
  combination of the chains of `m` lifts of these translates, restricted to `Y_m`. `Ψ` is a weak
  chain datum (`New.Data.IsWeakChainDatum`) if the combined tensor is invariant and the coefficients
  are admissible.
* `New.Data.gain`: The divisibility at a prime `p` that is asked of the chain.
* `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.integralForms`: The forms φ whose value φ(g) has gauge `New.weylGauge`
  at most 1 for every g.
* `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.normSqAt`: The class sum of the squared Gram norms `New.weylNormSq` of
  the vectors σ(φ(g)).
modules.literature:
The untwisted chain of lifts enlarges squared norms of all conjugates by at most an explicit factor,
which gives the size side of the product formula. Related work on algebraic modular forms as values
on lattice classes: Gross, Algebraic modular forms, 1999; Greenberg–Voight, Lattice methods for
algebraic modular forms on classical groups, 2014.

modules.title: Frobenius cycles, the twisted action of GL_k(W), depth and defect
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
This file contains the definitions for the theorem on elementary divisors
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors`). Let `W` be a local ring with finite residue field.
Variables are pairs `(b, s)` of an index `b : Fin k` and a letter `s : ZMod N`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.FrobeniusCycle`: a prime number `p` with a square root `sqrtPrime` in `R`, a power `P` of
  `p`, and ring maps `embedding s : W → R`, each marked even or odd, and each the `P`-th power of
  the one before modulo `p`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.letterMatrix`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.polyAction`,
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.letterRep`: `g` acts on the letter `s` through the image under `embedding s`
  of `g` (even) or of its inverse transpose (odd), both on polynomials and on coefficient vectors of
  forms of degree `n` in each letter. `New.FrobeniusCycle.polyAction_polyOfCoeffs` says that the two
  actions agree.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.depth`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectWeight`: the depth of a monomial, and the
  weight of a variable in the defect of a monomial at a letter.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.translatesIn`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectConditions`: vectors whose
  translates have given coefficients in an ideal.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.deepForms`: vectors all of whose translates have only monomials of large
  depth.

Notions from other files:
* `New.linSubst z`: for a matrix `z` over `R`, the `R`-algebra map of polynomial rings that sends
  `X b` to `∑ t, z t b • X t`.
* `New.Monomials σ n`: the exponent vectors of degree `n` on the variables `σ`.
* `New.exponentOf β`, `New.polyOfCoeffs F`: the exponent vector on the variables `(b, s)` that is
  `β s` in the letter `s`, and the polynomial `∑ β, F β • x ^ β`.
* `New.symPowMatrix n`, `New.kroneckerPi`: the `n`-th symmetric power of a matrix, and the Kronecker
  product of a family of matrices.
* `New.levi W τ`, `New.parahoric W τ`: for a labelling `τ : Fin k → ℕ` of the indices, the matrices
  in `GL_k(W)` whose entry `(i, j)` is zero whenever `τ i ≠ τ j`, and those whose entry `(i, j)`
  lies in the maximal ideal of `W` whenever `τ i < τ j`.

## Notation

Matrices act on vectors of coefficients, so they are the transposes of the matrices substituted in
the variables: for both parities, the translate of a polynomial `h` in the letter `s` by `g` is
`h ∘ g_sᵀ`, where `g_s = T.letterMatrix s g`.

modules.title: Gauss filtrations, Stepanov's count and the root lemma
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
The group GL_k(W) acts on polynomials over R in variables x_{b,s} (b < k, s ∈ ℤ/N) through a
`New.FrobeniusCycle`: a power P of a prime p, ring maps ι_s : W → R with ι_{s+1} ≡ ι_s^P mod p,
and w in R with w² = p. The indices s ∈ ℤ/N are called letters and are alternately even and odd.
This file shows which monomials can carry the least w-adic order plus weight among all translates
of a polynomial.

* `New.stepanov_count`: Stepanov's count of zeros at the residue classes of a local ring.
* `New.IsRealFiltration`, `New.adicFiltration`, `New.gaussFiltration`: multiplicative filtrations
  indexed by ℝ, the w-adic one, and the Gauss filtration on polynomials with weighted variables.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.RootAt`: a root and a letter, with the variables X_s, Y_s, the substitution
  that defines the auxiliary polynomial, and its expansions at the rational points.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defect_nonpos_of_extreme_term`: for weights that rise by an amount in [1/2, 1]
  from X_s to Y_s, a term of least order plus weight among all translates by SL₂(W) has defect at
  most 0 (see `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectWeight`).

The proof compares the degree of an auxiliary binary form with its zeros at the q + 1 rational
points of the projective line, in the affine coordinate t. For an extreme term it writes the defect
in the two variables X_s, Y_s of each letter, substitutes polynomials in t for them, and expands one
coefficient at infinity (which gives its degree) and at the q finite points.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.polyAction`: the action of GL_k(W) on polynomials in the variables x_{b,s}; g
  sends x_{b,s} to ∑_c (g_s)_{cb} x_{c,s}, where g_s is ι_s(g) for even letters s and ι_s of the
  inverse transpose of g for odd s.
* `New.levi`: the Levi subgroup of a labelling τ of the indices, the matrices in GL_k(W) whose (i,j)
  entry vanishes whenever τ(i) ≠ τ(j).
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.rootVar`: for indices a, a' and a letter s, the variable (a',s) if s is even
  and (a,s) if s is odd.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectWeight`: at a letter i along a root (a, a'), the weight of x_{b,s} is a
  signed multiple of P^((s - i) mod N) / (q - 1) at the variables X_s, Y_s and 0 elsewhere, plus 1
  at Y_i; the sum of these weights over a monomial is its defect.

## Notation

After the substitution the variable Y_s, s ≠ i, is kept by `mainSubst` as the variable
`X (D.varY s)` of the letter s. The functions `RootAt.sign` and `RootAt.moveSign` carry the signs.
modules.literature:
The group SL₂(W), placed in two rows and columns of GL_k(W), acts on polynomials in a circle of
variable sets, alternately by Frobenius twists and by inverse transposes, and a term that is least
for valuation plus a suitable weight among all translates has exponents obeying linear inequalities.
Other files use them to bound the elementary divisors of the Hecke operator. Twisted Dickson forms
on Frobenius twists of symmetric powers, weight inequalities via the Lang map, and the count of
zeros against degree are known in the literature. Related work: Ghate–Jana, Modular representations
of GL2(F_q) using calculus, 2025; Imai–Koskivirta, Automorphic vector bundles on the stack of
G-zips, 2021; Bombieri, Counting points on curves over finite fields, Sém. Bourbaki 430, 1973.

modules.title: An average on polynomials in the entries of a matrix
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Let `L` be a Levi subgroup of `GL_k`, `W` a local ring with large finite residue field, and
`ι : W → O` a ring map to a valuation domain of characteristic `0` in which the prime `p` is not a
unit. Let `ρ ∈ ℤ ^ k` weigh the indices, and call a monomial in the matrix entries *bad* if its row
weight exceeds a threshold. The file constructs an `O`-linear form `I` on polynomials in the matrix
entries (`New.Average.exists_isAverage`) that is invariant under conjugation by `L(W)`, vanishes
on bad monomials, and agrees modulo an ideal `J` with a power of `p` times evaluation at the matrix
`1` on every polynomial of small degree whose conjugates have no bad monomial modulo `J`
(`New.Average.IsAverage`, `New.Average.evalAtOne`).

* `New.Average.exists_isAdjointWeight`: the multinomial coefficients of the monomials of
  degree `< p ^ f` in `m` variables divide `p ^ (m f)` in `O`, and the quotients make the
  substitutions by a matrix and by its transpose adjoint.
* `New.Average.eq_top_of_schurMap_eq_leviMonomialValues`: the points of `L(W)` span the Schur
  algebra of `L` of degree `d`, which acts on `U = (O ^ k)^{⊗ d}`.
* `New.Average.dualOperator`: with the quotients above, a polynomial `ψ` gives an element `ψ♯`
  of the Schur algebra. For `d < p ^ f` its trace on `U` is the scaled value at `1` of the part of
  degree `d` of `ψ`, and conjugation of `ψ` becomes conjugation of `ψ♯`.
* `New.Average.averagePart`: in degree `d ≤ D` the form `I` is the trace of `ψ♯` on `U` minus its
  trace on the submodule `U₊` (`New.Average.largeWeightSubmodule`) generated by the basis tensors of
  large weight.

All `k ^ 2` entries are variables; a monomial with an entry outside the blocks has `ψ♯ = 0`.
The row weight of a monomial `α` is `∑ α (i, j) • ρ i`; the column weight has `ρ j` in place of
`ρ i`. The Schur algebra is built on the transpose of the matrix of variables, so the row indices
of a monomial are the column indices of `ψ♯`, and no transpose appears in the rule for conjugation.
Transposing the variables gives the same statements with column weights, since `L(W)` is closed
under transposition.

Notions from other files:
* `New.linSubst z`: for an `m × σ` matrix `z` over `R`, the `R`-algebra map from polynomials in
  variables indexed by `σ` to those indexed by `m` that sends `X b` to `∑ t, z t b • X t`.
* `New.levi W τ`: the Levi subgroup of a labelling `τ` of the indices, made of the matrices in
  `GL_k(W)` whose entry `(i, j)` vanishes whenever `τ i ≠ τ j`.
* `New.kroneckerPi A`: the Kronecker product of a family of matrices `A s`; its entry at `(β, α)`
  is `∏ s, A s (β s) (α s)`.
* `New.fockPairing`: the bilinear form on polynomials for which monomials are orthogonal and
  `⟨x ^ α, x ^ α⟩ = α!`.

The average serves the map `Av` of `New.UpperBound.ElementaryDivisors.AveragingMap`.
modules.literature:
Known result: the Schur algebra, and that group elements span it in degrees below the size of the
field. Here this is proved for Levi subgroups over local rings, in degrees `d` with `d + k` at most
the size of the residue field. Source: Green, Polynomial representations of GL_n, 1980; Benson–Doty,
Schur–Weyl duality over finite fields, 2009.

modules.title: Edges, halfway lattices and duality
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
An edge is a pair of lattices `L' ⊆ L` with `p L ⊆ L'` and `L / L'` of dimension `r` over the
residue field; `L'` is its origin. Let `w ^ 2 = p`, and consider forms of degree `n` in each of `N`
letters, with `k` variables in each letter. In a basis of `L'` adapted to the edge, the forms that
are integral for the lattice `L' + w L`, times `w ^ (-n N / 2)`, have as basis the normalized
monomials `w ^ (-depth β) z ^ β`, where the depth is the degree in the deep variables
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.deepIndicator`). This module of forms is the halfway lattice of the edge. The
file works with coefficient vectors in the normalized monomials, so the halfway lattice is the
module of all vectors.

* `New.monomialLattice`, `New.dividedPowerLattice`: the spans `H ⊇ H°` of the monomials `z ^ β` and
  of the `(n! ^ N / β!) z ^ β`; both are stable under `GL_k(W)`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.allEdgesForms`: the forms that lie in the halfway lattices of all edges from
  `L'`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing`: weights of a pairing for which `ρ(g)` and `ρ(gᵀ)` are adjoint;
  it pairs the halfway lattices of an edge and its dual.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.edgeRestriction`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.originFunctions`: functions on origins
  as functions on edges, and the functions on edges that depend only on the origin.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_originFunctions_factorization_det_dvd`,
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.mulVec_mulVec_eq_self_of_mem_originFunctions`: if every edge occurs, these
  functions form a direct summand, in which the integral functions on origins have small colength.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.pow_dvd_letterRep_mulVec_of_mem_allEdgesForms`,
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing.pow_dvd_pairing_letterRep`: vectors in `allEdgesForms` have
  coefficients divisible by a power of `w` at monomials of large defect, and pair with these
  monomials to multiples of a power of `w`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle`: a prime `p`, ring maps from `W` to `O` indexed by the letters `s ∈ ℤ/N`,
  which are alternately even and odd, and an element `w` of `O` with `w ^ 2 = p`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.letterRep`: the matrix `ρ(g)` of `g ∈ GL_k(W)` on coefficient vectors. It
  substitutes the image of `g` in even letters and of its inverse transpose in odd letters;
  `ρ(g) h` is the translate of `h` by `g`.
* `New.twoBlock`: the blocks of sizes `r` and `k - r`; `New.parahoric`, `New.levi`: the stabilizer
  of the edge and the block diagonal subgroup.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.translatesIn`: vectors whose translates by a Levi subgroup have coefficients
  in an ideal at a set of monomials. Two cases are `New.FrobeniusCycle.deepForms` (no translate has
  a monomial of depth below a bound) and `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectConditions`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectWeight`: real weights on the two variables of a root in each letter; the
  defect of a monomial is its weighted degree, and `defectConditions` is the condition on block
  diagonal translates at the monomials of large defect.

modules.title: Few forms have only deep translates
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Let `T` be a Frobenius cycle over a field `K` of characteristic `p`. The space
`New.FrobeniusCycle.deepForms` consists of the forms all of whose translates have only monomials of
depth at least `δ`. Such a form vanishes to order `δ` at many points, which are cut out by equations
with small leading powers, so it has a monomial of large weighted degree. The sum of the weighted
degrees of all monomials therefore bounds the sum of the dimensions of these spaces. With
`New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_originFunctions_factorization_det_dvd`, the bound leads to the theorem on
elementary divisors, `New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle N W K`: a prime `p` with a power `P`, ring maps `embedding s : W → K` for the
  letters `s` in `ZMod N`, which are alternately even and odd, and a residue field of `W` with
  `q = P ^ N` elements.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.deepIndicator`: the indicator of the variables `(b, s)` that are deep for `r`,
  that is, `s` is even and `r ≤ b`, or `s` is odd and `b < r`.
* `New.Exponents N k n`, `New.polyOfCoeffs`: the exponents of the monomials in the variables
  `(b, s)` of degree `n` in each letter, and the polynomial with given coefficients at them.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.polyAction`: the action of `GL_k(W)` on polynomials in the variables `(b, s)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.FrobeniusCycle.entryRow`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.entryCol`: for `k = 2 r + m`, the row `< r` and
  the column `≥ r` of the position in a `k × k` matrix named by `t` in `Fin r × Fin (m + 1)`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.entryFormValue`: the point attached to residues `y t` at the positions. Its
  coordinates are linear forms in lifts of the `y t`, with coefficients
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.entryCoeff`, each zero or a variable up to sign.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_le_weight_of_mem_deepForms`: a non-zero form in
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.deepForms` has a monomial of large weight.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.sum_finrank_deepForms_le`: the dimensions of the spaces of forms all of whose
  translates have depth at least `1, 2, …, M` add up to at most `New.FrobeniusCycle.divisorConstant`
  times the number of exponents.

modules.title: The substitution by Frobenius powers of generic matrices; weight and defect
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Fix a Frobenius cycle `T` (`New.FrobeniusCycle`; letters `s : ZMod N`, even or odd, `P` a power of
the prime `p`, `q = P ^ N`, `w ^ 2 = p`). The twists `T.embedding s g` are not algebraic in `g`, but
modulo `p` they are entrywise powers of one another. So we take one generic `k × k` matrix for each
letter (a copy) and let the copy `s - d`, `0 ≤ d ≤ ℓ`, act on the letter `s` through its entrywise
power `P ^ d`, or through the cofactor matrix of this power if `s` is odd; the last factor, `d = ℓ`,
acts on the deep variables only. The matrix of this substitution on forms is
`New.FrobeniusCycle.substitutionOperator` at the factors `New.FrobeniusCycle.frobGenericMatrix`.
Matrices act on vectors of coefficients, so they are the transposes of the matrices that are
substituted in the variables: the row index of an entry here is its column index there.

* `New.FrobeniusCycle.substitutionOperator_map_eq_conj`: conjugation of the factors by a block
  diagonal matrix.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.copyWeight`: the weight of a monomial in the entries of all copies.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.abs_defect_sub_copyWeight_le`: let `a' = a + 1`, `ℓ ≤ N` and
  `N n k (ℓ + 2) ≤ P ^ ℓ`, and take an entry in row `β` of the operator with `r = a'` at the factors
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.conjFrobGenericMatrix h` (the generic factors after a change of frame by `h`).
  If the coefficient of a monomial in it is not divisible by `w ^ c`, the weight of the monomial at
  the copy `i` is within `c* = 3 k c` of the defect of `β` at the letter `i + ℓ`.

A term of an entry of a product of matrices belongs to a path of indices. The weight of a step is a
difference of two scaled index weights (`New.FrobeniusCycle.scaledIndexWeight`) up to `1 / P ^ ℓ`,
so the weights telescope along a path and leave the scaled index weight of its last index, up to
`(ℓ + 2) / P ^ ℓ`. For an even letter this scaled index weight is `1 - 1 / q` times the defect
weight. For an odd letter the cofactor matrix changes its sign, which again gives this multiple of
the defect weight, and multiplies the loss by at most `k`. What remains, the defect divided by `q`,
has size at most `1`, as `2 n ≤ q`. `New.FrobeniusCycle.substitutionOperator_mem` carries this out
for all terms at once. An element has level `t` in a filtration `G` (`New.IsRealFiltration`) if it
lies in `G t`, and the levels of the entries are bounded from the levels of the factors. The main
filtrations used are `New.gaussFiltration (New.adicFiltration w) ω`: divisibility of coefficients by
powers of `w`, shifted by weights `ω` of the variables. They also absorb the error terms, which are
multiples of `p` (`New.FrobeniusCycle.conjFrobGenericMatrix_mem_gaussFiltration`). With `0` in place
of `w` the level bounds the weights of the monomials that occur.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.deepIndicator`: the indicator of the deep variables `(b, s)`: it is `1` if `s`
  is even and `r ≤ b`, or `s` is odd and `b < r`, and `0` otherwise.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectWeight i a a'`: the weight of `(b, s)` is
  `± P ^ ((s - i) mod N) / (q - 1)` for `b = a, a'` (with the sign `+` at `a'` for even and at `a`
  for odd `s`, and `1` added to the positive weight at `s = i`), and `0` for other `b`. The defect
  of a monomial at the letter `i` is the sum of these weights over its variables.
* `New.exponentOf`: a family `β` of exponent vectors, one for each letter, as one exponent vector on
  the variables `(b, s)`.
* `New.levi W (New.twoBlock k r)`: the block diagonal matrices in `GL_k(W)` with blocks of sizes `r`
  and `k - r`.

## Notation

Here `h` is a matrix in `GL_k(W)`, not a form.

modules.title: Averaging: removing the terms of large defect in all Levi translates at once
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Fix a Frobenius cycle `T` over `W` and `O` (`New.FrobeniusCycle`; `N = 2 ℓ` letters, `P` a power of
the prime `p`, `w ^ 2 = p`) and an edge, with the Levi subgroup `G` of blocks of sizes `r` and
`k - r`. Forms are written in the normalized monomials of the edge with weights `b_β`, and
`⟨h, h'⟩ = ∑_β h'_β b_β h_β` is the pairing with the forms of the dual edge
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing`). Fix `c : ℕ` and put `c* = 3 k c` (`New.defectThreshold`) and
`c₀ = T.multinomialExponent k`. Let `O` be a valuation domain of characteristic `0` in which `p` is
not a unit, and let `P ^ ℓ` be large. The main result
`New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_average_mem_defectConditions_and_dvd_sub` gives a matrix `Av` such that
no `G(W)`-translate of `Av h` has a term of defect above `3 c*` modulo `w ^ c`, while
`⟨Av h, h'⟩ ≡ p ^ (N c₀) ⟨h, h'⟩` modulo `w ^ c` for all `h'` in the halfway lattices of all edges
from the origin of the dual edge (`New.FrobeniusCycle.allEdgesForms`).

Substitute generic matrices, one copy for each letter, in `h`
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.substitutionOperator`). For a set `J` of copies, `Av_J h`
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.partialAverage`) is obtained by applying the average (`New.Average.IsAverage`)
in the copies `j ∈ J` and `p ^ c₀` times the evaluation at `1` in the others. Then
`Av_∅ h = p ^ (N c₀) h`, and `Av` is `Av_J` for the set of all copies. A monomial in one copy is bad
if its row weight for `New.rootVector a r`, `r = a + 1`, is above `2 c* P ^ ℓ`. The substitution in
the frame `g ∈ G(W)` is the one formed from the factors
`New.FrobeniusCycle.conjFrobGenericMatrix g`.

* `New.FrobeniusCycle.contractOtherCopies`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.conjSubst_contractOtherCopies_one`:
  the linear forms are applied in all copies but one, in a frame `g`; the change of frame conjugates
  the remaining copy.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.abs_weight_div_sub_defect_le`: let the forms be invariant under `G(W)`. If the
  coefficient of `α` in the entry `β` of `contractOtherCopies` is not divisible by `w ^ c`, then the
  row weight of `α` over `P ^ ℓ` is within `c*` of the defect of `β` at the letter `j + ℓ`, for the
  remaining copy `j`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.lt_weight_and_lt_defect_of_not_dvd_coeff_contractOtherCopies`: hence a defect
  of `β` above `3 c*` makes `α` bad, and a bad `α` makes the defect exceed `c*`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.pow_dvd_pairing_partialAverage_insert_sub`: one more copy in `J` does not
  change the pairing modulo `w ^ c`. The main result adds these differences along a chain of
  subsets.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.letterRep`: the matrix of `g ∈ GL_k(W)` on the forms, which have degree `n` in
  each letter and are twisted at the letter `s` by `T.embedding s`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.substitutionOperator`: the Kronecker product over the letters `s` of the
  matrices on forms of degree `n` that are built from given factors `ψ s d`; with
  `New.FrobeniusCycle.frobGenericMatrix` the factor is the entrywise power `P ^ d` of the copy
  `s - d` of the generic matrix, and odd letters take the cofactor matrix of the product.
* `New.Average.IsAverage`: a linear form that is invariant under conjugation by the Levi subgroup
  and vanishes on bad monomials. If a polynomial of bounded degree has all bad coefficients of its
  Levi conjugates in an ideal, the form agrees on it with a multiple of the evaluation at `1` modulo
  this ideal.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectConditions`: the vectors whose `G(W)`-translates have their coefficients
  of defect above a bound in a given ideal.
modules.literature:
Linear forms on polynomials in a generic matrix that are invariant under the Levi subgroup split
evaluation at the identity by weight, up to a power of `p`. This gives a map into the forms without
terms of large defect that keeps the pairing up to `p ^ (N c₀)` modulo `w ^ c`. The Schur algebra as
dual of polynomials in a generic matrix, its spanning by finite points in low degree, and truncation
by weights are known in the literature. Related work: Benson–Doty, Schur–Weyl duality over finite
fields, 2009; Green, Polynomial representations of GL_n, 1980; Donkin, On Schur algebras and related
algebras I, 1986.

modules.title: The Pieri cone, the step map and the slab: interlacing and volume of the cone
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Vectors `ν` are real functions on pairs `(b, j)`, with `b` in `Fin k` and `j` a letter (in `ZMod N`
for the final volume formula). The step map `New.permStep` sends `ν` to signed gaps between
consecutive letters, twisted by permutations. The cone `New.pieriCone v P` is cut out by Pieri's
inequalities, one half of the interlacing inequalities between `ν` and `P` times its shift. The slab
`New.degreeSlab k D` is the set of nonnegative vectors whose sum at each letter `j` lies in the unit
interval `[D j - 1, D j]`, a product of slices of orthants.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.detOneSubPerm`: the determinant `det (1 - τ / q)` for a permutation `τ` of coordinates.
* `New.det_interlacing_indicator`: interlacing of two decreasing sequences is the determinant of a
  matrix of indicators.
* `New.volume_real_inter_degreeSlab_eq_signed_sum`, `New.prod_mul_volume_real_inter_degreeSlab`: for
  `P > 1`, a set whose preimage under `New.permStep` (with trivial permutations) is the cone fills a
  fraction of the slab given by a signed sum over permutations, equal to
  `∏ l < k, (q - 1) / (q ^ (l + 1) - 1)` with `q = P ^ N`.

The result serves the dimension bounds mod `p` from flags in
`New.UpperBound.ElementaryDivisors.DefectCount`.

## Notation

The Boolean `v j` selects the sign of the steps at the letter `j`: `+` for true, `-` for false. In
the application `v j` is true for even `j`.

modules.title: The dimension of the forms of bounded defect
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
Let `T` be a Frobenius cycle (`New.FrobeniusCycle`) over a field `K` of characteristic `p`, with
`P = T.P` and `q = T.q = P ^ N`. Exponents are indexed by `(b, s) ∈ Fin k × ZMod N`, and `s` is
called the letter. The defect of an exponent `β` at the letter `i` along the root `(a, a')` is the
linear form `∑ x, T.defectWeight i a a' x * β x`. Pieri's inequalities say that the defects along
the simple roots `(b, b + 1)` are at most `0`.

The forms whose translates by a Levi subgroup with two blocks have bounded defect along the root
between the blocks are counted by flags and lattice points. One substitutes `x ^ m` for the
variables, `m` a power of `q`, and multiplies by one monomial for each class of exponents modulo
`m`. Give the variable `(b, s)` the height `b` for even `s` and `-b` for odd `s`. Among the terms of
all translates of the resulting polynomial by the Levi subgroup, one of least height has defect at
most `0` along the other simple roots, and it occurs in the translate by a representative of a flag,
that is, of a coset of the lower Iwahori subgroup. A shift by an integral vector moves its exponent,
divided by `m`, into the cone of Pieri's inequalities. As `m` grows, the count of these exponents
becomes the volume of the cone cut by a slab, and the share of the cone in a slab is the inverse of
the number of all flags.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectCone`: the real vectors of bounded defect along the simple roots.
* `New.powerPacking`: a family of forms in the `m`-th powers of the variables, packed into one
  polynomial.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_finrank_defectConditions_le_volume`: the dimension of the forms of
  bounded defect is at most a number of flags times the volume of the part of a slab in which
  Pieri's inequalities hold.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.index_mul_finrank_defectConditions_le`: in large degree, the parahoric index
  times the dimension of the forms of bounded defect is at most `1 + θ` times the number of
  exponents.

Notions from other files:
* `New.parahoric`: The parahoric subgroup of a labelling τ: matrices in GL_k(W), W local, whose
  (i,j) entry lies in the maximal ideal whenever τ(i) < τ(j).
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.defectConditions`: The forms F such that, for every g block diagonal with
  blocks of sizes a', k − a' and every β of defect above h along (a, a') at some letter, the
  coefficient of g·F at β lies in a given ideal I. In this file I = ⊥.
* `levi W (twoBlock k r)`: The block diagonal matrices with blocks r and k − r.
* `degreeSlab k D`: The real vectors β ≥ 0 whose degree ∑_b β(b,s) in each letter s lies in [D
  s − 1, D s].

## Notation

In the count, `m = q ^ j` is a power of `q`. As matrices act transposed, the lower Iwahori subgroup
is used.
modules.literature:
Volumes of interlacing regions, Frobenius amplification and counting by leading terms along flags
are known in the literature. Related work: Forrester–Zhang, Corank-1 projections and the randomised
Horn problem, 2021 (after Dixon, 1905; Anderson, 1991); Bombieri, Counting points on curves over
finite fields, Sém. Bourbaki 430, 1973; Okounkov, Brunn–Minkowski inequality for multiplicities,
1996.

modules.title: Elementary divisors of the edge Hecke operator
modules.group: Elementary divisors of a Hecke operator
modules.note:
The main result `New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors` bounds the mean exponent of the elementary
divisors of an edge Hecke operator `A`, outside a small proportion of them, under the size
conditions `New.FrobeniusCycle.IsLargeDegree`. Colengths in the sense of `New.ColengthDvd` take
the place of lengths, because the ring of coefficients need not be discrete;
`New.FrobeniusCycle.elementary_divisors_length` is the statement in lengths.

Let `w ^ 2 = p`, let `N` be the number of letters of the Frobenius cycle `T` and
`c₀ = T.multinomialExponent k`. Write `M` for the integral functions on lattices, `M_all` for the
functions on edges that depend only on the origin (`New.FrobeniusCycle.originFunctions`) and
`M_edge` for all functions on edges. The operator `A` acts on `M°`, the functions whose value at `L`
is dual to the integral forms on the dual lattice `L*`. Let `𝒩 ⊆ M°` consist of the functions whose
value at `L` is dual to the forms in the halfway lattices of all edges from `L*`. The map
`Add : M_edge → 𝒩` (`New.pairingMap`) adds the values at the edges into `L`. It is written in
coordinates dual to these forms, with one basis for all lattices `L` at once. Then, on vectors
multiplied by the pairing `b`, `A` is the composite `M ⊆ M_all ⊆ M_edge → 𝒩 ⊆ M°`
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing.edgeHeckeOperator_regroup`), and the image of `Add` contains
`p ^ (N c₀) 𝒩` (`New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing.pairingMap_mul_nearInverse_one`). At each edge
there are conditions modulo `w ^ c`, with the precision `c = T.congruencePrecision k`
(`New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_isEdgeCondition`).

1. The functions that satisfy the conditions have nearly the full image: `Add` has a near inverse
   `Inv` (`New.nearInverse`, `New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgeCondition.pow_dvd_mul_sub_smul_one`) whose
   values satisfy them.
2. The conditions hold on `M_all` and leave room for few further generators. By Nakayama's lemma the
   span of `Add M_all` and these generators contains `p ^ (2 N c₀) 𝒩`
   (`New.exists_finset_card_le_smul_top_le_sup_span`).
3. Both ends have small colength (`New.FrobeniusCycle.IsLargeDegree.exists_basis_det_dvd`, used
   twice), and the colengths add along the chain (`New.colengthDvd_mul_mul_of_smul_top_le`).

The three steps are put together in
`New.FrobeniusCycle.exists_colengthDvd_range_pairingMap_mul_edgeRestriction`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusCycle N W O`: a prime `p` with a square root `w` in `O`, a power `P` of `p` such
  that the residue field of `W` has `q = P ^ N` elements, and `N` maps `W → O` (the letters), each
  the `P`-th power of the one before modulo `p`.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.allEdgesForms`: the forms that lie in the halfway lattices of all edges from a
  lattice; `New.FrobeniusCycle.IsEdgePairing`: the pairing of an edge with its dual.
* `New.FrobeniusCycle.divisorConstant`: the bound `c_div` for the mean depth of the forms that are
  deep for all edges.

modules.title: Functions of positive type and singular minors
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
A function `Θ` on a finite group `G` is of positive type if `Θ (a⁻¹ * b) = ⟪u a, u b⟫` for some
vectors `u a` of a complex inner product space.

Notions from other files:

* `New.invTransposeGL` is the automorphism `g ↦ (gᵀ)⁻¹` of `GL n R`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.card_mul_sum_det_eq_zero_le`: let `k` be a field with `q` elements, `π` a representation by
  `n × n` matrices over `k`, `A₀` and `A₁` two `n × m` matrices and `Θ ≥ 0` of positive type.
  Suppose that, for `v ≠ 0`, the stabilisers of `A₀ v` under `π` and of `A₁ v` under the
  contragredient of `π` have `Θ`-mass at most `Y ≥ 0`. Then the set where `det (A₁ᵀ π(s) A₀)`
  vanishes has mass at most `(2 Θ(G) + q ^ (|m| + |n| / 2) Y) / q`. The proof counts the kernel with
  an additive character and uses Cauchy–Schwarz.

modules.title: Few translates fill
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
Let a finite group act unitarily on `T`, let `pr₀` be the projection onto a stable subspace `T₀`,
and let `B : S → T` be linear. Suppose that `pr₀ B` is almost an isometry from below in mean square
and that the second moment of the operators `B* s B` is nearly as small as Cauchy–Schwarz allows.
Then a few translates `s pr₀ B` span almost all of `T₀`. In this file `‖A‖`, written of a linear map
`A`, is its Hilbert–Schmidt norm.

* `New.hilbertSchmidtNorm`, `New.IsNearIsometry`: the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, and the first
  hypothesis.
* `New.isSpread_of_second_moment`: for any subspace `W` of `T₀`, the preimage of `W` under some
  translate `s pr₀ B` is small, in terms of the share of `W` in `T₀` (`New.IsSpread`).
* `New.IsSpread.exists_few_le_finrank_iSup_range`: a logarithm times `dim T₀ / dim S` translates
  span almost all of `T₀`.
modules.literature:
Rank bounds from second moments: Welch 1974. Greedy covering with a logarithmic loss: Wolsey, Greedy
algorithm for the submodular set covering problem, 1982.

modules.title: The dimension of the target and one good translate of the Poincaré map
modules.group: The second moment and the spanning theorem
modules.note:
For admissible data `D`, the finite group `Ḡ = D.chosenGL` acts on the forms on `Y₀`, and `e₀`
projects them onto the target `D.targetForms`, the good forms, of dimension `D.targetDim`. The
source `D.SourceForm` is the space of the forms that the Poincaré map `P = D.poincare` sends to
forms on `Y₀`. This file supplies the hypotheses of the lemma on one translate,
`New.isSpread_of_second_moment`, for `P` and draws its conclusion. The spanning theorem itself,
`New.Data.enough_forms`, is deduced in `New.Reduction.ShortAndEnough`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.targetDim_le_card_mul_besselDegree_mul_mass`: the target has dimension at most
  `#Ḡ · deg · mass_r`. It is counted on the definite space `D.spaceW D.m`, where the level is free.
* `New.Data.hasAmplitudeBlocks_scaledPoincare`: the blocks of `P* s P`, once `P` is scaled
  (`New.Data.scaledPoincare`).
* `New.Data.bad_types_rare`: `e₀` is a product of two central idempotents, one for each level prime,
  and their complements have a small coefficient at `1`.
* `New.Data.isNearIsometry_e₀_comp_scaledPoincare`,
  `New.Data.targetDim_mul_sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sq_le`: the two hypotheses of the lemma on one
  translate.
* `New.Data.isSpread_goodPoincare`: for every space of target forms, with share `α` of the
  dimension, some translate `s e₀ P` has a preimage of dimension at most about `(1 + α) / 2` times
  the dimension of the source.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.filling`: the data `New.Filling` attached to `D`: the level `N`, the two level primes
  with their chosen places, and Bessel systems chosen from `New.Data.exists_besselSystem`.
* `New.Filling.besselDegree`: the product `deg` of the formal degrees at the infinite places.
* `New.mass`: the mass `mass_r` of the genus of the standard lattice of rank `r`.
* `New.Data.paramW`: twice the parameter `New.Data.targetParameter`, indexed by the basis of `Y₀`.
* `New.Data.RowIndex`: the index set of the basis of `Y₀`.
modules.literature:
For every space `F` of target forms, with share `α` of the dimension, some translate `s e₀ P` has
rank modulo `F` at least nearly `(1 - α) / 2` times the dimension of the source. Spanning by
Poincaré series and the link between least second moment and tight frames are known in the
literature. Related work: Petersson, Über die Entwicklungskoeffizienten der automorphen Formen,
1932; Benedetto–Fickus, Finite normalized tight frames, 2003; Muić, Spectral decomposition of
compactly supported Poincaré series and existence of cusp forms, 2010.

modules.title: Spherical Hecke operators away from the level, and eigensystems
modules.note:
The level `M` is the product of the primes `D.levelPrime 0`, `D.levelPrime 1`, and `D.chosenPlace`
runs through the chosen places above it. The spherical Hecke operators away from `M` form an algebra
that acts at once on the forms `D.principalForms V` of principal level for all hermitian spaces `V`.
It commutes with the finite group `D.chosenGL`, so it acts on the good forms `D.goodForms V`, the
image of the idempotent `D.e₀`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.sphericalAlgebra`, `New.Data.heckeAlgebra`: the spherical elements of the group algebra
  and the operators that they give; `New.Data.heckeOnGood` is the action on good forms.
* `New.Data.heckeOperator`: the operators `T_{w,i}` at the places `New.Data.IsSplitOffLevel`, as
  members of the Hecke algebra; `New.Data.principalHeckeSplit` is the operator on one space.
* `New.Data.eigenPart`: the part with a given eigensystem. The parts are independent
  (`New.Data.iSupIndep_eigenPart`), and in finite dimension they span the forms
  (`New.Data.iSup_eigenPart_eq_top`).
* `New.Data.exists_hecke_proj_eigenPart`: a Hecke operator that is `1` on one part and `0` on
  finitely many others.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms on `V` of archimedean type `typeKernel D.paramW s` that are
  fixed by the principal level `J_M = D.chosenLevel` at the chosen places; `V.formRep` is the
  action of the finite adelic unitary group `G_f = Gf E n` on forms, and `K₀ = stdLevel E n` is its
  standard maximal compact subgroup.
* `New.heckeSplit`: the Hecke operator `T_{w,i}` at a split place `w`, of the double coset of
  `diag (ϖ 1_i, 1)`.
* `New.universalLevelAlgebra`: the elements of a group algebra that keep the vectors of a given
  level in every representation.

modules.title: Equality of multiplicities
modules.note:
The spaces `Y_0, W_1, …, W_m` share the group `G_fin`, the level and the parameter, and differ only
in their signs at the real places. Let `V`, `V'` be two hermitian spaces for whose signs the
parameter `New.Data.paramW` has gap `D.gap`. Then a spherical Hecke operator away from the level `M`
has the same trace on their good forms. The equality of traces is deduced from the comparison of
traces for a test function that is cuspidal at one split place (`New.trace_eq_of_isCuspidalAt`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_heckeAlgebra_eq_mul_inner_of_hasSum_rallisTerm`: the sums of scalar multiples of
  the Rallis series on two spaces are the same multiples of matrix coefficients of one element of
  the Hecke algebra.
* `New.Data.trace_heckeOnGood_eq`, `New.Data.charpoly_heckeOnGood_eq`,
  `New.Data.det_heckeOnGood_eq`: equal traces, characteristic polynomials and determinants.
* `New.Data.rallisOnGood`, `New.Data.det_rallisOnGood_eq`: the Rallis series preserves the good
  forms and has the same determinant on the good forms of both spaces.
* `New.Data.finrank_goodForms_inf_eigenPart_eq`: each eigensystem has the same multiplicity.
* `New.Data.targetDim_eq_finrank_goodForms_spaceW`: the good forms on `Y_0` and on `W_j` have the
  same dimension.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms fixed by the principal level `D.chosenLevel` at the chosen
  places above `M`.
* `New.Data.principalRep`: the action on them of `D.chosenGL = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w)`, over the chosen places
  w.
* `New.Data.goodForms`: the image of the idempotent `D.e₀` on these forms.
* `New.Data.heckeAlgebra`, `New.Data.eigenPart`: the spherical Hecke operators away from `M`, and
  the part with a given eigensystem.
* `New.HCParam.HasGap`: entries of the parameter with different signs are at least `h` apart.
modules.literature:
The equality of traces is the analogue of the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for a quaternion
algebra that is ramified exactly at the real places. Related work: Harris–Labesse, Conditional base
change for unitary groups, 2004; Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes, 2011.

modules.title: Bessel systems at a real place: length and norm bounds, lattice basis, discriminant
modules.note:
The file sets up the objects that connect the analysis at one real place with the filling argument.
`New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of a hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, a positive
space X₀ with basis κ and a vector z with h(z, z) = −1. The frame is (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z). The Bessel
subgroup `New.Shape.Form.besselS` is generated by the unipotent group 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`
and by `New.Shape.Form.besselH` = U(X₀). `New.frameVector y a` is the image under `y⁻¹` of the
`a`-th frame vector. The file first proves elementary bounds on the length `New.besselLength y`, the
infimum of `‖s * y‖ + 1` over `s` in `besselS`. It then defines the lattice basis, the discriminant
𝗀 and the link, and the structure `New.BesselSystem` listing what is used of a Bessel function W and
its cut W♭. Norms on G₁ are those of the Euclidean norm for which the basis e_a, x_i, z, e*_a is
orthonormal. The frame has n = ϱ + 1 vectors.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.norm_add_one_le_of_mem_frameBox`: `‖y‖` is bounded by the lengths of `y⁻¹ e_a`, `y⁻¹ z` and
  `y⁻¹ e*_a`.
* `New.orthoFrame`, `New.gramSchmidtMatrix`: Gram–Schmidt for the frame. The orthogonal vectors are
  left invariant under `besselS` (`New.orthoFrame_besselS_mul`), and the Bessel length bounds their
  lengths on both sides (`New.norm_orthoFrame_mem_Icc`). The triangular matrix depends continuously
  on the point (`New.continuous_gramSchmidtMatrix`).
* `New.besselLength_le_of_norm_orthoFrame`: conversely, these lengths bound `besselLength y`; the
  proof corrects `y` on the left until the first bound applies. `New.besselLength_le_of_dual` is the
  case of a frame with a bounded triangular dual system.
* `New.besselLatticeBasis`: the basis of the lattice, in which `x_{k₀}` is replaced by
  `v = x_{k₀} / p̄ + z / N`. `New.gram_besselLatticeBasis` gives its Gram matrix, with middle block
  `New.latticeMiddleGram`.
* `New.frameDisc`: the quantity `|D_{ϱ+1}|² - N² |D_ϱ|²` in the leading minors `New.leadingMinor`,
  written `𝗀`. Up to sign it is the Gram determinant of the frame and its image under an isometry
  (`New.det_gram_framePair`).
* `New.IsCutPair`: the L² bounds of W and W♭, the support of W♭, and decay below a common integrable
  majorant (`New.IsDecayMajorant`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.besselFrame`: The indices of the frame (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z) among the basis indices.
* `New.Shape.middleGram`: for a scalar N, the diagonal matrix on κ plus one point, with entries 1 on
  κ and −N at the extra point.
modules.literature:
References on Bessel functions and kernels are in `New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData`; references on
the decay of discrete series coefficients are in `New.Spanning.Bessel.CutTailBound`.

modules.title: The Gram section γ_Z of the frame Gram matrix map on the unitary group G₁
modules.note:
For `γ` in the unitary group `New.Shape.G₁`, let `Z(γ) = New.realFrameGram γ = Fᴴ J₁ γ F` be the
matrix of products of the frame `F = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` with its translate by `γ`. Let
`Ω = New.Shape.openCell` be the open set of invertible `Z` for which `ξ(Z) = invCorner Z`, the last
diagonal entry of `Z⁻¹`, has absolute value less than `1`. The file writes down an explicit matrix
`γ_Z` for `Z ∈ Ω` and proves that it is real differentiable with polynomial bounds.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealPlace.sectionMatrix`: a matrix in two variables `Z`, `W`, equal to `γ_Z` at `W = Zᴴ`.
* `New.RealPlace.differentiableAt_sectionMatrix`,
  `New.RealPlace.norm_sectionMatrix_le_and_norm_fderiv_le`: the matrix is real differentiable in
  `Z`, with polynomial bounds for it and its derivative.
  `New.RealPlace.IsBoundedInCell.norm_sectionMatrix_le` asks for bounds at the point `Z` only.
* `New.RealPlace.gramSection`: on `Ω` the matrix is an isometry of `J₁`
  (`New.RealPlace.sectionMatrix_isometry`), so it is the matrix of an
  element `γ_Z` of `G₁` (`New.RealPlace.coe_gramSection`).
* `New.RealPlace.measurable_gramSection`: the section is measurable.
* `New.RealPlace.realFrameGram_gramSection`: `Z(γ_Z) = Z` for `Z ∈ Ω`.
* `New.RealPlace.exists_eq_mul_gramSection_mul`: by Witt's theorem, `Z(γ) = Z ∈ Ω` determines `γ` up
  to factors `unipotentOf q * embedH k`, which fix the frame, on both sides.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: the index set of the basis `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `x_k` (`k ∈ κ`), `z`,
  `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ`; `k₀ = New.Shape.k₀` is a distinguished index in `κ`.
* `New.Shape.J₁`: the Gram matrix of the hermitian form defining `G₁`, with `ϱ` hyperbolic pairs
  `e_a, e*_a`, the identity on the span `X₀` of the `x_k` (`k ∈ κ`), and `h(z, z) = -1`.
* `New.Shape.frameCols`, `New.Shape.dualFrameCols`: the matrices `F` and `F'` whose columns are the
  basis vectors `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` and `(e*₁, …, e*_ϱ, x_{k₀})`.
* `New.Shape.FrameMatrix`: the complex `(ϱ+1) × (ϱ+1)` matrices; `New.Shape.top` is the last index.

modules.title: Normalisation of a Bessel function and of its cut
modules.note:
Let `W` be an integrable Bessel function on G₁ whose type is an irreducible representation of the
compact group `U(κ)`. The operator `∫ W ⊗ W^*` over 𝖴∖G₁ commutes with this representation, so it
is a scalar, and its trace is the squared L² norm of `W`.

* `New.BesselSystem.orthonormal`: for the full function of a Bessel system the operator is `1`, so
  its coordinates are orthonormal in L²(𝖴∖G₁).
* `New.IsCutPair.exists_integral_cut_mul_conj_eq`: for the cut function it is a scalar between `0`
  and `1`.
* `New.IsCutPair.lintegral_sq_inner_cut_le`: the upper bound, tested on a vector.

Notions from other files:

* `New.Shape.G₁`: the unitary group G₁ of the complex hermitian form given by a shape; `U(κ)` is
  the unitary group of the standard positive form on the index set κ of the shape, embedded in G₁
  by `New.RealPlace.embedH`.
* `New.besselQuotMeasure`: the measure on G₁ that computes integrals over 𝖴∖G₁, where 𝖴 is the
  unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`.
* `New.IsBesselFunction`: a bounded measurable function on G₁ that transforms on the left by a
  fixed character under 𝖴 and by a unitary representation, its type, under `U(κ)`.
* `New.IsCutPair`: a Bessel function (`.full`) whose squared L² norm is the dimension of its
  value space, and its cut (`.cut`): a Bessel function that vanishes outside a region of bounded
  size, is close to it in L² and agrees with it where the size is small.
* `New.BesselSystem`: a cut pair of irreducible type, with further bounds.

modules.title: The mean value inequality over the Gram matrix of two frames
modules.note:
Let `G₁` be the real unitary group `New.Shape.G₁`, `e = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` its frame, `R°` the fixer
of the frame, the product of the unipotent group `𝖴⁰ = New.Shape.Form.besselU0` and the compact
group `H = U(κ)`, and `γ_Z = New.RealPlace.gramSection Z` the section of the map that sends `γ` to
the matrix `Z` of the products of `e` with `γ e`, over the open set `Ω = New.Shape.openCell` of the
invertible `Z` whose inverse has last diagonal entry of absolute value less than `1`.

On the frames `y = γ e` the fibre measure of the Gram map is compared with Haar measure in
`New.LeGramFibre.mconv_fixerHaar_le`. This file bounds the same fibre measure from below, by `dZ`
times a measure on the frames whose products with `e` form the matrix `Z`. Such a frame is `y' Z`
with `y'` dual to `e`. The first `ϱ` vectors of `y'` are moved by `𝖴⁰`, and the part of the last one
in `X₀ = ℂ ^ κ` runs over a sphere.

One can find the measure on the frames over `Z` by letting both frames vary and dividing two
equalities of fibre measures, the one on pairs of frames, which are tuples of `2 (ϱ + 1)` vectors
with an invertible Gram matrix, by the one on frames. Here a fibre measure enters only through the
relation of being at most it (`New.LeFibreMeasure`); the measure over `Z` is computed directly in
coordinates as a lower bound, and the fibre measure on frames is used as an upper bound.

* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_eq_lintegral_sphereMass_mul_dualFrameOfGram`: Lebesgue measure on the
  tuples dual to the frame, in terms of their Gram matrix and of `R°`.
* `New.RealPlace.leGramFibre_gramSectionMeasure`: the law of `s γ_Z e`, with a density proportional
  to `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal Z ^ (|κ| - 1)`, is at most the fibre measure.
* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_le`: the mean value inequality for the integral of
  `f (s' γ_Z s)` over `s, s'` in `R°` and `Z` in `Ω`.

Notions from other files:
* `fixerHaar 𝔰`: the measure `du dh` on `R°`, with `u = unipotentOf q` for Lebesgue measure `dq` and
  `embedH h` for the Haar probability measure `dh` on `U(κ)`.
* `frameCols`, `dualCols`, `isotropicCols`, `definiteCols`, `freeCols`: the matrices with the
  columns `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `e*_b`, `e_b`, `x_i`, and `(e_b, x_i)` respectively.
* `J₁`: the hermitian form on the space with the basis `e_b, x_i, z, e*_b`, which pairs `e_b` with
  `e*_b`, is the identity on `X₀` and is `-1` at `z`.
* `top`, `k`, `k₀`: the last index of the frame, the number `|κ|` and a chosen element of `κ`.
* `embedH h`: the element of `G₁` that acts by `h` on `X₀` and fixes the other basis vectors.
* `hermOfReal t`: the hermitian matrix with the real coordinates `t`.
modules.literature:
Part of the bound on the open cell for the Bessel integrals at a real place; see
`New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData`. For fibre measures of the Gram map compare Siegel, Über die
analytische Theorie der quadratischen Formen, Ann. of Math. 36 (1935).

modules.title: Unfolding bounds over G₁ and the L² bound at the section γ_Z via Sobolev
modules.note:
`New.Shape.G₁` is the complex unitary group of the shape `𝔰`, with index set
`New.Shape.BesselIndex`. `𝖴 = New.Shape.Form.besselU` is its Bessel unipotent group, and
`𝖴⁰ = New.Shape.Form.besselU0` is the subgroup of `𝖴` fixing the frame e₁, …, e_ϱ, z; their Haar
measures are `New.Shape.besselHaar` and `New.Shape.besselHaar₀`. An unfolding inequality bounds
suitable integrals over `G₁` by integrals over `𝖴∖G₁`. An `L²` bound on the quotient `𝖴∖G₁` for
convolutions, the hypothesis `New.RealPlace.HasSchurBound`, then gives an `L²` bound on a bounded
part of the orbit of the section `γ_Z = New.RealPlace.gramSection Z`, at the price of a power of a
size bound `P`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.lintegral_mul_le_of_frameMatrix_le`: the unfolding bound on `G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.HasDerivWords`: families that behave like iterated right derivatives on `G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_integral_le`: the bound for the convolution at `γ_Z (u h)⁻¹`,
  integrated over `h ∈ U(κ)` and the `u ∈ 𝖴⁰` with `‖u‖ ≤ P ^ 20`. Sobolev's inequality on a small
  cube at `Z` (`New.sobolev_trace_cube`) replaces the value at `Z` by mean squares of derivatives,
  which are bounded by integrals over `𝖴∖G₁`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.besselS`: the Bessel subgroup, generated by `𝖴` and by the image of `U(κ)` under
  `New.RealPlace.embedH`.
* `New.besselQuotMeasure`: the measure on `G₁` that integrates a `𝖴`-invariant function over
  `𝖴∖G₁`.
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal`: 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|², D_ϱ the leading principal minor of order
  ϱ. In the coordinates `γ_Z` Haar measure has density at least c_G 𝗀(Z)^{|κ|−1}, with
  c_G = `New.Shape.openCellConst` (`New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_le`).
* `New.realFrameGram`: for y in `G₁`, the matrix of hermitian products of the frame vectors with
  their images under y; it sends `γ_Z` to Z when Z lies in the open cell Ω = `New.Shape.openCell`.
* `New.RealPlace.IsBoundedInCell Z P`: Z lies in Ω, and ‖Z⁻¹‖, ‖Z‖ and (1 − |ξ|²)^{−1/2} are at
  most P, where ξ is the last diagonal entry of Z⁻¹.

modules.title: The group of the Bessel period at a real place
modules.note:
The group `R = U ⋊ H` at one real place, its Haar measure `du dh`, and the integral over `R` that
defines the Bessel function.

Here a shape `𝔰` gives the number of hyperbolic planes and the index set `κ` of the middle block,
`𝔰.G₁` is the unitary group of the hermitian space of that shape, `besselU` (the `U` of
`R = U ⋊ H`) is its block upper unitriangular subgroup, `H` is the image of the unitary group
`U(κ)` under `embedH`, and `besselS` is the Bessel subgroup generated by `besselU` and `H`.

modules.title: Bounds near a point of Ω and the open cell bound for a Bessel system
modules.note:
Write Ω = `New.Shape.openCell`, 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|² and ν(Z)² = 1 − |ξ|², where ξ is the last
diagonal entry of Z⁻¹. At and near a point `Z` of Ω (so `0 < 𝗀(Z)`) the matrix, its inverse, 𝗀 and ν
obey explicit size bounds. Such bounds on a ball supply the hypothesis of
`New.RealPlace.lintegral_gramSection_integral_le`. For a Bessel system, a family of kernels is then
shown to be an `L²` contraction at each `γ` in `New.Shape.G₁` whose frame Gram matrix lies in Ω,
provided that some `y` and `γ⁻¹ y` both lie in a frame box of large enough size.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.RealPlace.isBoundedInCell_of_inv_le_gramDiscReal`: if `M⁻¹ ≤ 𝗀(Z)` and the entries of `Z` are
  at most `M ^ 2`, a power of `M` bounds the matrix, its inverse and `1 / ν`.
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal_div_two_le_and_isBoundedInCell`: on a small ball about such a `Z` the
  matrix stays in Ω with these bounds, and 𝗀 drops by at most a factor two.
* `New.BesselSystem.exists_isOpenCellBound`: the family of shifted kernels is a contraction from
  `L²(ν)` to `L²(m)`, with `m` a probability measure and `ν` of total mass at most `pairingBoundSq`
  (`New.BesselSystem.IsOpenCellBound`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.RealPlace.gramDiscReal`: 𝗀(Z) = |det Z|² − |D_ϱ|² for a (ϱ+1)×(ϱ+1) complex matrix Z
  (`New.Shape.FrameMatrix`), where D_l (`New.leadingMinor`) is the leading principal minor of order
  l.
* `New.Shape.openCell`: The set of invertible (ϱ+1)×(ϱ+1) complex matrices whose inverse has last
  diagonal entry ξ of absolute value less than 1; `New.RealPlace.oneSubNormSqInvCorner` is
  ν² = 1 − |ξ|².
* `New.RealPlace.gramSection`: For Z in Ω, an element γ_Z of G₁ whose frame Gram matrix
  (`New.realFrameGram`) is Z.
* `New.frameBox`: The set of y in G₁ such that every vector y⁻¹f_a of the moved frame
  (`New.frameVector`) has Euclidean norm at most a given bound.
* `New.besselLength`: For y in G₁, the infimum of ‖sy‖ + 1 over s in the Bessel subgroup S
  (`New.Shape.Form.besselS`).
* `New.BesselSystem 𝔰 B f`: a Bessel function `besselFn .full` on G₁ with values in ℂ^I, its cut
  `besselFn .cut` and their bounds. The real `B ≥ 8 r` (r the rank of G₁) sets the scale of the
  bounds, the natural number `f` the rate of decay, and |I| / `deg` is the constant of Schur's
  bound.

modules.title: One pairing on the open cell, at all places together
modules.note:
Let `X` be a finite family of Bessel systems (`New.BesselSystem`), `W` the tensor product of their
Bessel functions and `W♭` that of their cuts. Let `φ` be a function of `z` of modulus at most `1`,
left invariant under the fixers of the frames and not necessarily a product over the places, such
that `φ (z) W♭ (γ z) ⊗ W♭ (z)^*` vanishes outside boxes. The integral of this product is bounded by
the root of the product of the local bounds `New.pairingBoundSq`, plus the integral of `‖φ‖` times
the norm of the difference between the uncut and cut kernels.

The operator bounds of `New.BesselSystem.exists_isOpenCellBound` multiply over the places, and one
shift that is no worse than the mean gives the bound for `W`.

Notions from other files:
* `BesselSystem`: two continuous functions on the group `G₁`, `besselFn .full` and its cut
  `besselFn .cut`, with values in `ℂ^I`, parameters `b` and `f`, and a degree `deg`.
* `frameBox ρ`: the `y` with `‖y⁻¹ f_a‖ ≤ ρ` for every vector `f_a` of the frame; `besselFixer` is
  the subgroup that fixes these vectors.
* `besselLength y`: the infimum of `‖s y‖ + 1` over `s` in the Bessel subgroup.
* `realFrameGram γ`: the matrix of products `h(f_a, γ f_b)` for the hermitian form `h`;
  `gramDiscReal Z` is `|det Z| ^ 2 - |D| ^ 2`, with `D` the leading minor one size smaller.
* `pairingBoundSq γ deg ρ d`: the square of the bound of the open cell at one place, a power of
  `ρ ^ (9 n) / 𝗀` times `d ^ 2 / (deg * openCellConst * (𝗀 / 2) ^ (k - 1))`, where
  `𝗀 = gramDiscReal (realFrameGram γ)`, `n = 𝔰.n` and `k = 𝔰.k`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.BesselSystem.pairKernel`: the matrix of `W (y) ⊗ W (γ⁻¹ y)^*`. Its adjoint is the matrix of
  `W (γ⁻¹ y) ⊗ W (y)^*`, which is `New.BesselSystem.piKernel` at `γ⁻¹`.
* `New.BesselSystem.enorm_integral_pairKernel_cut_le`: compact support and the bound for the pairing
  of the cut functions.

modules.title: Bessel systems of discrete series type and a Bessel function large at a point
modules.note:
Given a unitary frame that diagonalises the form `New.Shape.J₁`,
`New.Filling.IsDiscreteSeriesBessel` ties an abstract Bessel system `New.BesselSystem` to a discrete
series parameter `l` and a weight `kw` of the subgroup `H = U(X₀)`. Let `𝖴` be the unipotent group
`New.Shape.Form.besselU` and let `R = 𝖴 H` be the Bessel group, realised as the subgroup
`New.Shape.besselGraph` of `G₁ × H`. There is a point `x` of bounded size at which the period of a
discrete series coefficient over `R` is large. For a parameter of large gap, the average of the
coefficient over `R` converges absolutely (`integrable_besselIntegrand`). It is a Bessel function
(`isBesselFunction_besselAverage`) that the kernel of the discrete series reproduces
(`convolve_besselAverage`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.UnitarySignFrame`: a unitary frame taking `J₁` to the diagonal matrix of signs
  `ε`.
* `New.Filling.IsDiscreteSeriesBessel`: the Bessel system has type `(l, kw)`.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsSteep.exists_stationary_point`: a point `x` of bounded length at which the
  period over `R` is large. It carries the stationary position of `U(X₀)` to the standard frame.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.G₁`: the unitary group of the complex hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, the
  standard positive form on X₀ = ℂ^κ, and one vector z with h(z, z) = −1. Its Gram matrix is
  `splitGram ϱ (middleGram κ 1)`, indexed by `New.Shape.BesselIndex`. Here n = ϱ + 1, k = |κ| and
  r is the dimension of the whole space.
* `New.Shape.besselGraph`: the Bessel group `R = 𝖴 H`, stored as the pairs of an element of G₁ and
  its image in H, with the measure `du dh`.
* `New.simpleRootSum`: the sum of the entries just above the diagonal on the frame e₁, …, e_ϱ, z.
* `New.besselLength`: for y in G₁, the infimum of ‖s y‖ + 1 over s in R; it is the length of y.
* `New.HCParam.HasLargeGap l A`: for `l = 2λ` with N coordinates, the entries are distinct, of the
  parity of N − 1, and entries of `λ` at coordinates of opposite sign are 500 N³ + A apart or more.
modules.literature:
See `New.Appendix.DiscreteSeries.Periods` for related work. See
`Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bessel.UnipotentHaarMeasure` for sources.

modules.title: The Bessel function at a real place: decay and cut
modules.note:
The file concerns Bessel functions (`New.IsBesselFunction`) on the real unitary group
G₁ = `New.Shape.G₁`: bounded functions to ℂ^I that transform on the left by a character of the
unipotent group 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU` and by `rep` under H = U(κ). Throughout, p is a unitary
frame that diagonalises the form, c_λ = `New.HCParam.dsCoeffInFrame` is the discrete series
coefficient of a parameter l = 2λ with large gap (`New.HCParam.HasLargeGap`), v is a unit vector of
ℂ^I, and e = deg·c_λ with deg = `New.HCParam.formalDegree`. F is reproduced by e if F * e = F for
the convolution `New.convolve`: (F * e)(y) = ∫ e(a⁻¹) F(ya) da. The measure of 𝖴∖G₁ is
`New.besselQuotMeasure`. G₁ consists of r × r matrices with r = `𝔰.r`, ‖g‖ is the operator norm, and
n = `𝔰.n` = ϱ + 1 with ϱ the number of hyperbolic planes of the form.
* `New.exists_isDecayMajorant_besselAverage`: the normalised average of c_λ over the Bessel subgroup
  decays in the length, below a bounded integrable weight (`New.IsDecayMajorant`).
* `New.besselCut`: the cut of a function at length b^(6n+2); it is close to the function in L²
  (`New.IsDecayMajorant.lintegral_sq_besselCut_sub_le`).
* `New.exists_isCutPair_besselAverage`: a multiple of the average is reproduced by e and forms a cut
  pair (`New.IsCutPair`) with its cut.

Notions from other files:
* `New.besselLength`: for y in G₁, the infimum of ‖sy‖ + 1 over s in the Bessel subgroup S = 𝖴H
  (`New.Shape.Form.besselS`).
* `New.Shape.besselGraph`: the group 𝖴H as a graph, the pairs (g, k) in G₁ × U(κ) with k⁻¹g in 𝖴.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.besselAverage`: the function y ↦ ∫_S c_λ(x⁻¹ s y) π(s)⁻¹ v ds, where π is the
  character on 𝖴 and `rep` on H.
* `New.scaledBesselLength`: the larger of 1 and the length divided by b^(6n).
modules.literature:
A Bessel function at a real place, an average of a discrete series coefficient with a large period
integral, inherits the coefficient's decay. Normalised and multiplied by a scalar cut-off, it gives
a continuous approximant, close in L² and compactly supported modulo the unipotent group, with an
explicit tail bound. Related work: Muić, Fourier coefficients of automorphic forms and integrable
discrete series, 2015; Miličić, Asymptotic behavior of matrix coefficients of the discrete series,
1977; Wallach, Real Reductive Groups II, 1992.

See `New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData` for related work.

modules.title: Schur's bound for a Bessel function and its derivatives
modules.note:
Let `l = 2λ` be a doubled Harish-Chandra parameter of large gap and `c_λ` the coefficient `dsCoeff`
on `U(diag ε)` of its discrete series; the same letter stands for its pullback
`New.HCParam.dsCoeffInFrame` to `G₁` by the frame. Let `deg` be the formal degree
`New.HCParam.formalDegree`. Write `(F * k) y = ∫ k a⁻¹ • F (y a)` and `e = deg · c_λ`; as
`e a⁻¹ = deg · conj (c_λ a)`, the condition `F * e = F` says that `F` is fixed by the idempotent of
the discrete series. Such a bounded function has right derivatives of all orders, and they are
convolutions with kernels of controlled norm. Schur's bound in `L²(𝖴 ∖ G₁)` follows, `𝖴` being the
unipotent group `besselU`.

Notions from other files:
* `l : New.HCParam ε` is twice a Harish-Chandra parameter; `HasLargeGap A` bounds its gaps below.
* `p : UnitarySignFrame 𝔰 ε` is a unitary frame in which the form of `G₁` is `diag ε`.
* `frameEquiv : G₁ ≃ₜ* U(diag ε)` is conjugation by the frame.
* `Bumps ε` are the smooth compactly supported functions on `U(diag ε)`; `smear f` sends a bump `β`
  to the convolution of the continuous function `f` with `β`.
* `bumpDeriv` is the action of matrices on bumps by differentiation, `adTwist g` precomposes it with
  conjugation by `g`, and `word w` applies the action of the matrix units of the word `w`.
* `New.IsBesselFunction rep F`: `F` is bounded, measurable and transforms by a character under
  `besselU` and by `rep` under `U(κ)`.
* `𝔰.r` is the number of indices `BesselIndex` of `G₁`, and `𝔰.n` is one more than the number of
  hyperbolic planes of the shape `𝔰`.
* `RealPlace.HasSchurBound F rep B C`: `F` has right derivatives of all orders that are again Bessel
  functions, those of order `s ≤ 2 n ^ 2` satisfying Schur's `L²` bound with `B ^ (2 s) C`.
* `besselQuotMeasure` is the measure on `G₁` that represents integration over `besselU ∖ G₁`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Smoothness and Schur's orthogonality relations for vectors of a discrete series
representation (Harish-Chandra).

modules.title: Filling data from admissible data, with Bessel systems at the real places
modules.note:
The filling theorem is stated for abstract data (`New.Filling`). This file builds such data from
admissible data D (`New.Data`). At each real place it constructs a Bessel system of the type fixed
by D. It then assembles these systems, the relevant primes and places, and the level `D.levelX 0`
into the filling data. It identifies that level with the preimage of the level K(M) of
`New.Filling.principalLevel`: here M = p₀ p₁, and K(M) includes a congruence modulo π.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_besselSystem`: the Bessel function at a real place, with its normalisation,
  Schur's bound, decay, cut and local bounds. That its coordinates are orthonormal is
  `New.BesselSystem.orthonormal`, in `New.Spanning.Bessel.Orthonormality`.
* `New.Data.filling`: the prime `New.Data.N`, the primes p₀, p₁ (field `levelPrime`) with their
  chosen places, the level `D.levelX 0` and a Bessel system at each infinite place.
* `New.Data.levelX_zero_eq_comap`: the level `D.levelX 0` is the preimage of the principal
  congruence subgroup K(M), that is `New.Filling.principalLevel`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.piNIdele`: the principal finite idele of `π`, where `N = π π̄`; `New.Data.piNPlaces` is
  the set of places dividing `π`.
* `New.Data.piM`: the conjugate of the integer `D.piMBar` of norm `p₀ p₁`; the chosen places are its
  prime divisors.
modules.literature:
At a real place, integrals of a Bessel function on an indefinite unitary group against its
translates have Fourier transforms decaying beyond a band; the bounds themselves are proved in the
imported files. These integrals replace Petersson's J-Bessel kernel in showing that few translates
almost span the target forms. Rank one is classical, and Bessel kernels are studied for GL(n) and
GSp(4).

Related work: Petersson, Über die Entwicklungskoeffizienten der automorphen Formen, 1932; NIST DLMF
§10.22; Baruch, Bessel distributions on the open cell, 2001–2004; Comtat et al., Effective Kuznetsov
trace formula for GSp(4), 2025.

modules.title: The data, standing hypotheses and amplitudes of the filling theorem
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The data and the vocabulary of the filling theorem. The space is `V` = (`ϱ` hyperbolic
planes) ⊕ `X₀ ⊕ E z`, with `X₀` definite of rank `k = |κ|` and `h(z, z) = -N`. Its Gram matrix is
`New.Shape.Form.splitGram`, its indices are `New.Shape.BesselIndex`, and the frame
`New.Shape.besselFrame` is `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`.

* `New.Filling`, `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the data with its size hypotheses, and the standing
  hypotheses.
* `New.Filling.G`, `New.Filling.GFin`, `New.Filling.ResidueGL`: `U(V)` over a ring, over the finite
  adeles in the lattice basis, and the product of `GL` over the residue fields of the chosen places.
* `New.Filling.ratToInf`, `New.Filling.ratToFin`, `New.Filling.reduction`: the maps to the infinite
  places (rescaled to `New.Shape.G₁`), to the finite adeles, and reduction.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`, `New.Filling.amplitude`, `New.Filling.amplitudeSum`: the rational terms
  over a block `(c, s, c')`, made of two classes and an element of `ResidueGL`; the amplitude of a
  term; and the sum of the amplitudes over a set `T` of terms. Divided by `unipotentCovolume`, this
  sum is the contribution of `T` to the block. Integrals over the quotients of G_∞ by the groups
  `classUnipotent c` are written with the cutoffs `classCutoff c`.
* `New.Filling.Agrees`, `New.Filling.IsStable`, `New.Filling.termsOfLink`: the elements of
  `ResidueGL` that respect the unipotent character, the stable sets of terms, and the terms of
  nonzero discriminant with a given link.

Letters in the docstrings: 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU` is the unipotent group,
𝖴⁰ = `New.Shape.Form.besselU0` is its subgroup fixing the frame, and H is `U(X₀)`. The group
`New.Shape.Form.besselS` is generated by 𝖴 and H. G_∞ is the product of copies of `New.Shape.G₁`
over the infinite places. K = `latticeStabilizer`, K(M) = `principalLevel`, h_c = `classRep c`,
Λ = `frameScaleProd`, and f_0, …, f_ϱ is the frame.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape`: the number ϱ, the index set κ of X₀ and one index k₀ in κ; k = |κ| and n = ϱ + 1.
* `New.BesselSystem`: for the real number b, two continuous functions W (`FullOrCut.full`) and W♭
