  (`FullOrCut.cut`) from G₁ to ℂ^I, I a finite index set, that satisfy bounds in b and in a positive
  constant `deg`; they are Bessel functions of an irreducible representation of U(k) on ℂ^I.
* `New.frameDisc`: for Z of size ϱ+1 with leading minors D_l, the quantity |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|²,
  where |x|² means x x̄.

modules.title: Bessel data: level subgroup, Eichler maps and strong approximation for the unipotent group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The file works with filling data `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` and the unitary group `S.G` of the form
`T.splitGram`, where `T` is the middle Gram matrix, at rational points, finite adeles and
archimedean points. The middle space is X₀ ⊕ E z, with X₀ spanned by the basis vectors indexed by
`κ`. Write 𝖴 for the Bessel unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`. Write H for
`New.Shape.Form.besselH`, the unitary group U(X₀), acting only on the basis vectors indexed by `κ`.
Write `New.Shape.Form.besselS` for the group they generate. Write σ = `New.simpleRootSum` for the
sum of the entries just above the diagonal on the frame. The level is `S.M = p₀ p₁` with
`pᵢ = S.levelPrime i`, and `S.chosenPlaces i` are the chosen places of norm `pᵢ`. K(M) is
`S.principalLevel`. For a class c, h_c = `S.classRep c` is its representative in H. For classes c,
d, `S.translateByClassReps c d γ` is h_c⁻¹ γ h_d, and `S.termsOver c s d` is the set of rational γ
with `S.translateByClassReps c d γ` integral of reduction s.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.besselFn_adelicToInf_mul_eq_prod_wave_smul`, `New.Filling.besselFn_ratToInf_mul`: how
  the Bessel function `New.Filling.besselFn` transforms under left translation by `𝖴`.
* `New.exists_mem_besselU_eq_eichlerMap`: for a hermitian invertible form, if x is a combination of
  the frame vectors of index below a and v is orthogonal to these vectors, then the Eichler map
  along x and v, with ς = τ h(v, v), lies in the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`; the lemma
  also computes its `New.simpleRootSum`.
* `New.besselU_dense`, `New.Filling.exists_besselU_approx`: strong approximation for 𝖴.
* `New.Filling.mem_reducedImage_besselU_iff_exists_termsOver`,
  `New.Filling.prod_wave_eq_star_unipotentChar`: the rational points of 𝖴 that are integral for a
  class map onto the reduction of the integral points of 𝖴(𝔸_f), and on them the character at
  infinity is the conjugate of the finite character at an integral point with the same reduction.
* `New.Filling.exists_besselS_mem_termsOver`: each reduction `s` of an integral element of
  `New.Shape.Form.besselS` is reached from each class c by a rational element of
  `New.Shape.Form.besselS`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: The Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix T: identity blocks pair the first and last ϱ indices, T is the middle block, all else is
  zero.
* `New.Filling.selfDualChar`: The additive character x ↦ ψ_f(−x/ϖ) of the finite adeles.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: The standing hypotheses on the data: among them, `sourceLevel` is the
  preimage of K(M), `reduction` is onto, and some size inequalities hold.
* `S.GFin`: The finite adelic points of the unitary group in the lattice basis.
* `New.Filling.unipotentChar`: The value of the additive character `S.selfDualChar` at M⁻¹ σ(u),
  where σ(u) = `New.simpleRootSum u` sums the entries of u at the simple roots.

modules.title: Near terms in the filling theorem: frames, cell ranks, nearness and integrality
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The terms `γ` of the count in the filling theorem are rational elements of the unitary group.
The data are `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` for a shape `𝔰`, with the size hypotheses
`New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, which compare all constants with powers of the large parameter `b`.
For the frame `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `New.frameImage γ` is the matrix of its image under `γ`, and
`S.frameProducts γ` is the Gram matrix of the frame against its image, with leading minors
`New.leadingMinor`. This file describes how the flags of the frame and of its image under `γ` meet,
defines the cell rank and nearness of `γ`, proves a norm identity for `S.termDisc γ`, bounds the
Gram entries of near terms by powers of `S.b`, and shows that the Gram entries of terms are
algebraic integers.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.CharsAgree`, `New.PairOccursAt`, `New.Filling.HasCellRank`: the terms that respect
  the unipotent character, the vectors common to the two flags of a term, and its cell rank.
* `New.Filling.IsNear`: `γ` is near if some boxed point `y` (`New.Filling.boxedPoints`) has `γ⁻¹ y`
  boxed.
* `New.Filling.norm_sq_middle_part_eq`, `New.Filling.map_termDisc_eq_norm`: a norm identity, which
  makes `S.termDisc γ` real and nonnegative at every infinite place. So `S.termDisc γ` is totally
  positive or zero (`New.Filling.termDisc_pos_or_eq_zero`).
* `New.Filling.IsNear.norm_frameProducts_le`, `New.Filling.IsNear.norm_map_leadingMinor_sq_le`: for
  a near term, the Gram entries and the leading minors are bounded by powers of the size parameter
  `S.b`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.G`: for a commutative ring R with involution, the unitary group over R of ϱ
  hyperbolic pairs and the middle Gram matrix diag(1, …, 1, −N) on X₀ ⊕ Ez, in the basis e₁, …, e_ϱ;
  x_i (i in κ), z; e*₁, …, e*_ϱ.
* `New.Filling.termDisc`: 𝗀(γ) = |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|², with D_l the leading minors of
  `New.Filling.frameProducts γ`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselU0`: the Bessel unipotent group 𝖴 of isometries
  that are block upper unitriangular and trivial on the middle block, and its elements that fix each
  vector of the frame.
* `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`, `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment`: the numbers
  sourceDim² / (besselDegree · mass), with the mass of the genus of the standard lattice, and
  sourceDim times the order of the reduced image of the Bessel subgroup `besselS`.

modules.title: Links of isometries, the link isometry Υ_γ, and invariance under `besselU`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
Let `γ` be an isometry of the form `T.splitGram`, which is made of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a
middle space with Gram matrix `T`. Let `A` be the span of the first `ϱ` basis vectors, and let
`New.frameImage γ` be the image of the frame `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`. The link of `γ` is the set of pairs
of middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`.

A filling `S` over a CM field `E` provides a prime `N = S.N`. Its middle space is `X₀ ⊥ E z_N`,
where `X₀` has an orthonormal basis indexed by `𝔰.κ` and `z = z_N` has the norm `-N`. The positive
space `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` has the same coordinates, and `z⁺` has the norm `N`. After an exchange of the
`z_N`-coordinates of the two members of each pair (`linkSource`, `linkTarget`), the link is the
graph of an isometry `Υ_γ` (`linkIsometry`) of the positive space. The quantity `termDisc γ`
vanishes if and only if the spans of the frame and of its image under `γ` share a nonzero vector.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.link_inv_mul_mul_of_mem_besselU`,
  `New.Filling.frameDisc_frameGram_inv_mul_mul_of_mem_besselU`: the link and `New.frameDisc` are
  unchanged under `γ ↦ u⁻¹ γ u'` with `u`, `u'` in `besselU`.
* `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom.besselU_mul`, `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom.inv`: the norm-one pair
  condition is preserved by left multiplication by `besselU` and by inversion. With the invariance
  of the minors and of `termDisc`, this makes the cells stable (`New.Filling.isStable_hasCellRank`).
* `New.Filling.frameDisc_weylElem_mul`, `New.Filling.link_weylElem_mul_eq_iff`: values on the big
  cell, at `weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p * σ` with `σ` an isometry of the middle space. There the link determines
  `σ`.
* `New.Filling.linkIsometry`, `New.Filling.mem_link_iff_linkIsometry`: the isometry `Υ_γ`, and the
  link as its graph.
* `New.Filling.linkIsometry_frameImage_mulVec`, `New.Filling.mul_dotProduct_comp_indexX₀_eq_sub`:
  the link on combinations of the second frame, and the norm identity that follows.
* `New.Filling.termDisc_eq_zero_iff`: the criterion for the vanishing of `termDisc γ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix `T`. The basis is `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, the middle vectors, `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ` (indices `New.eStar`).
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the isometries that are block upper unitriangular for this basis.
* `New.Shape.Form.frameGram`: the `(ϱ + 1) × (ϱ + 1)` matrix of the products `h(f_j, γ f_l)` of the
  frame `f` with its image under `γ`, where `h` is the form `T.splitGram`.
* `New.Filling`: arithmetic data over a CM field `E`, among them the prime `S.N`. The matrix
  `S.ratMiddle E` is the Gram matrix of `X₀ ⊥ E z_N`, `S.ratGram` is its `splitGram`, `S.G E` is the
  group of isometries of `S.ratGram`, and `S.frameProducts γ` is the frame Gram matrix of `γ`.
* `New.frameDisc`: for a matrix of size `ϱ + 1` with leading minors `D_l`, the quantity
  `|D_{ϱ+1}|² - N² |D_ϱ|²`. Its value at `S.N` and the frame Gram matrix of `γ` is
  `New.Filling.termDisc γ`.
* `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`, the condition that a norm-one pair occurs from `j`: there is a
  `c` with `c c̄ = 1` such that, for every frame index `a ≥ j` (counted from `0`), the flags of `f`
  and `γ f` share a vector with leading coefficients `c` and `1` at `a`.

modules.title: Eichler-type unipotent elements, colouring bounds and reduced points
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file gives explicit elements of the congruence subgroup `New.Filling.classUnipotent` of
`New.Shape.Form.besselU` by Eichler's formula along isotropic basis vectors `e_a`. It also proves
counting tools for the remaining terms: weighted sums are bounded by colouring, and the index of a
scaled lattice is computed.
Finally, every point at the infinite places is moved to a reduced point by exactly one coset of
unipotent elements, so that the indicator of the reduced points is a partition of unity in boxes.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_mem_classUnipotent_eq_one_add_smul`: the general element, along several `e_a`
  at once.
* `New.Filling.exists_eichler_classUnipotent`: an element with one prescribed row.
* `New.Filling.tsum_le_of_encard_range_le`: a weighted sum is at most the number of colours times
  the bound for one colour; `New.Filling.tsum_le_relIndex_pow_mul`: colours are residue classes
  modulo a subgroup of finite index.
* `New.Filling.IsResidueDomain.exists_mul_mem_reducedPoints_iff_rightCoset`: exactly one coset of
  unipotent elements moves a point to a reduced point (`New.Filling.reducedPoints`).
* `New.Filling.IsResidueDomain.isBoxPartitionOfUnity`: the indicator of the reduced points has the
  properties `New.Filling.IsBoxPartitionOfUnity`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.classUnipotent c`: the group `𝖴_c(M)` of rational unipotent elements that lie in the
  principal congruence subgroup at the class `c`; `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀ c` is its subgroup
  fixing the frame `e_1, …, e_ϱ, z`, whose indices are given by `New.Shape.besselFrame`.
* `New.Filling.IsResidueDomain`: a measurable set `D` of representatives modulo `M 𝓞_E` of modulus
  at most `b ^ 26`; `New.Filling.reducedPoints D`: the points with all entries of their triangular
  matrix above the diagonal in `D`.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses, among them `|ϖ| ≤ b` and `1 ≤ |κ_v|` at
  every infinite place.

Here and below `M = S.M` is the level of the filling data `S`.

modules.title: Class cutoffs and counting frames in boxes
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The translates of the cutoff `S.classCutoff c` of a class `c` are shown to add up to one, and
weights bounded by cutoffs are shown to add up to at most a bound for the number of frames in a box.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.frameImage_eq_frameImage_one_of_close`: a term that moves the frame vectors of a
  point in a box very little fixes the frame.
* `New.Filling.encard_image_frameImage_le`: terms `γ` with `γ⁻¹ y` in a box have few images of the
  frame, since the frame vectors of the points `γ⁻¹ y` lie in a ball and are separated.
* `New.Filling.tsum_le_of_le_classCutoff_mul`: weights bounded by cutoffs add up to at most that
  bound for the number of frames.

Notions from other files:
* `New.frameImage`, `New.frameVector`: the image `γ f` of the frame `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` under a
  matrix `γ`, and the vector `y⁻¹ f_a` in Euclidean space.
* `New.frameBox`, `New.besselLength`: the points whose frame vectors have norm at most `ρ`, and the
  infimum of `‖s y‖ + 1` (operator norm) over `s` in the Bessel subgroup.
* `New.Filling.frameBoxRadius`, `New.Filling.basisScale`: the number `S.b ^ (37 n)`, and the scales
  of the normalised basis at an infinite place.
* `New.Filling.classUnipotent`, `New.Filling.classCutoff`: the congruence group of rational
  unipotent elements attached to a class `c`, and a cutoff for its subgroup fixing the frame times
  the indicator of the reduced points.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: the rational `γ` with `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` integral and of reduction `s`, where
  `h_c` is the representative `New.Filling.classRep` of the class `c`.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses, among them the size inequalities between
  `S.b`, `S.realM v` and `S.N`.

modules.title: The Bessel kernel and the integral of a class cutoff over the real unipotent group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves that the kernel `New.Filling.besselKernel`, the tensor
`besselFn(y) ⊗ besselFn(γ⁻¹ y)^*` of Bessel functions at the infinite places, is continuous.
It bounds the amplitude `New.Filling.amplitude` by the integral of the norms
`New.Filling.amplitudeMajorant`. It then computes the integral of a class cutoff
`S.classCutoff c` over the real unipotent group as `S.unipotentCovolume`. The group is unfolded
one coordinate at a time (`New.Filling.rowCoords`). The integral is then a product of covolumes of
explicit lattices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.enorm_amplitude_le`: the norm of the amplitude
  `∫ β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹ y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹ y)^* dy` is at most the integral of the norm of its integrand.
* `New.Filling.lintegral_classCutoff_eq_unipotentCovolume`: let `E` contain a primitive 5040th
  root of unity and let `S` be admissible. For every class `c` and archimedean point `y`, the
  integral of the cutoff `u ↦ S.classCutoff c (u y)` over the real unipotent group 𝖴_∞, for the
  product of the Haar measures `New.Shape.besselHaar`, is the number `S.unipotentCovolume`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.besselFn`: for a tuple `i` of coordinates (`New.Filling.BesselCoord`), the product
  over the places `v` of the `i v`-th coordinate of `W side (y v)`.
* `New.Filling.M`, `New.Filling.classUnipotent`: the level M = p₀ p₁, the product of the two primes
  `S.levelPrime`; the rational points u of 𝖴 with h_c⁻¹ u h_c in the principal congruence
  subgroup K(M).
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselS`: the group 𝖴 of block upper unitriangular
  isometries, and the Bessel subgroup, which 𝖴 generates together with the unitary group of the
  standard form on κ.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses. The level `sourceLevel` is the preimage of
  K(M), `reduction` is onto, and size inequalities hold between b, M and ϖ, κ_v, N, the second
  moments, the number of Bessel coordinates, an index and the constant `scaledSiegelConst`.
* `New.Filling.unipotentCovolume`: an explicit positive number built from M, N, |κ|, ϱ, the
  discriminant of E and the scales of the frame at the infinite places.

modules.title: Sums of amplitudes over blocks
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves convergence, change of weight and the behaviour under the Bessel subgroup of the
block sums `S.amplitudeSum side T c s c'`. The block is the sum, over the rational `γ ∈ T` that lie
over `(c, s, c')` (`New.Filling.termsOver`), of the amplitudes
`∫ β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹ y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹ y)^* dy`. Here `β_c = S.classCutoff c` is a cutoff for the group
`S.classUnipotent c`, the argument `side : FullOrCut` selects the full or the cut Bessel function
`W`, and `ν = New.Filling.unipotentCovolume`. The listed results assume that `S` is admissible
(`New.Filling.IsAdmissible`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_tsum_classCutoff_mul_prod_enorm_le`,
  `New.Filling.tsum_amplitudeMajorant_lt_top`,
  `New.Filling.tsum_lintegral_enorm_besselKernel_sub_cut_le`: the sums are bounded and converge
  absolutely, and cutting `W` changes them little.
* `New.Filling.hasSum_amplitudeSum_of_cutoff`: for stable `T`, any measurable weight with orbit sums
  `1` may replace the product of the cutoffs `S.classCutoff c` and `S.classCutoff c'`.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_mul_mul_inv`, `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_besselU_mul`: moving a block by
  the Bessel subgroup; the unipotent part acts through the character `New.Filling.unipotentChar`.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_eq_zero_of_not_agrees`: the block of a stable set vanishes unless `s`
  agrees.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_besselS_one_eq_ite`: for the full Bessel function only, at `s = 1` the
  Bessel subgroup contributes `S.unipotentCovolume` times the identity if `c = c'`, and `0`
  otherwise.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`, `New.Filling.reduction`, `New.Filling.ResidueGL`: the group K of
  integral elements of the finite adelic unitary group, and its reduction modulo the chosen places
  above p₀ and p₁, with values in the product `ResidueGL` of the general linear groups over the
  residue fields. The kernel is K(M) = `New.Filling.principalLevel`.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: a rational `γ` is a term over `(c, s, c')` if h_c⁻¹ γ h_c' lies in K and
  has reduction `s`; here h_c = `S.classRep c` represents the class `c`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselS`, `New.Filling.IsStable`: the group 𝖴 of block
  upper unitriangular isometries, and the Bessel subgroup, which 𝖴 generates together with the
  unitary group of the standard form on κ; a set `T` of rational elements is stable if
  multiplication on either side by rational points of 𝖴 does not affect membership in `T`.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses. The level `sourceLevel` is the preimage of
  K(M), `reduction` is onto, and size inequalities hold between b, M and ϖ, κ_v, N, the second
  moments, the number of Bessel coordinates, an index and the constant `scaledSiegelConst`.
* `New.Filling.classUnipotent`, `New.Filling.unipotentCovolume`: the rational points u of 𝖴 with
  h_c⁻¹ u h_c in the principal congruence subgroup K(M); an explicit positive number built from M,
  N, |κ|, ϱ, the discriminant of E and the scales of the frame at the infinite places.
modules.literature:
The results on block sums belong to two steps: the bound for the second moment of the Poincaré
series (`New.Spanning.Unfolding.Moments`, which lists related work) and the bound for degenerate
terms and pairs with different links (`New.Spanning.RemainingTerms.Sum`).

modules.title: Residue lifts, lattice charts and common flag vectors: which filling terms contribute
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file sorts the terms of the second moment of the filling theorem and shows which of them
contribute. Common vectors of two flags are moved up the flags by elementary linear algebra.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.mem_congruenceGL_iff_isIntMatrix_scaleAt`: for an integral idele `p` that is a unit
  at one of each pair of conjugate places, a unitary `k` is integral with row `o` congruent to that
  of `1` modulo `p` iff `k - 1` stays integral after dividing row `o` by `p` and column `o` by `p̄`.
* `New.Filling.inclHFin_mem_latticeStabilizer_iff`: `S.inclHFin k` is integral iff `k` is integral
  and its row `k₀` is congruent to that of `1` modulo `S.piN`.
* `New.Filling.MeetsAt`, `New.Filling.fixer`, `New.Filling.IsOpenElement`,
  `New.Filling.InScalarCoset`: the meeting places, and the subsets of the finite group.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum_eq_zero_of_not_charsAgree`: a stable set of terms none of which agrees
  contributes `0`.
* `New.Filling.mul_star_eq_and_pairOccursAt_of_le`,
  `New.Filling.exists_pairOccursInColumnsAt_top_of_meetsAt`: when the characters agree, the leading
  coefficients of a common vector of two flags have equal norms and recur at all higher indices over
  `E`; modulo a place above `M` where the flags meet, some pair not both zero occurs at the top
  index.
* `New.Filling.CharsAgree.exists_hasCellRank`: a term with agreeing characters and discriminant `0`
  has a cell rank.

Notions from other files:
* `S : New.Filling E 𝔰`: the filling data over the CM field `E`; `S.chosenPlaces i` is a set of
  places of `E` of norm the prime `S.levelPrime i` (`i = 0, 1`). The places above `M` are these and
  their conjugates, indexed by pairs `(w, false)` and `(w, true)`.
* `S.latticeStabilizer`, `S.reduction`, `S.ResidueGL`: the integral elements of the finite adelic
  unitary group, and their reduction to the product of the general linear groups over the residue
  fields `ResField w` at the chosen places.
* `New.frameImage γ`: the columns of `γ` at the indices of the frame `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`; so
  `frameImage 1` is the frame itself.
* `S.CharsAgree γ`, for rational `γ`: the character `S.unipotentChar` takes equal values on rational
  `u`, `u'` in `besselU` with `u γ = γ u'`. `S.Agrees s` is the analogue for `s` in `S.ResidueGL`.
* `besselH`, `besselU`, `besselS`: the unitary group of `X₀`, the unipotent group of the frame, and
  the Bessel subgroup that they generate.
* `Ô E`, `𝔸f E`: the integral finite adeles and the finite adeles of `E`.
modules.literature:
Take a rational element under which the unipotent character of the Poincaré series agrees with its
conjugate. For such an element, a vector shared by the standard frame and its image forces a
norm-one pair to occur. Take an integral adelic element k whose reduction modulo M agrees, and two
integral vectors orthogonal, in the standard form, to all vectors of f and kf but the last of each
(f is the frame). If the determinant δ of their products with these two last vectors is a finite
idele, the norm of the product of the primes over M where the span of f meets that of kf is at most
the index of δÔ in Ô (`New.Filling.meetNorm_le_genIndex_det`). This sorts the terms of the unfolded
second moment. Related work: Friedberg, Poincaré series for GL(n), 1987; Y. Liu, Relative trace
formulae toward Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods, 2014; Furusawa–Shalika, Central critical values
of degree four L-functions for GSp(4), Mem. AMS 782, 2003.

modules.title: The finite groups `Ū`, `H̄` and `R̄`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The factor of `Ū = S.reducedImage besselU` at each chosen place `w` consists of the block
unitriangular matrices over `𝔽_w` (`mem_reducedImage_besselU`). Counting free entries gives the
order of `Ū` (`card_reducedImage_besselU`). Each element of `R̄ = S.reducedImage besselS` is a
product of elements of `Ū` and `H̄ = S.reducedImage besselH` (`mem_reducedImage_besselS`), and
these two meet in the identity, giving `|R̄| = |H̄| |Ū|` (`card_reducedImage_besselS`). The order of
`H̄` is the index of `S.principalLevel.comap S.inclHFin` in `S.latticeStabilizer.comap S.inclHFin`
(`relIndex_comap_principalLevel`).

Notions from other files:
* `unitriangular lev R`: the invertible matrices over `R` that agree with `1` at the entries
  `(i, j)` with `lev j ≤ lev i`; `BesselIndex.level` is the level function of the Bessel basis.
* `S : Filling E 𝔰`: the data of the filling theorem, among them the sets `S.chosenPlaces i`.
* `S.latticeStabilizer`: the elements of the finite adelic unitary group `S.GFin` that are
  invertible over the integral adeles `Ô E`; `S.reduction` reduces them modulo the chosen places.
* `S.reducedImage B`: the image of `B ⊓ S.latticeStabilizer` under `S.reduction`.

modules.title: The structure of a term
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
An element `γ` gives two frames, with the spans `A⁺` and `γ A⁺`, and two isotropic spaces `A` and
`γ A` with the intersection `I_γ`. This file describes `A⁺_γ = A⁺ + γ A⁺`, its radical and its
orthogonal complement, which modulo `I_γ` is isometric to `X₀^γ = X₀ ∩ Υ_γ⁻¹ X₀` by the map
`framePerpToX₀`. For an element that agrees and has `gr(γ) = 0` it proves that `A = A_{≤j} ⊕ I_γ`
and `γ A = γ A_{≤j} ⊕ I_γ` for `j = n - 1 - rk I_γ`, and that `j` is the cell rank of `γ`. It also
shows that `I_{u γ u'} = u I_γ` for `u`, `u'` in the unipotent group `U₀`, and that agreement
depends only on the double coset `U₀ γ U₀`. Finally it defines the set `Γ*` (`remainingTerms`) of
the terms that are left for the estimate of the second moment.

Here `n = ϱ + 1`, the frame is `e_1, …, e_{n-1}, z_N` (indexed from `0` in the code), `A` is spanned
by `e_1, …, e_{n-1}`, `A⁺ = A + E z_N`, and `A_{≤j}` is spanned by the first `j` vectors of the
frame. The space has rank `r` and `A^⊥ / A = X₀ ⊥ E z_N` with `X₀` of rank `k`. For `y` orthogonal
to `A` and `γ A` the classes of `y` and `γ⁻¹ y` are `y₀ + λ' z_N` and `y₀' + λ z_N`. A pair
`(μ, μ')` occurs at an index `a` if the two frames share a vector with coefficients `μ`, `μ'` at `a`
and `0` above `a`. In names, `_one` and `_coe` after a word for a span, as in `isotropicSpan_one`
and `flagSpan_coe`, refer to the frames `e_•` and `γ e_•`. The hypothesis `HasPrimitiveRoot5040 E`
says that `E` contains a primitive root of unity of order `5040`.

Notions from other files:
* `linkIsometry γ` is the link isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` with `y₀ + λ z⁺ ↦ y₀' + λ' z⁺`.
* `termDisc γ` is `gr(γ) = |δ_n|² - N² |δ_{n-1}|²` for the leading minors `δ_j` of the matrix
  `frameProducts γ` of products of the two frames.
* `CharsAgree γ` (`γ` agrees) says that the character `unipotentChar` takes the same value at
  rational `u`, `u'` in `U₀` whenever `u γ = γ u'`.
* `HasCellRank j γ` says that one pair `(ζ, 1)` with `ζ ζ̄ = 1` occurs at all indices `a ≥ j`
  (`NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`), that `δ_j ≠ 0`, and that `j = n` exactly when `gr(γ) ≠ 0`.

modules.title: The expansion of the squares and the second moment near the Bessel subgroup
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves the expansion of the squares and the bound on the second moment near `R̄₀`, where
`R̄₀ = reducedImage besselS` is the reduction of the Bessel subgroup. These results concern the
operators `P_s = P* s P`, stated in terms of their blocks. The terms in the Bessel subgroup give the
operator `r_ψ(s)`, which is `New.Filling.besselTranslate`, and the terms off it give `P_s - r_ψ(s)`.
Along the way it treats the terms of cell rank `0` and the cosets `ζ R̄₀` by integral `ζ ∈ E` with
`ζ ζ̄ = 1`, called roots of unity (these are the roots of unity of `E`, by Kronecker's theorem), and
it computes the blocks of the Bessel subgroup.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.sqrt_secondMoment_compl_besselS_le`: the expansion of the squares.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_compl_besselS_le`: `P_s` is close to `r_ψ(s)` near `R̄₀`.

Notions from other files:
* `termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` such that `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` (`translateByClassReps`) is integral
  with reduction `s`; such a `γ` lies over the block `(c, s, c')`.
* `amplitudeSum side T c s c'`: the sum of the amplitudes of the elements of `T` over that block.
* `secondMoment A Ω`: the sum of `‖A c s c'‖² / unipotentCovolume²` over all classes `c`, `c'` and
  `s ∈ Ω`.
* `reducedImage A`: the image in the finite group `ResidueGL` of the integral elements of `A`.

modules.title: The second moment over the whole group
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file proves the bound on the sum of the second moments of the operators `P_s = P* s P` over the
whole group, stated in terms of their blocks. It bounds the contribution of the cosets of `R̄₀` and
that of the elements that are not open.

The blocks of `P_s` are the complex conjugates of the sums `amplitudeSum` over all terms, divided by
`unipotentCovolume`, so `‖P_s‖²` (Hilbert–Schmidt norm) is the `secondMoment` of these sums at `s`.
In the same way the terms in the Bessel subgroup `R₀ = besselS` give `r_ψ(s)`, and those off it give
`P_s - r_ψ(s)`. The operator `r_ψ(s)` is `New.Filling.besselTranslate`; the passage from operators
to blocks is `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks`.

We write `R̄₀` for `reducedImage besselS`, `D_X` for `sourceDim`, `𝒟_id` for `identitySecondMoment`,
`𝒟_main` for `mainSecondMoment`, `b` for the parameter `S.b` of the filling, `p_i` for
`levelPrime i`, `M = p₀ p₁` for the level, `f` for the number of infinite places, `k = |κ|`,
`n = ϱ + 1` for the length of the frame, `e₁` for its vector of index `0` and `δ_l` for the leading
minors of `frameGram`. In `InScalarCoset ζ s` the scalar `ζ` is an integral adele, acting through
its residues.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.sum_secondMoment_le`: `∑ ‖P_s‖² ≤ (1 + 9 b⁻⁴) 𝒟_main`, if `s ↦ ‖P_s‖²` has positive
  type and `‖P_1‖² ≤ 2 D_X`.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_univ_eq_secondMoment_compl_besselS`: if `Ω` is disjoint from the
  reduction `R̄₀` of the Bessel subgroup, then the terms in the Bessel subgroup give `0` over `Ω`,
  so all terms and the terms off the Bessel subgroup have the same second moment over `Ω`.

Notions from other files:
* `termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` such that `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` (`translateByClassReps`) is integral
  with reduction `s`; such a `γ` lies over the block `(c, s, c')`.
* `amplitudeSum side T c s c'`: the sum of the amplitudes of the elements of `T` over that block.
* `secondMoment A Ω`: the sum of `‖A c s c'‖² / unipotentCovolume²` over all classes `c`, `c'` and
  `s ∈ Ω`.
* `reducedImage A`: the image in the finite group `ResidueGL` of the integral elements of `A`.

modules.title: The second moments of the operators `P* s P`, and good forms
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
Let `S` be admissible filling data, with size parameter `b = S.b`. The finite group
`Ḡ = S.ResidueGL` has one factor for each of the two level primes `p_i = S.levelPrime i`, and
`R̄₀ = S.reducedImage besselS` is the image of the Bessel subgroup in it. The source is the space of
dimension `D_X = S.sourceDim` with coordinates indexed by the classes and the coordinates of the
Bessel function. For a map `P` from the source to a representation `ρ` of `Ḡ` put `P_s = P* ρ(s) P`;
all norms of operators are Hilbert–Schmidt norms. The file proves the two moment bounds for the
`P_s`, and deduces that `e₀ P` is almost an isometry for the projection `e₀` onto the target forms.
We write `𝒟_id = S.identitySecondMoment` and `𝒟_main = S.mainSecondMoment`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks`: the blocks of `P_s` are the conjugates of the amplitude sums,
  divided by the covolume.
* `New.Filling.besselTranslate`: the unitary representation `r_ψ` of `R̄₀` on the source, extended
  by `0`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sub_besselTranslate_sq_le`: over `R̄₀`
  times one factor of `Ḡ`, `∑ ‖P_s - r_ψ(s)‖² ≤ b⁻¹² 𝒟_id`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.hilbertSchmidtNorm_sub_one_sq_le`: `‖P* P - 1‖² ≤ b⁻¹² D_X`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.sum_hilbertSchmidtNorm_sq_le`: `∑ ‖P_s‖² ≤ (1 + 9 b⁻⁴) 𝒟_main`
  over `Ḡ`.
* `New.Filling.HasAmplitudeBlocks.isNearIsometry_piTensorElem_comp`: `e₀ P` is almost an isometry in
  mean square, with the error `5 b⁻⁴`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.reduction`: the homomorphism from the stabilizer `K = S.latticeStabilizer` of the
  lattice to `Ḡ` that reduces matrix entries modulo the chosen places above `p₀` and `p₁`.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: the terms over a block `(c, s, c')`, the rational `γ` such that
  `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` lies in `K` and has reduction `s`.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeSum`: the sum of the amplitudes of the terms of a set over a block.
* `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment`, `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`: the numbers `#R̄₀ · D_X` and
  `D_X² / (deg · mass)`, with `deg = S.besselDegree` and the mass `New.mass` of the genus of the
  standard lattice of rank `r`.
modules.literature:
For the normalised Poincaré map `P`, the mean over level translates `s` of `‖P* s P‖²` is at most
nearly `D_X² / D₀`, with `D₀` the expected dimension of the target, and bad types carry little of
`P`. In rank one, Poisson summation on a product of two Kloosterman sides with a sharp diagonal term
is known in the literature. Related work: Herman, Beyond endoscopy for the Rankin–Selberg
L-function, 2011; Iwaniec–Li, The orthogonality of Hecke eigenvalues, 2007;
Michel–Ramakrishnan–Yang, Bessel periods on U(2,1)×U(1,1), 2023.

See `New.Spanning.SecondMoment.SpanningTheorem` and `New.Spanning.RemainingTerms.Sum` for related
work.

modules.title: Poincaré series of fitting spaces, unfolding, Petersson products and source form coordinates
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
This file builds Poincaré series from the Bessel functions of filling data S (`New.Filling`) on a
hermitian space V that fits S, and computes their Petersson products.

K = `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer` and K(M) = `New.Filling.principalLevel` are levels in the
lattice basis of S. Here K(M) is the kernel of reduction at the chosen places, and M in this
notation is the product of the two level primes, not an adelic point. For a graded space Y on V that
fits S, the groups attached to Y correspond to those of S under `New.Filling.Fits.adelicEquiv` and
`New.Filling.Fits.finiteEquiv`, and algebraic forms of level `S.sourceLevel` get coordinates indexed
by classes and indices.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.Fits`: V matches S; this gives the identifications `New.Filling.Fits.ratEquiv`
  (rational points), `New.Filling.Fits.realHomeomorph` (infinite places) and
  `New.Filling.Fits.finiteEquiv` (finite places).
* `New.Filling.Fits.cutBessel`, `New.Filling.Fits.poincareSeries`: a coordinate i of the Bessel
  function, cut off and supported on the coset of a class c, and the series ∑_a φ_a ∑_γ of these,
  a = (c, i).
* `New.Filling.Fits.petersson_poincare`: the Petersson products of translated series are the
  amplitude sums `New.Filling.amplitudeSum` times the volume of the level.
* `New.Filling.Fits.poincareMap`, `New.Filling.Fits.coe_poincareMap`: the series are forms of level
  `New.Filling.stdPrincipalLevel`, linear in φ.
* `New.Filling.Fits.sourceFormCoords`: algebraic forms of level `S.sourceLevel` as vectors of the
  Euclidean space on classes times indices.
* `New.Filling.Fits.finrank_levelSpace_eq_sourceDim`: the dimension of the space of these forms is
  the number of classes times the dimension of the weight, and it is positive.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.besselFn`: W_i(y), the product over the infinite places v of the i_v-th coordinate of
  the local Bessel function W_v at y_v. Only the full (not the cut) function is used: `.full`.
* `New.Filling.classRep`, `New.Filling.classUnipotent`, `New.Filling.classCutoff`: for a class c,
  its representative h_c, the group 𝖴_c(M) of rational unipotent u with h_c⁻¹ u h_c ∈ K(M), and a
  cutoff β_c at the infinite places whose translates under 𝖴_c(M) sum to 1.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: the rational γ such that h_c⁻¹ γ h_c' lies in K and has reduction s.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the Bessel unipotent group 𝖴: the isometries of
  `New.Shape.Form.splitGram` T that are block upper unitriangular for the levels
  `New.BesselIndex.level`, so trivial on the middle block.
* X₀ is the hermitian space on κ with the standard form, all signs +1; U(X₀) is its unitary group.
modules.literature:
The file also contains known results stated on this proof's data: Poincaré series along a Bessel
subgroup and their unfolding. See `Lib.DiscreteSeries.Bruhat.FloorGroups`.

modules.title: The Bessel function as an integral over `R(F_∞)`
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
The group `R(F_∞)` is the product of the groups `R` at the infinite places. So the tensor product of
the local Bessel functions, each an integral over `R`, is one integral over `R(F_∞)`.

Notions from other files:
* `GInf E ε` is `G(F_∞)`, one copy of `U(diag ε)` for each infinite place of `E`, and `New.G E ε` is
  the adelic group `G(F_∞) × G(𝔸_f)` of the hermitian space `V`. The group `𝔰.G₁` is the complex
  unitary group of `ϱ` hyperbolic planes, the positive form with basis `𝔰.κ` and a negative vector.
* `S.Fits V l kw Y η`: the grading `Y` of `V` is standardly indexed, the Bessel system of the
  filling data `S` at each infinite place `v` has type `(l v, kw v)`, the kernel `typeKernel l ε` is
  idempotent, and the finite part of `V.x` is described by `S` and the central element `η`.
* `Y.besselGroup` is `R = U ⋊ H`, with `U = Y.unipotent` and `H` the unitary group of `κ`, embedded
  by `Y.inclX`; `Y.leviPart (n * Y.inclX a) = a`, and `Y.besselReal` is the group `R(F_∞)` of the
  real points of `R`.
* `𝔰.besselGraph` is the local group `R`, as pairs `(g, a)` in `G₁ × U(κ)` with `g (embedH a)⁻¹` in
  the local unipotent group `besselU`.
* `S.adelicToInf` takes the components at the infinite places in rescaled bases, and
  `h.realHomeomorph` identifies `G(F_∞)` with the product of copies of `G₁`: at each place it
  changes the basis and multiplies on the left by a fixed element, made from the distinguished
  matrix `V.x` of `V`.
* `𝔰.besselGraphMeasure` is the Haar measure `du dh` on the local group `R`, and
  `(l v).dsCoeffInFrame` is the coefficient of the discrete series of parameter `l v` on `G₁`.
* `S.besselSystem v` is the Bessel system at `v`. Its functions take values in `ℂ^I`, with
  `I = (S.besselSystem v).Index` finite, and `U(κ)` acts on `ℂ^I` by the unitary matrices
  `(S.besselSystem v).rep`. An element of `S.BesselCoord` is a choice of one index in `I` at each
  `v`, so `S.BesselCoord → ℂ` is the tensor product of the spaces `ℂ^I`.
* `WeylIndex 𝔰.κ kw` indexes a basis of the Weyl module of weight `kw`, in which forms take values.
* `h.weylBesselEquiv` is a fixed linear identification of the values of forms with the dual of the
  values of the Bessel function, and `ψ_U` is the generic character of `Y.unipotent`.
modules.literature: Related work on Bessel periods and on second moments is listed in `New.Spanning.Unfolding.Moments`.

modules.title: Masses of spheres and of frames
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
For the data `D` and an infinite place `v`, the file defines the mass `sph_l` of the unit sphere of
`ℂ ^ l` and the product `fr_v = N ^ k sph_{k+1} ⋯ sph_r`. By the approximate formula for the ratio
of masses in consecutive ranks, the product of the `fr_v` over the infinite places is at most
`N ^ (k f) mass_k / mass_r` up to a factor close to one, where `f` is the number of infinite places
and `mass_l` is the mass `New.mass` in rank `l`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.unitSphereMass`, `New.Data.frameMass`: the numbers `sph_l` and `fr_v`.
* `New.Data.prod_frameMass_mul_le`: the upper bound for the product of the `fr_v`.
* `New.Data.prod_frameMass_mul_openCellConst_eq`: the product of the `fr_v` in terms of the
  constants `New.Filling.siegelConst` and `New.Shape.openCellConst`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data`: the data: a CM field `E` with `f` infinite places (the type `D.Φ`) and root
  discriminant `rd = D.rootDisc`, a generator `P.deltaE D.towerExp` of its different, a prime level
  `N`, a weight `b`, the length `x` of the prime sum, and ranks `r = k + 2 ϱ + 1`.
* `New.Data.shape`: the shape of the hermitian space `Y₀` of rank `r`, which is the sum of `ϱ`
  hyperbolic planes, a space `X₀` of rank `k` and a line.
* `New.mass E l`: the mass of the genus of the standard hermitian lattice `O_E ^ l`.
* `New.Filling.siegelConst`: `c_S = (π ^ k / ((k - 1)! N ^ k)) ^ f |disc E| ^ (1/4) vol(Ô) ^ k`.
* `New.Shape.openCellConst`: `c_G = vol U(k) (2 π ^ k / (k - 1)!) / vol U(r)`.
* `New.volÔ E`: the volume `vol(Ô) = (2 / rd) ^ f` of the integral finite adeles.

modules.title: Filling data for admissible data: fit to Y₀, Bessel bounds, standing hypotheses
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
For admissible data `D`, the file shows that the filling data `New.Data.filling` fit the space `Y₀`.
It also shows that they satisfy the standing hypotheses `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, so that the
general filling theorem applies.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.filling_fits`: the filling data `New.Data.filling` fit the space `Y₀`
  (`New.Filling.Fits`).
* `New.Data.sourceFormCoords`: source forms in coordinates, indexed by pairs (class, Bessel
  coordinate).
* `New.Data.goodProjTranslate`: the map from forms of level `M` on `Y₀` to the image of the good
  idempotent `New.Data.e₀`. It is a translation followed by this idempotent, scaled by the order of
  the finite group `𝖦`.
* `New.Data.card_besselSystem_le_pow`, `New.Data.card_besselCoord_le_pow`: the Bessel system at one
  place has at most `b ^ (2 k)` coordinates, and their tensor product at most `b ^ (2 k f)`.
* `New.Data.log_filling_besselDegree_mem_Icc`: two-sided bounds for the logarithm of the degree of
  the Bessel systems.
* `New.Data.card_mul_card_classes_mul_prod_le`, `New.Data.card_sq_mul_mass_mul_prod_le`: two
  products built from group orders, class number, masses, dimensions and degrees are at most
  `(1 + b⁻⁹)` times `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`. `New.Data.card_mul_prod_frameMass_le` states
  both.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.spaceY`: for an index `j`, the hermitian space `Y_j` with its adelic frame, hence its
  lattice `𝖬_j`, chosen as in `New.Data.exists_space_isStd_of_le_and_gram_eq_of_lt`. Only `j = 0`
  occurs in this file.
* `New.Data.chosenGL`: The finite group 𝖦 = ∏ GL_r(𝔽_w), over the chosen places w above p₀ and p₁.
* `New.Data.targetParameter`: The entry i (from 0) of the target parameter at v: k/2 − 1 − i for
  i < k − 1, and Δ/2 − w_{i+2−k}(v) otherwise, where Δ/2 = `D.halfGap` and
  w_j(v) = `D.liftWeight j v`.
* `New.Filling.besselDegree`: The product over infinite places of the degrees of the Bessel systems.
* `New.Data.logLevelTarget`: a number `λ`, built from the mean of the `log (D.weight v)`, from
  `log (M rootDisc / 2π)` and from `log b`, with `λ ≤ log N ≤ λ + √(log b)`.

modules.title: The Poincaré map as a Poincaré series of the Bessel function
modules.group: Unfolding, and the proof of the moments
modules.note:
There are a real point `g₀` and a linear form `t` for which the form `D.poincareAt g₀ t φ`, which
represents the Bessel period of `φ`, is the Poincaré series of the Bessel function; the map
`D.poincare` is defined by such a choice. Pair the series with a form `y` of the conjugate type.
Unfolding gives a sum over the classes `c` of integrals over `U_c \ G(F_∞)`. Insert the integral
formula of the Bessel function, an integral over `R(F_∞)`, and move the quotient by `U_c` to that
variable; the conjugate kernel reproduces `y`, and the sum
`∑_c ∫_{U_c \ R(F_∞)} 𝒲 (s, h_c) y (s g₀, h_c) ds` remains. The period is a multiple of the same
sum, because `[R] / J'` is the disjoint union of the `U_c \ R(F_∞)`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.Fits V l kw Y η`: the space `V` with the grading `Y` and the central element `η` fits the
  filling data `S`; it identifies the adelic group of `V` with that of `S`.
* `h.poincareSeries φ`: the series `g ↦ ∑_a φ_a ∑_{γ ∈ G(F)} h.cutBessel a (γ g)`, where `a` runs
  over the pairs `(c, i)` of a class and a coordinate, and `h.cutBessel (c, i)` is `β_c` times the
  `i`-th coordinate of the Bessel function on `G(F_∞) × h_c J` and zero elsewhere.
* `Y.besselGroup`, `Y.unipotent`, `Y.inclX`: the group `R(𝔸)`, its unipotent radical and the
  inclusion of `H(𝔸)`, the unitary group of the form on the part `𝔰.κ` of the basis;
  `Y.ratBessel` is `R(F)`, `Y.besselReal` is `R(F_∞)`, `Y.besselFin` is `R(𝔸_fin)`, and
  `Y.besselMeasure` computes integrals over `[R] = R(F) \ R(𝔸)`.
* `J = S.stdPrincipalLevel` is the principal level, and `J' = R(𝔸_fin) ∩ J`.
* `h_c = h.classPoint c`, `U_c = S.classUnipotent c`, `β_c = S.classCutoff c`: the image in
  `R(𝔸_fin)` of `c.out * η⁻¹`, with `c.out` the representative of the class `c`; the group of
  rational unipotents `u` with `h_c⁻¹ u h_c ∈ J`; and a weight at the infinite places whose
  translates under `U_c` add up to one. An integral over a quotient by `U_c` is written as an
  integral against `β_c`.
* `h.besselChar`: the character of `R(𝔸)` given by the entries at the simple roots. The hypothesis
  `hj_genericConst` is `ȷ Y.genericConst = -(M ϖ)⁻¹`, with `ȷ = WeilData.j`, `M = S.M`,
  `ϖ = S.deltaE` and `Y.genericConst` the constant of `ψ_U = Y.unipotentChar`; it makes
  `h.besselChar` equal to `ψ_U` on `U(𝔸)`.
* `Y.sourceFn t φ`: the function `𝒲 (u a) = ψ_U (u) t (ǎ_∞⁻¹ φ (a_fin))` on `R(𝔸)`, where `ǎ_∞`
  is the action `conjWeylRep` of the real component `a_∞` of `a`.
modules.literature: Unfolding a Poincaré series against an automorphic form is standard.

modules.title: Discriminants of sublattices, Siegel's lemma and a height zeta function of subspaces
modules.note:
Let `E` be a CM field containing a primitive 5040th root of unity, `𝔸f E` its finite adeles and
`Ô E` their integers. A lattice is given by an adelic basis: a matrix over `E`, embedded by
`New.Filling.finAdeleMatrix`, times a matrix over the finite adeles. Subspaces `T` of `E^κ` have
heights relative to the lattice `E^κ ∩ u Ô^κ` of a finite adelic unitary matrix `u : New.Gf E κ`.
Here `d T = New.Filling.sublatticeDiscriminant u.val.val_inv T` is the discriminant of `T ∩ u Ô^κ`;
the first argument proves `u u⁻¹ = 1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.sublatticeBasis`, `New.Filling.sublatticeDiscriminant`: a basis and the discriminant
  of the points of a subspace `V` that `H` makes integral.
* `New.Filling.siegel_lemma`: a subspace of codimension `s` is cut out by `s` short vectors.
* `New.Filling.tsum_sublatticeDiscriminant_inv_le`: an explicit bound for `∑ (d T)⁻¹ ^ (#κ + 1)`
  over the subspaces `T` of `E^κ` of codimension `s`. It follows from `New.Filling.siegel_lemma`:
  each `T` is charged to its tuple of vectors, and a packing bound sums over the lattice.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CMType E`: `E` is a CM number field (it extends `NumberField E` and `IsCMField E`) with a
  chosen complex embedding `Φ v` inducing each infinite place `v`.
* `New.IsPrimitiveMatrix O X`: `X` has entries in `O` and a left inverse with entries in `O`.
* `New.genIndex a`: the inverse of the factor by which a unit `a` scales Haar measure, `0` for a
  non-unit.
modules.literature:
Known result: Siegel's lemma over number fields (Bombieri–Vaaler). It is stated for lattices in the
genus of the standard hermitian lattice over a stably unramified CM field
(`New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`: `E` contains a primitive `5040`-th root of unity). A subspace is cut
out by lattice vectors; a power of the product of their norms is bounded by an explicit constant,
depending on the degree, the codimension and the root discriminant, times its discriminant. Source:
E. Bombieri, J. Vaaler, On Siegel's lemma, Invent. Math. 73 (1983).

modules.title: The box
modules.note:
Let `S : Filling E 𝔰` be admissible data for a CM field `E` and a shape `𝔰`, with `M = S.M` the
level and `b = S.b`. Consider the tuples of complex numbers, one for each infinite place, modulo
`M 𝓞_E`, and fix a measurable set `D` of representatives, each coordinate of each point of `D`
having modulus at most `b ^ 26`.

An archimedean point `y` is reduced if the entries above the diagonal of its triangular matrix
`S.ratTriangle y` lie in `D`. It is boxed if it is reduced and lies in the cut at every place `v`,
that is, `besselLength (y v) ≤ b ^ (6 n + 2)`, where `n = 𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `frameVector z a`: for `z` in `𝔰.G₁`, the image of the `a`-th frame vector under `z⁻¹`;
  `orthoFrame z` is the result of the Gram–Schmidt process on these vectors.
* `gramSchmidtMatrix z`: the unitriangular matrix of the coefficients of `frameVector z` in
  `orthoFrame z`; `S.ratTriangle` reads it in the rational frame.
* `besselLength z`: the infimum of `‖s * z‖ + 1` over `s` in the Bessel subgroup.
* `frameBox r`: the points at which all frame vectors have length at most `r`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_isResidueDomain`: such a set `D` exists.
* `New.Filling.boxedPoints`: the boxed points.
* `New.Filling.mul_mem_boxedPoints_iff`: invariance under the unipotent elements fixing the frame.
* `New.Filling.mem_frameBox_of_mem_boxedPoints`: at a boxed point the frame vectors have length at
  most `b ^ (37 n)`.

modules.title: Links, lifts and gauges of a term
modules.note:
The data are `S : New.Filling`, and terms are rational elements `γ` of the unitary group
`New.Filling.G`. The frame is `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `A` is the span of the `e_a` and `X₀` that of
the `x_i`. `S.frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of `f` with `γ f`, and `S.HasCellRank j γ`
says that `γ` has cell rank `j`. `New.Filling.minorNorm j γ` is the absolute norm of the leading
`j × j` minor of `S.frameProducts γ`, scaled by a power of `N` when `j = ϱ + 1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.gram_linkForm_eq_zero_of_le_link`: the link is isotropic for `S.linkForm`.
* `New.Filling.linkMetric` is a totally positive form (`New.Filling.linkMetric_posDef`), and
  `New.Filling.linkDiscSq` is the squared discriminant of a lattice for it.
* `New.Filling.HasIntegralLifts`: the predicate that the columns of an adelic matrix are images
  under `New.linkMatrix γ` of vectors of `h_c Λ₀` that are adelic combinations of rational vectors
  orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`.
* `New.Filling.paddedLeading`: the first `j` rows of a matrix, completed by rows of `1`; its
  determinant is the leading minor of order `j` (`New.Filling.det_paddedLeading`). For the matrix
  `S.frameProducts γ` its inverse gives the vectors that `f` and `γ f` share
  (`New.Filling.HasCellRank.exists_shared_frame_vector`).
* `New.Filling.latticeDisc`, `New.Filling.isotropicRowsIndex`, `New.Filling.torsionIndex`: a
  discriminant and two lattice indices. `New.submoduleIndex M M'` is the index of `M ⊓ M'` in `M'`,
  `New.colLattice` a column span.
* `New.Filling.subframeMinor`: the minor `δ_*(γ)`, nonzero for a term with a cell rank
  (`New.Filling.HasCellRank.subframeMinor_ne_zero`).
* `New.Filling.minorGauge`, `New.Filling.maxGauge`: the gauges of a term.
  `New.Filling.IsNearRepresentative` marks the kept terms, and `New.Filling.IsNearTermAt` selects
  the terms that are counted.

Notions from other files:
* `New.link`: the pairs of middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A` and
  `γ A`; `New.linkMatrix γ` is the matrix of the map that sends `t` to this pair.
* `New.framePair γ`: the matrix `(f | γ f)` of the two frames; `New.isotropicFramePair γ` is its
  part `(A | γ A)`.
* `New.Filling.Classes`: the classes `c` of a finite double coset space of `U(X₀)`; `h_c` is the
  representative of `c`, and `S.translateByClassReps c c' γ` is `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`.
* `New.Filling.classCoord`: `S.classCoord c` takes rational coordinates to coordinates in the
  basis of `h_c Λ₀`, in which the middle Gram matrix is `S.latticeMiddle`; in rational coordinates
  it is `S.ratMiddle = diag(1, -N)`, and `S.linkForm` is the form `diag(T, -T)` for this matrix `T`.
* `New.genIndex`: the generalised index `[a]` of an adele `a`; it is `0` for a non-unit.

modules.title: Frames of near terms: short shared vectors and moves between frames
modules.note:
This file proves lemmas for counting the frames `γ f` of the remaining terms `p = (c', γ)` modulo
moves. Here `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` is the standard frame, `New.frameImage γ` is the frame `γ f`, and
`Z = S.frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of `f` with `γ f`. At boxed points the frames are
uniformly independent, so the vectors shared by the two frames of a near term are short.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.IsNearTermAt.eq_of_frameImage_eq`: near terms moved by elements of
  `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀` are determined by their frames.
* `New.Filling.HasCellRank.mulVec_eStar_eq_zero_and_sum_indexX₀_le`,
  `New.Filling.col_eq_zero_of_norm_lt_one`: certain vectors have a short `X₀`-part, and a short
  vector of the lattice of `c` in `X₀` is zero.
* `New.Filling.exists_mem_classUnipotent₀_frameImage_mul_eq`: take two terms with the same integral
  `S.frameProducts`, with nonzero leading minor of order `j`, and the same shared vectors, whose
  frames agree outside the first block of rows and differ in that block by `S.frameModulus` times an
  integral matrix. Then an element of `S.classUnipotent₀ c` carries one frame to the other.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.paddedLeading`: the first j rows of Z, completed by rows of the identity matrix.
* `New.Filling.HasCellRank`: γ has cell rank j, that is, the flags of the two frames share vectors
  from the index j on (`NormOnePairOccursFrom`), the leading minor D_j of Z(γ) is nonzero, and the
  discriminant `termDisc` of γ is nonzero exactly when j = ϱ + 1.
* `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀`: the rational unipotent elements of level M for the class c that fix
  every vector of the frame.
* `New.Filling.IsNear`: γ is near if y and γ⁻¹y are both boxed points for some archimedean y.

modules.title: The covolume of the lattice of columns
modules.note:
The tuples of vectors of the lattice `Λ ∩ X₀` of a class form a lattice in the product of the
complex places. The real inner product of two of its points is an integer, so its covolume is at
least `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.columnLattice`, `New.Filling.exists_isAddFundamentalDomain_columnLattice`: the
  lattice of tuples of vectors of `Λ ∩ X₀` and its fundamental domain.

Notions from other files:

* `S : Filling E 𝔰`: the data of the filling theorem over the CM field `E` for the shape `𝔰`; the
  space `X₀` has a basis indexed by `𝔰.κ`, a set of `𝔰.k` elements.
* `c : S.Classes`: a class of the definite unitary group of `X₀`, with lattice `Λ`.
* `S.classCoordX₀ c`: the matrix that writes vectors of `X₀` in a basis of `Λ`; thus a vector lies
  in `Λ ∩ X₀` if its image under this matrix is integral.
* `Φ v`: the chosen complex embedding of `E` at the infinite place `v`.
* `Ô E`, `finAdeleMatrix q`: the integral finite adeles, and the matrix `q` over the finite adeles.

modules.title: The weight of Schur's test at one real place
modules.note:
`New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of the form `New.Shape.J₁`, which consists of `ϱ` hyperbolic
planes, a positive part `X₀` indexed by `κ` and one negative vector `z`. The frame is
`f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`, `A` is the span of the `e_a`, and `V₋` is the `-1` eigenspace of `J₁`. The
weight is a power `ν(y) ^ (-(k + i))`, `k = dim X₀`, of the ratio of the volumes of the projections
of the frames `γ f` and `f` to the negative space `y V₋`. Let norm-one pairs occur for `γ` from
level `j` and put `i = min ϱ j`. Then `ν(y)` can be computed modulo `I = A ∩ γ A`, on the subframe
`e₁, …, e_i, z`. It is bounded from below by a multiple of `det (1 + v vᴴ)`, where the columns of
`v` lie in `X₀` and move affinely when `y` is moved by a unipotent element `g` that fixes the frame.
Since `ν` for `γ` at `g y` is `ν` for `g⁻¹ γ` at `y`, the point `y` stays fixed here and `γ` is
replaced by `g⁻¹ γ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.frameCols`, `New.Shape.definiteCols`: the matrices with the vectors of the frame,
  respectively the basis of `X₀`, as columns.
* `New.realFrameGram γ`: the matrix of the products of `f` with `γ f`.
* `New.NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`: at each index from `j` on, the flags of `f` and `γ f` share a
  vector, with leading coefficients `c` and `1` for one fixed `c` of modulus `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.volumeRatio`: the ratio `ν(y)` of the two volumes.
* `New.RealPlace.IsNegativeBasis.volumeRatio_eq`: `ν(y)` in a basis of `y V₋ ∩ I^⊥`.
* `New.RealPlace.IsTriangularBasis.norm_det_mul_le_volumeRatio`: the lower bound for `ν(y)`.
* `New.RealPlace.differenceX₀_eq_add`: the dependence of `v` on the unipotent element.
* `New.RealPlace.exists_majorant_volumeRatio_inv_pow`: an integrable majorant of `ν ^ (-(k + i))`.

modules.title: Schur's test: Cauchy–Schwarz and integration in stages
modules.note:
The amplitude majorant of a term is bounded by Cauchy–Schwarz with a weight that is inverted when
the two frames are exchanged. The resulting integrals are bounded by a mean over the unipotent
elements that fix the frame. The frame is the list of basis vectors e₁, …, e_ϱ, z of the hermitian
space: one isotropic vector from each hyperbolic plane and the vector z of negative norm.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.boxCutoff`: the cutoff restricted to the set `New.Filling.boxedPoints`.
* `New.Filling.besselCutNormSq`: the squared norm of the cut Bessel function.
* `New.Filling.amplitudeMajorant_sq_le`: Cauchy–Schwarz with the weight `New.Filling.schurWeight`, a
  boxed cutoff times powers of `New.volumeRatio`, bounds the square of
  `New.Filling.amplitudeMajorant` by a product of two integrals `New.Filling.schurIntegral`.
* `New.Filling.lintegral_boxCutoff_le_of_average`: integration in stages.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.classCutoff`: the cutoff of a class at the infinite places.
* `besselU0`: the unipotent elements that fix the frame; `classUnipotent₀ c` is the group of
  rational such elements in the class `c`.

modules.title: Discriminants of lattices and sums over sublattices
modules.note:
Lattices of rational subspaces of a space with the standard hermitian form, written over `Ô`;
their discriminants; and a bound for the sum of a negative power of the index over all sublattices
of finite index.

The bound for the sum over sublattices is a consequence of Hey's formula for the zeta function of a
lattice. Here it is proved directly, by induction on the rank, over any
commutative ring whose ideals of finite index are principal.

The formula that compares the discriminant of `L ∩ W` with that of the dual lattice in `W^⊥` is
`New.Filling.jacobi_perp_discriminant`, stated for Gram determinants.

modules.title: Near terms in the filling theorem: the bound for an orbit, the tail and the open-cell term
modules.note:
This file defines the size allotted to a near orbit of terms `γ` and bounds the tail and the
open-cell term by it. The data are `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` for a shape `𝔰`, with the size hypotheses
`New.Filling.IsAdmissible`, which compare all constants with powers of the large parameter `b`.
For admissible data, if `S.termDiscNorm γ` is at least 1, then the orbit bound at the top cell
rank, with that norm as gauge, bounds the open-cell term of `γ` and, if `γ` is near, also the tail.
Here `k = |κ|`, `f` is the number of infinite places and `τ = b^(kf/4)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.cellRankSecondMoment`: the second moment D_j against which the size of a term of cell
  rank j is measured. It is the main second moment at the top cell rank and τ^(−16) = b^(−4kf) times
  the identity second moment below it.
* `New.Filling.orbitBound`: the bound allotted to a near orbit, as a function of its cell rank j and
  of its gauge x. It is τ² (D_j / (n_p (M^(2j'f) x)^k))^(1/2) with j' = min ϱ j, in units of the
  covolume ν.
* `New.Filling.IsNear.inv_pow_le_orbitBound`, `New.Filling.prod_pairingBoundSq_le`: the two bounds
  by the orbit bound at the top cell rank, for the tail and for the open-cell term.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.termDisc`: 𝗀(γ) = |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|², with D_l the leading minors of
  `New.Filling.frameProducts γ`.
* `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`, `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment`: the numbers
  sourceDim² / (besselDegree · mass), with the mass of the genus of the standard lattice, and
  sourceDim times the order of the reduced image of the Bessel subgroup `besselS`.
* `New.Filling.unipotentCovolume`: the number ν that serves as covolume of the unipotent group.
* `New.Filling.IsNear` (from `New.Spanning.Unfolding.Terms`): `γ` joins two boxed archimedean
  points.
* `New.Filling.termDiscNorm`, `New.Filling.pairCountScale` (from `New.Spanning.Unfolding.Terms`):
  the product over the infinite places of |𝗀(γ)|_v, and the number n_p = #R̄₀ n_X N^(−kf).

modules.title: The data of a term and of a pair of terms
modules.note:
The lattice `L_γ` of a term, the common lattice `L₁₂` of two terms, the gauge `𝗀*` with the factor
due to the level, the size of a term, and the terms and pairs that are counted.

We write `X₀` for the definite hermitian space with coordinates `𝔰.κ`, and `z` for the vector that
spans the rest of the middle part.

Here a term is a rational element `γ`, taken with two classes `c` and `c'`, `A` is the span of
`e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `Λ` is the lattice of the class `c`, `M = S.M` is the level and `f` is the number of
infinite places. A term in the cell `j` has `rk A / (A ∩ γ A) = min ϱ j`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.classCoordX₀ c`: the matrix of a basis of `X₀` in the coordinates of `Λ`; it is orthonormal
  for the Gram matrix `S.latticeMiddle` of the middle part of `Λ`.
* `S.translateByClassReps c c' γ`: the adelic element `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`, where `h_c` represents `c`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: `γ` lies in the cell `j ≤ ϱ + 1`; there is at most one such `j`.
* `New.link γ`: the pairs of middle coordinates (in `X₀ ⊕ E z`) of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t`
  orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`. `New.commonLink γ γ'`: the vectors `x` of `X₀` such that some pair
  `(x, y)` lies in both links, with `x` and `y` orthogonal to `z`.
* `S.maxGauge j c c' γ`: the larger of the gauge `𝗀♯` and `Nm 𝗀`, for a term in the cell `j`.

modules.title: Orthogonal lifts and the two isotropic lists of a link
modules.note:
Let `γ` have cell rank `j`, let `Λ` be the lattice of a class, `A` the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`,
`I = A ∩ γ A`, and let `z` be the last vector of the frame, of norm `-N`. This file defines
orthogonal lifts of a basis `v` of the link of `γ`. These are vectors orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`
over the columns of `(0 | v)`, whose first columns form a basis of `I`. It proves that such lifts
exist and that they are isometric to `v` for `S.linkMetric` after a correction by their products
with `z` and `γ z`. It then adjoins two vectors `z'`, `z''` of norm `N` and computes the
discriminant of the isotropic lists `(e_a, z + z')` and `(γ e_a, γ z + z'')`, `a < j`. It also
shows that `torsionIndex k` divides the index of the classes of the `e_a` and `k e_a` in the
integral vectors of their span, for finite-adelic `k`.

Notions from other files:
* `framePair γ` has the columns `e₁, …, e_ϱ, z` and their images under `γ`;
  `isotropicFramePair γ` leaves out `z` and `γ z`.
* `linkMatrix γ` sends `t` to the middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`; `link γ` is its image of
  the orthogonal complement of `A + γ A`.
* `HasCellRank j γ` says that `γ` has cell rank `j`: `NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`, the leading
  `j`-minor of the products of the two frames is nonzero, and `S.termDisc γ ≠ 0` exactly when
  `j = ϱ + 1`.
* `isotropicRowsIndex j k` is the index, among the products of `Λ ∩ A` with the frame of `k`, of
  those from the `e_a`, `a < j`; `torsionIndex k` is the index of the lattice spanned by the
  `e_a` and `k e_a` in the integral vectors of their span.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.IsOrthogonalLift`, `New.Filling.exists_orthogonal_lift`: orthogonal lifts of a basis
  of the link, and their existence for `γ` of cell rank `j`.
* `New.Filling.abs_norm_det_gram_eq_abs_norm_subframeMinor_sq`,
  `New.Filling.isotropicRowsIndex_mul_dvd_submoduleIndex`: the discriminant of the two lists, and
  a divisor of the index attached to the classes of the `e_a` and `k e_a`, `a < j`.

modules.title: The lattice of a link
modules.note:
Let `γ` be a term of cell rank `j`, `Λ` the lattice of a class, `A` the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`,
`I = A ∩ γ A`, `z` the last vector of the frame, of norm `-N`, and `M = S.M` the level of the
congruence group. The vectors of `Λ` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A` give a lattice `L¹` in the link of
`γ`, and those whose `e_a`-coordinates are divisible by `M` give the lattice `L⁺_γ`. The lattice
`L¹` is realized as an orthogonal complement: adjoin two vectors `z'`, `z''` of norm `N` to the
unimodular lattice `(Λ ∩ I^⊥)/(Λ ∩ I)` (`New.IsQuotientBasis`), and take the complement of the
isotropic lists `(e_a, z + z')` and `(γ e_a, γ z + z'')`, `a < j`.

Notions from other files:
* `linkMatrix γ` sends `t` to the middle coordinates of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`; `link γ` is its image of
  the orthogonal complement of `A + γ A`.
* `HasCellRank j γ` says that `γ` has cell rank `j`: `NormOnePairOccursFrom j γ`, the leading
  `j`-minor of the products of the two frames is nonzero, and `S.termDisc γ ≠ 0` exactly when
  `j = ϱ + 1`.
* `isotropicRowsIndex j k` is the index, among the products of `Λ ∩ A` with the frame of `k`, of
  those from the `e_a`, `a < j`; `torsionIndex k` is the index of the lattice spanned by the
  `e_a` and `k e_a` in the integral vectors of their span.
* `isotropicFramePair γ` has the columns `e₁, …, e_ϱ` and their images under `γ`.
* `New.Filling.IsOrthogonalLift` (earlier file): vectors orthogonal to `A` and `γ A` over the
  columns of `(0 | v)`, whose first columns are a basis of `I`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_lifts_linkDiscSq_le`: the discriminant of `L¹`.
* `New.Filling.exists_hasLevelLifts_linkDiscSq_le`: the discriminant of `L⁺_γ`.

modules.title: The part in `X₀` of a frame, moves, and lifts of a lattice
modules.note:
The lemmas that are used to count, round by round, the frames over a lattice `L ⊆ Λ ∩ X₀`, where `Λ`
is the lattice of a class. A move is a unipotent element of the congruence level `M` that fixes the
standard frame. For a term, `Ξ₀` consists of the first `ϱ` rows of the matrix of products, and `δ`
is the leading minor of that matrix whose order is the cell rank of the term.

Notions from other files:
* The frame is `e₁, …, e_ϱ, z`, `A` is the isotropic space spanned by the `e_i`, and `X₀` is the
  space with the indices `𝔰.κ`; `frameMiddle` takes the coordinates in `X₀ ⊕ Ez` of a frame.
* `frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of the frame with its image under `γ`.
* `translateByClassReps c c' γ` is `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`, and `γ ∈ termsOver c s c'` says that it
  stabilises the standard lattice and has the reduction `s`.
* `classCoordX₀ c` gives the coordinates of vectors of `X₀` in the lattice `Λ` of the class `c`;
  `classLatticeX₀ c` is `Λ ∩ X₀`.
* `termLattice c c' γ` consists of the vectors `v` of `Λ ∩ X₀` such that some vector of
  `v + M (Λ ∩ A)` is orthogonal to the frame of `γ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_framePartX₀_mul_eq_sub_smul`: every row `η` of vectors of `Λ ∩ X₀` gives a
  move, which subtracts `M η Ξ₀` from the part in `X₀` of a frame.
* `New.Filling.exists_isLift`, `New.Filling.exists_conjTranspose_mul_eq_of_row_mem`: if `L` lies in
  the lattice of a term, it lifts linearly to vectors orthogonal to the frame; two lifts in one
  coset of the products with vectors of `L` differ by the products with a rational row `η`.
* `New.Filling.complementLattice`: the lattice `P = Λ ∩ X₀ ∩ L^⊥`, which has the corank of `L` as
  its rank.
* `New.Filling.HasCellRank.exists_framePartX₀_sub_eq`: parts in `X₀` that are congruent modulo
  `M δ` differ by `M η Ξ₀`.

modules.title: Counting frames over a lattice of small discriminant
modules.note:
Modulo moves, few frames of near terms have a lattice `L_γ^M` that contains a given lattice `L` of
small discriminant (`New.Filling.IsFrameSet.encard_le`, and for the terms of one label
`New.Filling.encard_setOf_isNearTermAt_and_le_termLattice_le`). After the cell rank and the matrix
of products are fixed, the frames are sorted in three rounds: by the lift of `L`, by the part in
`X₀`, and by the part in the isotropic space.

Notions from other files:

* `New.frameImage γ`: the frame `γ f` of `γ`, the image of the standard frame
  `f = (e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)` of `n = ϱ + 1` vectors; `S.frameProducts γ` is the matrix of products of
  `f` with `γ f`.
* `S.classUnipotent₀ c`: the group of moves for the class `c`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: the element `γ` has cell rank `j ≤ ϱ + 1`: from the index `j` on, the flags
  of `f` and `γ f` share vectors whose two leading coefficients have the same norm, and the leading
  minor of order `j` of the matrix of products is nonzero; a further condition singles out
  `j = ϱ + 1`.
* `S.sharedVectors j γ`: the matrix whose columns `k ≥ j` are the coordinates in the isotropic
  space of the columns of `γ f · adj Y`, the others being `0`. Here `Y` consists of the first `j`
  rows of the matrix of products completed by rows of `1`; for `γ` of cell rank `j` these columns
  lie in the spans of both frames.
* `S.termLattice c c' γ`: the lattice `L_γ^M` of the `v ∈ Λ ∩ X₀` such that some vector of
  `v + M (Λ ∩ X)` is orthogonal to `γ f`, where `Λ` is the lattice of `c` and `X` is the isotropic
  space spanned by `e₁, …, e_ϱ`.
* `New.genIndex d`: the generalised index of an idele `d`, the inverse of the factor by which `d`
  scales Haar measure.

modules.title: Sums over lattices of given corank and small discriminant
modules.note:
This file bounds the sum of `(disc L) ^ (-k)` over all classes and all lattices `L ⊂ Λ ∩ X₀` of
given corank and small discriminant (`sum_discriminant_inv_le`).

Notions from other files:
* `X₀ = E ^ κ` is the hermitian space with the standard form, `k` is the cardinality of `κ`, and
  `k₀ = 𝔰.k₀` is a distinguished element of `κ`. `Gf E κ` is the finite adelic unitary group of
  `X₀`, and `stdLevel E κ` is the stabiliser of the standard lattice `Ô ^ κ` in it.
* `S.piN` is the finite idele `π̄` with `π π̄ = N`, and in the bounds `f = numInfPlaces E`.
* `S.Classes` is the set of double cosets of `Gf E κ` under the rational points and the level
  `S.sourceLevel`. If `g` is the chosen representative of the class `c`, then the lattice
  `S.classLatticeX₀ c`, also written `Λ ∩ X₀`, consists of the vectors `v` for which `g⁻¹ v` is
  integral with entry `k₀` divisible by `π̄`.
* `discriminant r L` is the square root of the generalised index `genIndex` of the Gram determinant
  of a basis of the lattice `L` of rank `r`.

modules.title: Schur's test for one orbit
modules.note:
A term is a rational point `γ` of the unitary group with
`S.translateByClassReps c c' γ = h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` integral. Its orbit is the double coset of `γ` under
the groups `New.Filling.classUnipotent₀` of unipotent elements of level `M = S.M` that fix the
frame. The amplitude majorants of the terms of an orbit are summed by Schur's test: the mean of the
sum of the weights over the orbit is reduced to a sum over a lattice, and then to the integral of a
kernel divided by the covolume of the lattice.

Throughout, `Λ` is the lattice of the class `c`, `A` is the isotropic space spanned by `e₁, …, e_ϱ`,
and `X₀` is the positive definite part of dimension `k`. For a term of cell rank `j`
(`New.Filling.HasCellRank`) put `i = min ϱ j`. The unit frame at an infinite place is the frame
rescaled by `New.Filling.basisScale`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.frameProducts γ`: the matrix of products of the frame `e₁, …, e_ϱ, z` with its image by `γ`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: in `γ` a norm-one pair occurs from `j`, its leading minor of order `j` is
  nonzero, and `S.termDisc γ` is nonzero exactly when `j = ϱ + 1`.
* `S.schurWeight c' γ i y`: the boxed cutoff of `c'` at `γ⁻¹ y` times the product over the places of
  the powers `-(k + i)` of the ratio of volumes `volumeRatio`.
* `S.tailScale`: the number `α = b ^ (k f / 4)`, where `f` is the number of infinite places.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.tsum_orbit_le_of_isLatticeTranslate`: the frames of an orbit lie in at most
  `isotropicRowsIndex ^ k` cosets of a lattice.
* `New.Filling.exists_tsum_schurWeight_le`: from cosets to the lattice.
* `New.Filling.tsum_schurIntegral_le`: from the lattice to an integral.
* `New.Filling.sq_tsum_amplitudeMajorant_doubleCoset_le`,
  `New.Filling.tsum_amplitudeMajorant_orbit_le`: the test, and its form as a bound by
  `New.Filling.orbitBound`.

modules.title: The vectors `z⁺` and `Υ_γ⁻¹ z⁺`
modules.note:
Let `γ` be an element of the unitary group, with the link isometry `Υ_γ` of the positive space
`X₀ ⊥ E z⁺`. Let `z` be the last vector of the frame and let `A` be spanned by the others.

* `New.Filling.linkVectors_mulVec_eq_zero_iff`: the orthogonal complement of `z⁺` and `Υ_γ⁻¹ z⁺`
  is `X₀^γ = X₀ ∩ Υ_γ⁻¹ X₀`.
* `New.Filling.gram_linkVectors`, `New.Filling.HasCellRank.norm_det_gram_linkVectors`: the Gram
  matrix of `z⁺` and `Υ_γ⁻¹ z⁺`, and the modulus of its determinant at each infinite place.
* `New.Filling.linkVectorPairs`: the negatives of the two vectors, as pairs in the graph of `Υ_γ`;
  there they represent the products with `z` and `γ z`
  (`New.Filling.linkVectorPairs_mul_linkMetric_mul`).

Notions from other files:
* `S.G E`: the unitary group of the form `S.ratGram` on the space with the basis `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, a
  basis of `X₀`, `z`, `e*₁, …, e*_ϱ`; the frame is `(e₁, …, e_ϱ, z)`.
* `S.positiveGram`: the Gram matrix of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺`, where `z⁺` has the norm `N = S.N`.
* `linkIsometry γ`: the isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: the term `γ` has the cell rank `j`, the order of a distinguished leading
  minor of the products of the frame with its image under `γ`.

modules.title: The orbit bound: a bound for a block of amplitudes; the second moment of a set of terms
modules.note:
Let `S : New.Filling E 𝔰` be filling data. The block `New.Filling.amplitudeSum S side T c s c'` is
the sum of the amplitudes of the rational elements of `T` that lie over the classes `c`, `c'` with
reduction `s` in `New.Filling.ResidueGL S`. The argument `side : New.FullOrCut` selects the full or
the cut Bessel functions. Write `ν` for `New.Filling.unipotentCovolume S`, the covolume of the
unipotent group of a class, `d₁` for `New.Filling.identitySecondMoment S` and `b` for the size
parameter `S.b ≥ 1`. The file defines the second moment of a family of blocks and proves that its
square root is subadditive. Its main result bounds the norm of a single block by ν times the sum of
the orbit bounds of the near orbits.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.secondMoment A Ω`: for a family of blocks `A c s c'`, the sum of the squared norms of
  the blocks with `s ∈ Ω`, divided by `ν²`.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_sub_cut_le`: the second moment of the difference between the blocks of
  `U` and those for the cut functions is at most `b⁻⁴⁰` times `identitySecondMoment`.
* `New.Filling.enorm_integral_besselKernel_le`: the bound for one term on the open cell, from the
  bound `New.BesselSystem.enorm_integral_pairKernel_cut_le` for a family of real points.
* `New.Filling.enorm_amplitudeSum_le_orbitBound_top`: the bound for a block when
  `New.Filling.termDisc` vanishes nowhere on `T`; it rests on a change of weight
  (`New.Filling.hasSum_amplitudeSum_of_cutoff`) and the bound for one term.
* `New.Filling.enorm_amplitudeSum_le_orbitBound`: one bound for a stable set of terms of one cell
  rank `j` (`New.Filling.HasCellRank`), none of cell rank `0` over the block. Terms with large
  `New.Filling.termDiscNorm` use the open cell, the others are summed by
  `New.Filling.tsum_amplitudeMajorant_orbit_le`.
* `New.Filling.enorm_amplitudeSum_le_tsum_termSize`: a cut block of a stable subset of
  `New.Filling.remainingTerms` is at most `ν` times the sum of the sizes of its near
  representatives.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: The rational γ such that h_c⁻¹ γ h_c' is integral and has reduction s,
  where h_c is the representative of the class c.
* `New.Filling.ResidueGL`: The finite group of reductions, a product of general linear groups over
  the residue fields at the chosen places.
* `New.Filling.termDisc`: The element 𝗀(γ) = |D_{ϱ+1}|² − N²|D_ϱ|² of E, formed from the last two
  leading minors of the matrix of products between the frame and its image under γ; N = S.N.
* `New.Filling.IsNear`: Some archimedean point y has both y and γ⁻¹ y among the boxed points;
  `New.Filling.IsNearRepresentative` says also that γ is the chosen element of its orbit.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: The standing hypotheses on the filling data, mostly size inequalities
  between its parameters.

modules.title: The cut: from the lattice of a link to the vectors common to two links
modules.note:
Let `A` be the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `Λ` the lattice of a class and `M` the level. The vectors of
`Λ` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A` whose part in `A` is divisible by `M` give a lattice `L⁺_γ` in the
link of a term `γ`. We descend from it to its intersection with the link of a second term `γ'`,
and from there to the part orthogonal to `z⁺` and `Υ_γ⁻¹ z⁺`, which lies in
`L_γ = S.termLattice c c' γ`. The last step costs at most a principal minor of their Gram matrix.
So the discriminant of this part, times the torsion index `S.torsionIndex`, the discriminant of
the projection to the complement of the intersection and a gain `x` from the places where the
residue meets, is at most the gauge `S.levelGauge` of the term (`nonempty_linkSplitting` below).

* `New.Filling.HasCellRank.abs_norm_minor_gram_linkVectors_mul_le`,
  `New.Filling.minorNorm_sq_le_linkDiscSq_mul`: the cost of the cut, in the three cases of rank
  `0`, `1` and `2`. The first bounds the principal minors of the Gram matrix of the two vectors;
  the second is the resulting lower bound for the discriminant of a lattice in the link on whose
  span the `z`-forms are injective.
* `New.Filling.LinkSplitting`, `New.Filling.nonempty_linkSplitting`: the splitting of a link along
  its intersection with a second link.
* `New.Filling.HasIntegralLifts.isIntMatrix_linkForm`: for two terms over one block, the form
  `S.linkForm / M` is integral on pairs of lifts.

Notions from other files:

* `New.link γ`: the space of pairs (class of `y`, class of `γ⁻¹ y`) in `(A^⊥ / A)²`, with `y`
  orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`. Here `A^⊥ / A = X₀ ⊥ E z` with `z` of norm `-N`, and the link is
  the graph of an isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺`, with `z⁺` of norm `N`.
* `New.Filling.linkDiscSq`: for a rational basis `v` and an adelic change of basis `e`,
  `S.linkDiscSq v e` is the squared discriminant of the lattice `v e` for `S.linkMetric`, which on
  the link is the form of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺`.
* `New.Filling.HasIntegralLifts`, `New.Filling.HasLevelLifts`: the columns of a matrix are the
  images in the link of vectors of `Λ` orthogonal to `A` and `γ A`, respectively lie in `L⁺_γ`.
* `New.Filling.termsOver`: `S.termsOver c s c'` is the block of rational `γ` whose matrix in the
  bases of the lattices of `c` and `c'` is integral with reduction `s`.

modules.title: The gain: a discriminant bound for the common lattice of two terms over one block
modules.note:
Take two terms `γ`, `γ'` over one block `(c, s, c')` whose `s` agrees. The square of the
discriminant of their common lattice `L₁₂` is at most the product of their values of `S.levelGauge`,
divided by a power of `M / 2` if the links differ, and by the square of the norm of the places at
which `s` meets if the links are equal and `S.termDisc` does not vanish
