(`New.Filling.pairDiscriminant_sq_le`). A block is a pair of classes `c`, `c'` with an element `s`
of the finite group `S.ResidueGL`. The element `s` agrees if the character `S.unipotentChar` takes
the same value on any two integral unipotents `u`, `u'` whose reductions satisfy `ū s = s ū'`.

The proof descends from the lattice `L⁺_γ` of each link in three steps.

* The congruence (`New.Filling.LinkSplitting.one_le_mul_linkDiscSq`): passing to the intersection of
  the two links gains a power of `M / 2`, as `γ γ'⁻¹` is `1` modulo `M` on `Λ`.
* The cut (`New.Filling.nonempty_linkSplitting`): passing to `commonLink γ γ'`, the vectors of `X₀`
  that both links send to one vector of `X₀`. This gives
  `New.Filling.torsionIndex_mul_discriminant_commonPart_le`, a bound for the parts `S.commonPart` of
  the lattices of the two terms, with the torsion indices saved.
* The index (`New.Filling.submoduleIndex_pairLattice_dvd_torsionIndex`): passing to `L₁₂` costs at
  most the torsion index of the other term.

Here `A` is the span of `e₁, …, e_ϱ`, `Λ` is the lattice of the class `c`, `M` is the level and
`L_γ = S.termLattice c c' γ`. The lattice `L⁺_γ` consists of the vectors of the link of `γ` with an
integral lift whose part in `A` is divisible by `M` (`New.Filling.HasLevelLifts`). The space `X₀`
and the line `E z` make up the middle space of the frame, and `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` is positive definite, with
`z⁺` of norm `S.N`. The torsion index of `γ` is `S.torsionIndex (S.translateByClassReps c c' γ)`.

Notions from other files:
* `link γ`: the pairs of classes in `A^⊥ / A` of `t` and `γ⁻¹ t`, for `t` orthogonal to `A + γ A`.
* `linkIsometry γ`: the isometry `Υ_γ` of `X₀ ⊥ E z⁺` that the link of `γ` determines.
* `S.termsOver c s c'`: the rational `γ` with `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` in the stabilizer of the lattice and
  reducing to `s`; this product is `S.translateByClassReps c c' γ`.
* `S.HasCellRank j γ`: `γ` has cell rank `j ≤ ϱ + 1`, the top one exactly if `S.termDisc γ ≠ 0`.
* `S.levelGauge j c c' γ`: the gauge `𝗀*` of the term, a positive real bound for discriminants.

modules.title: The sum over pairs of near terms
modules.note:
For a fixed class `c`, a pair of near terms over a block `(c, s, c')` is sorted by its label, a
component of `s` in the reduced image of the Bessel subgroup, and by its common lattice. Over a
given lattice and label there are few terms, and the sum over the lattices is bounded.

The main notions used in the statements:
* a class `c : S.Classes` is a double coset of the unitary group of the definite space `X₀` at the
  finite adeles, with representative `h_c`;
* a block is a triple `(c, s, c')`, with `s` in the finite group `S.ResidueGL`. A rational isometry
  `γ` is a term over it if `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` is integral with reduction `s`;
* `S.IsNearPairOverAgreeingBlock c c' q`: the two terms in `q` are near, are the chosen
  representatives of their double cosets, have a cell rank, and lie over one block `(c, s, c')`
  whose `s` agrees (`S.Agrees s`);
* `commonLink γ γ'`: the subspace of `X₀` that two terms have in common; its dimension is the rank
  of their common lattice `L₁₂ = S.pairLattice c c' γ γ'`, which has corank `l` if this dimension is
  `k - l`;
* `S.termLattice c c' γ`: the lattice `L_γ ⊆ Λ ∩ X₀` of a term, where `Λ` is the adelic lattice of
  the class `c` and `Λ ∩ X₀` is `S.classLatticeX₀ c`.

The main result is `New.Filling.sum_pairDiscriminant_inv_le`.

modules.title: The remaining terms: a bound for their sum
modules.note:
Size, gain and count are combined: pairs of terms that do not lie in the same link class contribute
at most `b ^ (-k f) 𝒟_id`, and pairs in the same link class gain the norm of the places at which the
block meets.

* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_le`: sets of near pairs, one for each two classes, with
  `τ ^ (l + 6) D η ^ (-k) ≤ B` contribute at most `τ B` in all. Here `l` is the corank of the common
  lattice, the gain `η` is such that `(d η)²` is at most the product of the two gauges for the
  discriminant `d` of that lattice, and `D` bounds the second moments of both cell ranks.
* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_not_inSameLinkClass_le`: pairs with different links, or with equal
  links and `𝗀 = 0`, contribute at most `b ^ (-k f) 𝒟_id`.
* `New.Filling.sum_termSize_mul_inSameLinkClass_le`: pairs with equal links and `𝗀 ≠ 0` over blocks
  that meet at places of total norm at least `z` contribute at most `(b ^ (2 f) / z) ^ k 𝒟_main`.
* `New.Filling.secondMoment_remainingTerms_le`, `New.Filling.linkSecondMoment_le_of_le_meetNorm`:
  the resulting bounds for the second moment of the remaining terms.

Here `b = S.b` is the scale, `M = S.M` the congruence level, `k = 𝔰.k` and `n = 𝔰.n` are sizes of
the shape, `f` is the number of infinite places, `τ = S.tailScale = b ^ (k f / 4)` is the number
whose powers may be lost, `𝗀 = S.termDisc`, `𝒟_id = S.identitySecondMoment` and
`𝒟_main = S.mainSecondMoment`.

Notions from other files:
* `S.cellRank γ`: the cell rank of a rational element `γ`, the index of its cell.
* `S.termsOver c s c'`: the rational elements that are integral in the position given by the classes
  `c`, `c'` and have reduction `s`; the triple `(c, s, c')` is called a block.
* `S.IsNearPairOverAgreeingBlock c c' q`: both terms of `q` are near, are the chosen elements of
  their orbits, have a cell rank, and lie over one block `(c, s, c')` whose `s` agrees
  (`S.Agrees s`).
* `S.pairDiscriminant c c' γ γ'`: the discriminant of the common lattice `L₁₂` of two terms, a
  lattice in `commonLink γ γ'`; its corank is `k - finrank E (commonLink γ γ')`.
* `S.termSize c c' γ`: the bound `τ² (D_j / (n_p G ^ k)) ^ (1 / 2)` for the orbit of `γ`, with the
  second moment `D_j = S.cellRankSecondMoment j`, the gauge `G = S.levelGauge j c c' γ` and
  `n_p = S.pairCountScale`.
modules.literature:
The second moment of the Poincaré series expands over pairs of rational elements congruent mod `M`.
Discriminant gains, lattice counts and a weighted Schur test show that degenerate terms and pairs
with different links are negligible, and that the remaining terms shrink where frames meet mod `M`,
which isolates the main term. Discarding small cells and off-diagonal terms of Petersson-type and
relative trace formulas by congruences and counts is known in the literature. Related work:
Michel–Ramakrishnan–Yang, Bessel periods on U(2,1)×U(1,1), 2023; Kowalski–Saha–Tsimerman, Local
spectral equidistribution for Siegel modular forms, 2012; Blomer, Density theorems for GL(n), 2023.

modules.title: Sieve systems over places: products, positivity and lower semicontinuity
modules.note:
An abstract sieve. A system `New.SieveSystem` over a ring `C` with a measure (a place, or a product
of places) consists of forms `J i p q`, `i ≤ n + 1`, on pairs of sequences ("heads"), each but the
last the integral of the next one over a common entry, with bounds `B₀`, `Λ`, `β`.

* `New.SieveSystem.pi`: a product of finitely many systems on `ℂ` (one for each real
  place in the application) and one more system is a system.
* `New.SieveSystem.integrable_sum_update`, `New.SieveSystem.integral_sum_update`,
  `New.SieveSystem.norm_integral_mul_sum_update_le`: sum the forms `J (i + 1)` over all pairs of
  heads from one finite family, with a common entry at position `i ≤ n`. The sum is integrable in
  the common entry, its integral is the sum of the `J i`, and its twisted integrals are bounded by
  `β` and `Λ`. `New.SieveSystem.integrable_and_integral_sum_update` collects the three.
* `New.SieveSystem.sum_nonneg`, `New.SieveSystem.lowerSemicontinuousAt_sum`: such a sum is
  nonnegative, and its real part is lower semicontinuous in a parameter `x : C` at each point where
  every head is continuous. `New.SieveSystem.sum_nonneg_and_lowerSemicontinuousAt` collects the two.
* `New.dampedPower`, `New.headWeight`: the decay in the frequency and the weights `Λ` of the heads
  at the real places.

modules.title: The orbital integral at the finite places is a Kloosterman sum
modules.note:
Let `𝖴` be the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU` over a finite place, or a product of finite
places, let `K(M)` be the principal congruence subgroup of a level `M`, and let `ψ_𝖴` be the
character of `𝖴`. The finite Bessel function `χ` is `ψ_𝖴(u)` on `u K(M)` and zero off `𝖴 K(M)`.

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.kloostermanSum`: the sum of `ψ_𝖴(u) conj ψ_𝖴(u')` over the pairs `u`, `u'`
  in `𝖴 / (𝖴 ∩ K(M))` with `u⁻¹ x u' ∈ s K(M)`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.besselOrbitalIntegral_besselVector_apply`: the entry
  `(a, b)` of the orbital integral of the finite Bessel vector at `x` is the volume of `K(M)` times
  the Kloosterman sum of `x` at `s = a b⁻¹`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of `𝔰.ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle space with
  Gram matrix `T`. The group `T.G` is its unitary group.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData ι T (m + 1)`: the data of a place. They include the level `M = F.levelUnit`
  and a basis of the middle space made of `m + 2` hyperbolic pairs and orthonormal vectors indexed
  by `ι`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData`: these data come from the lattice of vectors
  integral over `P.integers`, with conditions on the rank, the character of the place and the group.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar`: the finite Bessel function `χ`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup.besselVector`: for a group `Z` between `K(M)` and the
  integral points, the vector of the translates of `χ` by the cosets of `K(M)` in `Z`.
* `New.besselOrbitalIntegral μ W x`: the orbital integral of `W(y) ⊗ W(x⁻¹ y)^*` over `y`.

modules.title: Sums over frequencies
modules.note:
The frequencies are the elements `ν` of a totally complex number field `E`. If `E` has `f` infinite
places, the sum of `∏_v [ν]_v ^ (-3)` over any finite subset of `E` is at most `C ^ f` with
`C = 64 * 38 * e ^ 4`. At an infinite place `[ν]_v` is `(max 1 |ν|_v) ^ 2`, with `|ν|_v` the usual
absolute value, and the finite places together give the norm of the denominator of `ν`. The numbers
with a given denominator `𝔟` lie in `N 𝔟` cosets of the ring of integers, each coset is counted by
small squares, and the sum over `𝔟` is at most the value at `2` of the Dedekind zeta function.

Notions from other files:
* `Φ v`: the chosen complex embedding of `E` that induces the infinite place `v`
  (`PlaceEmbedding E`).

modules.title: One-sided Poisson summation, sums over frequencies, and the sieve over all places
modules.note:
The sieve over the infinite places of the CM field `E` and a finite set `T` of finite places, which
bounds the main term.

* `New.Filling.charOnPlaces`, `New.Filling.globalChar`: the character of the product of the
  completions at `T`, and its product with the characters at the infinite places.
* `New.Filling.sum_ratPoint_le_mul_add_integral_of_fourier_le`: one-sided Poisson summation over the
  infinite places and `T`, at rational points integral off `T`.
* `New.Filling.entryDensity`, `New.Filling.densitySum`: the sum of densities at a common next entry,
  and the sums of densities in which the first `i` entries are summed over `A`.
* `New.Filling.densitySum_succ_le_mul_densitySum_add`: each sum of densities is bounded by the one
  before plus an error, up to the constant of Poisson summation (`New.Filling.poissonConst`).
* `New.Filling.densitySum_le`: the bound after all entries are removed in turn.
* `New.Filling.sieve`: the sieve for the product of one system for each infinite place and one
  system at `T`, read at rational points (`New.Filling.ratPoint`).

Conventions: `𝔰.k` and `𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1` are parameters of the shape `𝔰`; in
`New.Filling.frequency_term_le` and `New.Filling.sum_frequencies_le`, `k` is any natural number.
`Φ v` is the chosen embedding of `E` at the infinite place `v`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling`: the data `S`, among them the size parameter `b = S.b`, the level `M = S.M`, the
  prime `N = S.N` and a generator `ϖ = S.deltaE` of the different of `E`.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses on `S`, among them `1 ≤ |S.realM v| ≤ b ^ 23`
  and `N ≤ b ^ (60 n)`.
* `New.ψf E`, written `ψ_f`: the character of the finite adeles with `ψ_f(x) = exp (2πi Tr a)` for
  any `a ∈ E` with `x - a` integral. `New.stdAddChar E` is the standard character of the adeles, and
  `New.Filling.selfDualChar` is `x ↦ ψ_f(-x / ϖ)`.
* `New.LocProd T`: the product of the completions at `T`, with integers `New.SemilocalField.O`;
  `New.evalPlaces T` and `New.ratToPlaces T` map the finite adeles and `E` to it.
* `New.integralOff T`, `New.Filling.ratIntegralOff T`: the finite adeles and the elements of `E`
  (the `T`-integers) that are integral at every finite place outside `T`.
* `New.genIndex a`, `New.denomIndex O a`: the generalised index `[O : a O]` and the denominator
  `[O : O ∩ a⁻¹ O]`.
* `New.SieveSystem`: the axioms of the sieve for a family of forms `J i` on pairs of heads, at a
  place or a product of places.
modules.literature:
A system of positive kernels, of one kind at archimedean and finite places, has each kernel the
integral of the next over a common last entry. Systems multiply over places, and one-sided Poisson
summation, entry by entry, bounds the sum over rational points by the mass times a factor near 1, up
to the constants of summation and a small error, as the main term of the second moment requires.
Inductive Fourier transforms of Kloosterman integrals and spectral large sieves losing a constant or
X^ε are known in the literature. Related work: Jacquet, Smooth transfer of Kloosterman integrals,
2003; Jacquet, Kloosterman identities over a quadratic extension, 2004; Blomer–Buttcane, Global
decomposition of GL(3) Kloosterman sums and the spectral large sieve, 2015; Deshouillers–Iwaniec,
Kloosterman sums and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms, 1982.

modules.title: The place and level of a set of primes, orbit sums and the set of entries
modules.note:
This file sets up the local theory at a finite set `T` of finite places, stable under conjugation.
It defines the projection `New.Filling.toPlaces` of the finite adelic unitary group to `T` and the
condition `New.Filling.IsIntegralOff` of being integral off `T`. It also defines the orbit sums
`New.Filling.cosetAmplitude`, the finite set `New.Filling.entrySet` of entries and the condition
`New.Filling.IsFillingData`. It shows that the product `New.LocProd T` of the completions at `T` is
a finite place that carries such a datum.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_isIntegralOff_toPlaces_eq`: every point of the unitary group at `T` is the
  projection of a finite adelic point that is integral off `T`.
* `New.Filling.exists_isFillingData`: `New.LocProd T` is a finite place (`New.Floors.IntegralPlace`)
  with a place datum satisfying `New.Filling.IsFillingData`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`, `New.Filling.principalLevel`: The group `K` of integral points of
  the finite adelic unitary group, and the kernel `K(M)` of its reduction modulo `M`;
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.congruenceSubgroup` is the group `K(M)` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.amplitude`: The integral of β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹y)^* over the infinite
  points y, with β_c the cutoff `New.Filling.classCutoff` and W the full or the cut Bessel function
  at infinity, according to the argument `side`.

modules.title: Class sums as orbit sums, and unfolding at a set of primes
modules.note:
This file links the global sums of the filling argument to the local theory at a finite set `T` of
finite places, stable under conjugation. A finite adelic point is studied through its projection
`New.Filling.toPlaces` to `T` and the condition `New.Filling.IsIntegralOff` of being integral off
`T`. This file writes a class sum as a finite sum of orbit sums over the terms in the big cell. It
compares levels, moduli and characters with those at `T`, and it counts images modulo `M` by
measures. It unfolds each orbit sum to a Kloosterman sum at `T` times an orbital integral at
infinity.

With `h_c` the representative `New.Filling.classRep c` of the class `c`,
`New.Filling.translateByClassReps c c' γ` is `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'`, `New.Filling.termsOver c s c'` the set
of rational `γ` for which it is integral of reduction `s` modulo `M`, and
`New.Floors.FloorGroups.weylElem ϱ p` the Weyl element `w_p`. `New.Filling.boundedNonzeroIntegers`
is the finite set of bounded nonzero integers that contains the nonzero leading minors of
contributing terms. `New.Filling.entrySet` is the set 𝒯 of quotients of two of its elements. The
number `New.Filling.termDisc γ` is formed from the last two leading minors of the frame products of
`γ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.exists_amplitudeSum_eq_sum_cosetAmplitude`: a class sum for the cut function is a
  finite sum over the heads with entries in the finite set `New.Filling.entrySet`. Let these entries
  be units off `T` and let all terms over `(c, s, c')` lie in the big cell. If the terms with
  `termDisc γ ≠ 0` and one link have a nonzero sum, those that contribute lie in the double cosets
  of the `w_p σ` for one `σ`. These cosets carry the orbit sums `New.Filling.cosetAmplitude`, over
  the `u γ u'⁻¹` with `u`, `u'` in the unipotent group `New.Shape.Form.besselU`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.card_reducedImage_mul_measure_congruenceSubgroup_eq`: let `B` be a
  subgroup of the finite adelic group and `μ` an s-finite measure at `T`, carried by the projections
  of elements of `B` integral off `T` and right invariant under the projections of `B`. Then the
  order of the image of `B ∩ K` modulo `M` times `μ K(M)` is the `μ`-measure of the integral points.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.cosetAmplitude_eq_kloostermanSum_smul`: for `γ = w_p σ` with
  `σ ∈ floorGroup ϱ`, and with `h_c⁻¹ γ h_c'` and the inverses of the entries of `p` integral off
  `T`, the orbit sum is a Kloosterman sum at `T` times an orbital integral at infinity. Each double
  coset unfolds to one integral, the double cosets correspond to the pairs in the Kloosterman sum,
  and the values of the extended Bessel character are its terms.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.scaledOrbitalIntegral_smul_eq_cosetAmplitude`: so the orbit sum times
  `headDensity` and the mass of `K(M)` is an entry of the integral at `T` times the integral at
  infinity.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`, `New.Filling.principalLevel`: The group `K` of integral points of
  the finite adelic unitary group, and the kernel `K(M)` of its reduction modulo `M`;
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.congruenceSubgroup` is the group `K(M)` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.amplitude`: The integral of β_c(y) β_c'(γ⁻¹y) W(y) ⊗ W(γ⁻¹y)^* over the infinite
  points y, with β_c the cutoff `New.Filling.classCutoff` and W the full or the cut Bessel function
  at infinity, according to the argument `side`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar`: The finite Bessel function, a character of u on u
  K(M) for u in 𝖴 = `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, and 0 off 𝖴 K(M).
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData` (in `New.Spanning.MainTerm.FillingLevel`): the place data at `T` is
  large lattice data for the chosen place structure, with modulus the component of `M` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.cosetAmplitude` (in `New.Spanning.MainTerm.FillingLevel`): the sum of the amplitudes
  of the `u γ u'⁻¹` over the pairs of rational points of 𝖴 for which it is a term over `(c, s, c')`.

modules.title: Siegel's formula as an upper bound, and domination of class sums by the density at the last entry
modules.note:
Finite-place estimate of the filling theorem: global sums are bounded by integrals over the product
of the completions at a finite set `T` of places, stable under conjugation.

* `New.Filling.adelicFrequency`, `New.Filling.localFrequency`: passage between skew-adjoint
  frequencies at `T` and self-adjoint finite adeles, through multiplication by `-ϖ⁻¹` and `-ϖ`,
  where `ϖ = S.deltaE` generates the different.
* `New.Filling.normDensity_indicator_eq_mul`: the density of a test function that is `Ψ` at `T` and
  the indicator of the lattice off `T` splits into an integral of Gauss sums of the lattice and the
  density of `Ψ` at `T`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.enorm_normDensity_le_mul_lintegral_normFiberMeasure`: this density is
  at most `1 + b⁻⁶` times the volume of the lattice times the integral of `Ψ` over the sphere of `β`
  at `T`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.siegel_sum_le_lintegral_sphere`: Siegel's formula bounds the sum of a
  step function over rational points with last entry `t` by a constant times its integral over the
  sphere of `t`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_step_sum_fiberPairing`: for any matrix `R`, the positive part of
  the real part of the sum of the fiber pairings against `R` is, on the top quadric, the restriction
  of a compactly supported invariant step function.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.sum_mul_norm_sum_cosetAmplitude_sq_le_lastEntryDensity`: the squared
  norms of class sums with one last entry `t` are bounded by `(1 + b⁻⁶) * S.scaledSiegelConst` times
  archimedean densities and densities at `T`, divided by the normalized mass.

The `IsFillingData` results assume `S` admissible, `S.ideleM⁻¹` integral off `T` and `F` filling
data. Conventions: `Φ v` is the embedding of the CM type at `v`. The last entry of `γ` is the
product of the last frame vector with its image under `γ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace`: A structure on `LocProd T`, the product of the completions at `T`: an
  open compact self-dual subring `R` of volume one, a character `ψ`, a trace-one element `τ`, a skew
  unit and the modulus `modulus`.
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: The standing hypotheses: `sourceLevel` is the preimage of K(M),
  `reduction` is onto, and size inequalities hold between b and ϖ, κ_v, N, `besselDegree`, the
  second moments, the number of Bessel coordinates, an index and the mass.
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`: The group `K` of integral points of the finite adelic unitary
  group; `New.Floors.PlaceData.congruenceSubgroup` is the group `K(M)` at `T`, the kernel of
  reduction modulo `M`.

modules.title: The sieve system at the finite places
modules.note:
The finite half of the input of the sieve `New.Filling.sieve`.

* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_sieveSystem`: read the completions at a finite
  set `T` of places as one ring `LocProd T`. There is a subgroup `Z` of the unitary group over it
  that contains the components at `T` of the integral elements fixing given vectors at a set `Sg` of
  chosen places, and for which the forms `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorForm` and the density
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.lastEntryDensity`, divided by `Z.massRatio`, satisfy `New.SieveSystem`.

The subgroup is that of `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_norm_floorForm_div_le`,
which bounds the form of floor `0`: it saves the power `b ^ (6 * 𝔰.k)` of the base `b` of the
filling for each place in a given set `Sg` of chosen places.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: the standing hypotheses on the level and the sizes of a filling `S`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData`: `F` is a large lattice datum over `LocProd T`, its modulus
  `g = F.levelUnit` is the component at `T` of `S.ideleM` (the product `S.M` of the two level primes
  as a finite idele), and the character is that of `S` at `T`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.massIntegral`: `ϰ(Z) = ∫ |∫_Z phase(y x y⁻¹) dy| ^ 2 dx`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup.massRatio`: `vol(Z) vol(K(g)) / unipotentMass ^ 2`, where
  `vol` is `New.Floors.PlaceData.groupMeasure` and `Z` lies between `K(g)` and the integral points.
* `New.SieveSystem`: the recursion, positivity, continuity and bounds that the sieve asks of a
  family of forms at a place.

modules.title: Main-term bound for the second moment over open reductions fixing given vectors
modules.note:
This file proves the main-term estimate of the filling theorem. The subgroup
`New.Filling.fixer Sg D` consists of the reductions s that fix the given vectors `D w` modulo w or
its conjugate, at the chosen places `w ∈ Sg` above the first prime. It shows that every term over an
open reduction lies in the big cell. It then proves Siegel's step and uses it to bound the sum over
the open reductions that fix the vectors at `Sg`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.mul_sum_norm_sum_cosetAmplitude_sq_le`: Siegel's step, which bounds the
  squared norms of finitely many class sums by densities at finite places weighted by the local
  bounds.
* `New.Filling.sum_norm_sum_cosetAmplitude_sq_le`: the estimate for finitely many distinct classes
  whose reductions fix the vectors at `Sg`. The bound is (1 + b⁻⁴) b^(−6 𝔰.k |Sg|) times the main
  second moment times `unipotentCovolume`².
* `New.Filling.linkSecondMoment_isOpenElement_le`: the squared norms of the class sums of the cut
  function add up to at most the same bound. The sum runs over all links, pairs of classes and
  reductions s that are open and fix the vectors at `Sg`; only terms with `termDisc γ ≠ 0` enter.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling.IsAdmissible`: The standing hypotheses: `sourceLevel` is the preimage of K(M),
  `reduction` is onto, and size inequalities hold between b, M and ϖ, κ_v, N, the constant
  `scaledSiegelConst`, the second moments, the number of Bessel coordinates and an index.
* `New.Filling.mainSecondMoment`: The real number `sourceDim`² / (`besselDegree` · mass), with the
  mass `New.mass` of the genus of the standard lattice of rank dim V.
* `New.Filling.termsOver` c s c': The terms over (c, s, c'): rational γ such that h_c⁻¹ γ h_c' lies
  in the stabiliser K of the lattice and has reduction s.
modules.literature:
In the unfolded second moment of the Poincaré series, the summed main terms are dominated by the
quadratic form of a positive kernel of local Bessel (orbital) integrals at a finite set of primes,
with a constant close to one. With the sieve this bounds the main term above. Kloosterman sums as
local orbital integrals, normal forms for Bessel double cosets and Siegel's formula are known in the
literature. Related work: Jacquet–Ye, Germs of Kloosterman integrals for GL(3), 1999; Y. Liu,
Relative trace formulae toward Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods, 2014; Siegel, Über die analytische
Theorie der quadratischen Formen, 1935.

modules.title: The share of non-allowed polynomials and the bad share
modules.note:
This file bounds the share of the bad types for tuples of polynomials over fields with q elements.
A label is a monic squarefree polynomial of degree `r` that does not vanish at `0`. The file
counts the monic polynomials that are not allowed and the primitive polynomials. It then bounds
the coefficient at the identity of one minus the sum of the idempotents of the good tuples.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.card_not_primitive_mul_le`: for `1 < r < q`, with every polynomial weighted by
  `(1 - r / q) / q ^ r`, the monic polynomials of degree `r` that are not primitive polynomials
  weigh at most `exp (-1 / (2 r (2 r log q + 1)))` in total.
* `New.re_coeff_one_sub_sum_tupleIdem_le`: the bound on the coefficient at the identity of one minus
  the sum of the idempotents of the good tuples.

Notions from other files:
* `New.tupleIdem`: For a tuple (c_w) of polynomials over the fields k_w, the tensor product of the
  polynomial idempotents e_{c_w} in the group algebra of ∏ GL_n(k_w).
modules.literature:
In the regular representation of a product of groups GL_r(F_q), types that are not good have share
at most a multiple of 1/q per factor plus a term decaying exponentially in the number of factors. So
the projection to good types discards little when translates of the Poincaré series fill the rows.
It computes the Plancherel shares for GL_r(F_q) from Green's degree formula and counts of squarefree
and primitive polynomials over F_q, followed by a union bound over the factors. Related work: Green,
The characters of the finite general linear groups, 1955; Dudko, Plancherel measures for GL(n,q),
arXiv 0806.1345, 2008; Lidl–Niederreiter, Finite Fields, ch. 3, 1983.

modules.title: Sizes, lengths and balanced frames
modules.note:
A filtration `ofSize i` of the ring `A` measures numbers, vectors and matrices on one scale L. It
gives the length of a vector at a point `g` of the unitary group, the induced length on the quotient
Y^(l) along the frame, and balanced frame vectors.

Letters used in this folder: G^(l) = `floorGroup l`, R^(l) = `partialUnitriangularGroup l`,
U_(<l) = `unipotentBelow l`; Y^(l) is the quotient of the vectors orthogonal to the e_b, b < l, by
their span; for a place datum `F` (`New.Floors.PlaceData`), K = `F.boxSet` is its compact set and
M = `F.levelUnit` its modulus; for a gauge `Γ` (`New.Floors.Gauge`), Λ = `Γ.loss` is its constant.

## Guide to this folder

The files of this folder bound the local densities of pairs of frames, at a real place and over the
ring of all finite places of a finite set. Steps 3 to 6 rest on the gains of step 13, which steps 7
to 12 prepare.

1. Gauges, lengths of vectors and balanced frames. `New.Floors.Gauge`, `New.Floors.Size.LengthLeAt`,
   `New.Floors.Size.IsBalanced`.
2. A density is an integral over a position and two frames. `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorForm`,
   `New.Floors.Gauge.integral_psi_mul_floorForm_succ`,
   `New.Floors.Gauge.inner_besselOrbitalIntegral`.
3. The positions are cut into shells by their height; a few factors of the gain pay for the sum over
   the shells. `New.Floors.Gauge.IsShell`, `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_le_of_shells`.
4. The finite places, taken together: the decay in the frequency and the mass on the congruence
   subgroup. `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.enorm_floorForm_le`,
   `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.massIntegral_le_main_add_error`.
5. The gain in the mass from the fixed vectors, and the resulting system.
   `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_places`,
   `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_sieveSystem`.
6. The mass at a real place, against the uncut Bessel function.
   `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.norm_floorForm_zero_le`.
7. Plancherel's formula on a quadric, for the pivots and for the vectors after them.
   `New.Floors.Gauge.fourierSqNormLe_floorQuadricMeasure`, `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_section_le`,
   `New.Floors.Gauge.parseval_heisenbergMeasure_le`.
8. Depth, and a subspace of large rank that looks the same from both points.
   `New.Floors.PlaceData.depth`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.depthWeight`,
   `New.Floors.PlaceData.commonVectors`.
9. Deep vectors are rare, and long coordinates force depth.
   `New.Floors.Gauge.floorMassLe_depth_pow`,
   `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_heisenbergMeasure_inv_depth_le`.
10. A position of large height has a deep vector after the head.
    `New.Floors.Gauge.hasMatrixSize_sub_one_of_stableProducts`,
    `New.Floors.Gauge.exists_unit_mem_stableProducts_of_isHead`.
11. One frame, along the Heisenberg groups. `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_weightedSquareIntegral_le`.
12. A weight made of depths separates the two frames.
    `New.Floors.Gauge.sq_lintegral_le_mul_lintegral`,
    `New.Floors.Gauge.sq_lintegral_mul_comp_weylElem_inv_le_of_section`.
13. The gains at one position: a frequency, two heads, a deep vector.
    `New.Floors.Gauge.formIntegrandL1Norm_sq_le_of_char`,
    `New.Floors.Gauge.formIntegrandL1Norm_sq_le_of_heads`,
    `New.Floors.Gauge.formMajorant_sq_le_of_hasDeepVector`.

The equation of a quadric is solved in a block of orthonormal coordinates, in the same way at both
kinds of place (`New.Floors.Place.IsSolvedIn`, `New.Floors.Gauge.exists_blockKernel`). Both pivots
are first moved into one space; their equations are solved in two disjoint blocks, and Plancherel's
formula acts on the orthonormal coordinates off both blocks.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Size`, `New.Floors.Size.vecsOfSize`, `New.Floors.Size.HasMatrixSize`: sizes of
  numbers, vectors and matrices.
* `New.Floors.weylRatio`, `New.Floors.coe_weylRatio`: the quotient of two Weyl elements is diagonal.
* `New.Floors.IsOrthogonalBelow`, `New.Floors.CongrBelow`: the vectors of Y^(l) and their lifts.
* `New.Floors.Size.LengthLeAt`, `New.Floors.Size.InducedLengthLe`, `New.Floors.Size.IsBalanced`:
  lengths at a point, induced lengths, balanced vectors.
* `New.Floors.Size.GaugesDifferLe`, `New.Floors.Size.HasShortDual`, `New.Floors.Size.IsHead`: the
  notions compared in `New.Spanning.Frames.TwoGauges`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.BesselIndex`: the index set of the basis e_a, x_i, z, e*_a (a < ϱ) of V; the x_i and z
  form the middle block.
* `New.Shape.Form.splitGram`: the Gram matrix of ϱ hyperbolic planes and a middle space with Gram
  matrix `T`; `New.Floors.IsHermitianUnit` says that it is hermitian and invertible, and `T.G` is
  its unitary group.
* `New.BesselIndex.level`, `New.Floors.FloorGroups.floorOf`: e_a has level `a`, the middle block
  level `ϱ`, e*_a level `2ϱ - a`; both e_a and e*_a have floor `a`, z has floor `ϱ` and the x_i have
  floor `ϱ + 1`.
* `New.Shape.Form.partialUnitriangularGroup`: the group R^(l), for l ≤ ϱ + 1 unitriangular on the
  first l vectors of the frame (e_0, …, e_(ϱ-1), e_ϱ = z).
* `New.Shape.Form.unipotentBelow`: the group U_(<l) of the isometries that are unitriangular when
  the basis vectors of floor at least l are all given the middle level `ϱ`.

modules.title: Comparing the lengths at two points; minors and heads
modules.note:
Each isometry g of the form `T.splitGram` gives a gauge, the size of g⁻¹ y, on vectors y. The
gauges at two points differ little on Y^(l-1) if they differ little on Y^(l), the frame vector
e_(l-1) has short lifts at both points, and it has a short dual that looks nearly the same from both
points. Over a head, such duals come from determinants of blocks of the isometries (Cramer's rule).

Notions from other files:
* `S.ofSize i`, `S.vecsOfSize i`, `S.HasMatrixSize i`: the numbers x of size i (|x| ≤ L^i at a real
  place, L^i x integral at the finite places, for a fixed scale L), and the vectors and matrices all
  of whose entries have size i.
* Y^(l): the vectors orthogonal to e_0, …, e_(l-1) (`IsOrthogonalBelow l`) modulo the span of these
  (`CongrBelow l`). The basis vectors e_a and e*_a have the indices `inl a` and `eStar a`.
* `S.GaugesDifferLe r g g' l t`: for each ω orthogonal to e_0, …, e_(l-1) with g⁻¹ ω of size i, the
  class of ω in Y^(l) has a lift ω' such that (g⁻¹ ω - g'⁻¹ ω') / r has size i + t.
* R^(l) = `partialUnitriangularGroup l`: the isometries that change each frame vector of index below
  l by a combination of the earlier ones. U_(<l) = `unipotentBelow l`: the isometries that are
  unitriangular when all basis vectors other than e_a, e*_a (a < l) are put on one middle level.
* `S.IsHead j p`: the inverses of the products p₀ ⋯ p_(l-1), l ≤ j, have size 1. The Weyl element
  w_p = `weylElem j p` sends e_a to p_a e*_a for a < j.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Size.GaugesDifferLe.of_succ`,
  `New.Floors.Size.GaugesDifferLe.on_whole_space_of_hasShortDual`: the recursion down the quotients.
* `New.Floors.Size.GaugesDifferLe.hasMatrixSize_sub_one`: a bound on the whole space bounds the
  matrix `(x - 1) / r`.
* `New.Floors.Size.leadingMinor_mem_ofSize`, `New.Floors.Size.head_products_mem_ofSize`: the leading
  minors have bounded size.
* `New.Floors.Size.dual_mem_vecsOfSize`, `New.Floors.Size.hasMatrixSize_of_isHead`: short duals over
  a head, and bounds for the sizes of g and w_p⁻¹ g.

modules.title: Place data, floor measures and depth
modules.note:
A place datum `F` fixes a unit M, a compact set K and a basis adapted to the frame. The group
measure is built floor by floor: floor `l ≤ ϱ` chooses the frame vector f_l on its quadric and an
element of the Heisenberg group along it, and floor ϱ + 1 carries the measure of H. The letters
Y^(l), K and M are those of the head of `New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`.

Notions from other files:
* G = `T.G` is the unitary group of `T.splitGram`, a hermitian form with ϱ = `𝔰.ϱ` hyperbolic pairs
  e_a, e*_a; its basis vectors are indexed by `𝔰.BesselIndex`, and n = `𝔰.n` is ϱ + 1.
* G^(l) = `floorGroup l` is the group of isometries that fix the basis vectors of floor below l;
  H = `besselH` is G^(ϱ+1).
* R^(l) = `partialUnitriangularGroup l` is the group of isometries that are unitriangular on the
  first l frame vectors, and U = `besselU` is the Bessel unipotent group.
* `orbitPoint b g` is the vector g⁻¹ f_b, where f_b is the frame vector of floor b, and
  `F.floorQuadricMeasure b` is the measure on the quadric through f_b.
* η_l = `heisenbergMeasure l` is the measure of the Heisenberg group of floor l, and `weylLaw l` is
  a measure carried by the inverse Weyl elements of floor l.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.PlaceData`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorMeasure`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.groupMeasure`:
  the data and the measures.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsNear`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsStable`,
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.stableProducts`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.depth`,
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.depthWeight`: points near K, stable vectors, their products with e_a, depth
  and the weight.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.measurePreserving_orbitPoint`: a floor measure maps to the measure of the
  quadric.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.partialGroupMeasure_mconv_dirac`,
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.lintegral_partialGroupMeasure_weylElem_inv_mul`: invariance on the right,
  and invariance under a Weyl element on the left for the lower floors, for integrals of functions
  fixed on the left by G^(j), when the group measure is Haar.

modules.title: The scale, near points and partial correlations
modules.note:
The structure `New.Floors.Gauge` collects the few facts about a place that the estimates use. A
correlation is a kernel on pairs of points with a character law; integrating it over the floors from
`l` on gives the partial correlations. The letters G^(l), R^(l), U_(<l) are those of the head of
`New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`, and K, M those of `New.Spanning.Frames.Levels`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Gauge`, `New.Floors.Gauge.positionsOfSize`: a scale with its constant Λ =
  `Γ.loss`, and the close positions.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsPairingKernel`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.partialCorrelation`: kernels and
  partial correlations.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.weightedSquare`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.weightedSquareIntegral`: the second
  moments of one frame.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.isBalanced_of_isNear`: near points are balanced.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.PlaceData`: the data of a place, among them the level M = `F.levelUnit`, the compact
  set K = `F.boxSet` of the unitary group G = `T.G`, and the set `F.positions` of the elements by
  which the second point of a pair differs from the first.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsNear`: g is near at j if R^(j) g meets K, for R^(j) =
  `partialUnitriangularGroup j`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorMeasure`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.quotientMeasureFrom`: the measure of
  floor l on G^(l) = `floorGroup l`, and the convolution of the measures of the floors from l on.
* `New.Floors.Size`: a filtration `ofSize i` of the numbers by size; a vector or a matrix has size i
  if all its entries have.

modules.title: Volumes on quadrics and on sections
modules.note:
The equation of a quadric is solved in a block of orthonormal coordinates: the other coordinates
are free, and the points of size j of the fibres have mass bounded in terms of j. A section
⟨e_a, y⟩ = c of an isotropic cone, for a unit c, is an orbit of a Heisenberg group. The letters
G^(l), U_(<l) and Y^(l) are those of the head of `New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Gauge.exists_isSolvedIn`: the quadric of a floor is solved in a block.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.setLIntegral_orthonormalPart_le`: integrals of functions of the orthonormal
  coordinates.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_heisenbergMeasure_le`: integrals over a Heisenberg group.
* `New.Floors.sectionPoint`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.lintegral_floorQuadricMeasure_eq`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.setLIntegral_sectionMeasure_le`: sections and their measures.

Notions from other files:

* `Γ.ofSize j`, `Γ.vecsOfSize j`: the numbers of size j and the vectors whose entries have size j.
  The powers of the number `Γ.loss` bound moduli |u| = `modulus u` and volumes.
* `F.floorBasis b`: a basis of V_b, the span of the basis vectors of floor at least b (a space of
  representatives of Y^(b)), made of hyperbolic pairs and orthonormal vectors indexed by ι. The
  orthonormal vectors whose index lies in the range of `F.freeIndex : F.FreeIndex → ι` span X'.
* `IsSolvedIn blk ρ S B`: the measure ρ is the volume in the coordinates off the block `blk` times
  measures in the block, each of mass at most B on the vectors with coordinates in S.
* `heisenbergElem a (ω, β)`: the element of the Heisenberg group of floor a with vector part ω and
  skew part β.
* `CongrBelow l ω ω'`: the vectors ω and ω' differ by a combination of the e_b with b < l.

modules.title: Plancherel's formula on quadrics
modules.note:
Cauchy–Schwarz in the fibres and Plancherel's formula in the orthonormal coordinates bound a Fourier
kernel between two quadrics. Along a Heisenberg group a partial correlation is a Fourier transform
in the next frame vector. The letters G^(l), R^(l), U_(<l), Y^(l) are those of the head of
`New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`, and K, M those of `New.Spanning.Frames.Levels`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Gauge.fourierSqNormLe_floorQuadricMeasure`: the kernel from the quadric of a floor to
  the same quadric or to the whole floor, by solving in two disjoint blocks.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.partialCorrelation_heisenbergElem_eq_integral`: the correlation along a
  Heisenberg group.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.parseval_heisenbergMeasure_le`: Parseval's inequality along a Heisenberg group.

Notions from other files:
* `F.partialCorrelation l k g y`: the correlation from floor l on, an integral of k(σ g, σ y).
* `F.IsPairingKernel l k d`: the rules obeyed by an orbital integral twisted by d.
* `orbitPoint b σ`: the vector σ⁻¹ f_b, for the b-th frame vector f_b; its law on floor b is
  `F.floorQuadricMeasure b`.
* `Γ.vecsOfSize i`, `Γ.HasMatrixSize i`: vectors and matrices all of whose entries have size i.
* `FourierSqNormLe`: a bound for the kernel ψ(ξ ⟨v, y⟩) on square norms.

modules.title: Depth
modules.note:
For a fixed position few frame vectors are deep, and for a fixed frame vector few translates of the
position leave it shallow. Both are read on vectors that look the same from the two points. A
position far from 1 has a deep vector, and a head keeps the first vectors shallow. The letters
G^(l), R^(l), U_(<l), Y^(l) are those of the head of `New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`, and K, M those
of `New.Spanning.Frames.Levels`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsCommonBound.depth_le`, `New.Floors.Gauge.floorMassLe_depth_pow`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_depth_pow_section_le`: deep vectors are rare, also on a section.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.exists_lift_of_mem_closeBelow`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_heisenbergMeasure_inv_depth_le`: long coordinates force depth.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_invDepthWeight_le`, `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_depthWeight_le`: the
  two halves of the weight over all floors of a head.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.hasMatrixSize_sub_one_of_stableProducts`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.exists_unit_mem_stableProducts_of_isHead`: bounded depths bound the position;
  under a head, each 𝔡_a with a < j contains a unit with bounded inverse.

Notions from other files:
* `F.IsStable l g g' ω`: ω is orthogonal to the e_b, b < l, and (g⁻¹ ω, g'⁻¹ ω') lies in
  `F.closePairs` for some ω' congruent to ω modulo these e_b.
* `F.stableProducts a x y`: the set 𝔡_a of the products ⟨e_a, ω⟩ with the ω stable at x and x y.
* `F.depth a x y`: the inverse of the volume of 𝔡_a.
* `F.depthWeight j x y`: the product over a < j of the depth^(-s), s = `F.volumeExponent`.
* `F.IsNear j g`: ξ g lies in the box `F.boxSet` for some ξ in `partialUnitriangularGroup j`.

modules.title: The densities as integrals over pairs of frames
modules.note:
For a cut Bessel function `W` and two heads (sequences of units `p`, `q`), the form of floor `j` is
a density times an integral, over a position `x` and two frames, of a weighted product of two
correlations. The file defines these forms and their majorants, and proves the descent from one
floor to the next.

Notions from other files:
* `F : PlaceData ι T m` is the data of a place: the measures of the floors, the level `F.levelUnit`
  and the compact set `F.boxSet` (the box) of the unitary group `T.G`; a `Gauge F` is a notion of
  size with a number Λ = `Γ.loss` whose powers bound moduli and volumes.
* G^(l) = `floorGroup l` and R^(l) = `partialUnitriangularGroup l` are the subgroups described in
  `New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`, and 𝖴 = `T.besselU` is the Bessel unipotent group. A point `g` is
  near at `j` (`F.IsNear j g`) if R^(j) g meets the box.
* θ_j = `F.floorMeasure j` is the measure of floor `j`, 𝗆_j = `F.partialGroupMeasure 0 j` the
  convolution of the Heisenberg and floor measures of the floors below `j`, and 𝖬 = `F.groupMeasure`
  that of all floors.
* `F.partialCorrelation j k g y` is the correlation from floor `j` on, the integral of
  `k (σ g) (σ y)` against `F.quotientMeasureFrom j`, the convolution of the θ_l with l ≥ j.
* w_p = `weylElem j p` is the Weyl element of the first `j` hyperbolic pairs with the entries `p a`,
  and `weylRatio j p q` is the diagonal element w_q⁻¹ w_p.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsCut`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorForm`,
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.formIntegrandL1Norm`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.formMajorant`: the forms and
  their majorants.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.inner_besselOrbitalIntegral`: the product of two orbital integrals as a double
  integral.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.isPairingKernel_frameCorrelation`: the rules for correlations.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorForm_zero_eq_integral`: the mass: the form of floor 0 is the integral
  of a square.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.integral_weight_mul_floorForm_succ`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.integral_psi_mul_floorForm_succ`: descent from one floor to the next.

modules.title: One frame
modules.note:
After Cauchy–Schwarz each frame is paired with itself. The square of a partial correlation is
integrated over the position ball along the Heisenberg groups of the frame: a step below the pivot
uses up a weight, a step above it adds a vector by Parseval's formula. The letters G^(l), R^(l),
U_(<l), Y^(l) are those of the head of `New.Spanning.Frames.Lengths`, and K, M those of
`New.Spanning.Frames.Levels`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsPairingKernel.pivotL1Norm_sq_le`: Cauchy–Schwarz for a pivot whose range
  has small mass.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_cutSquare_le`: one step above the pivot.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_weightedSquare_le`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_weightedSquareIntegral_le`: the bound for one frame.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.headDensity_mul_lintegral_le_mul_pairingNormSq`: a gain on the position ball
  survives the integration.

Notions from other files:
* `F.floorMeasure l`, written θ_l: the measure of floor l, carried by G^(l) = `floorGroup l`;
  `descConv F.floorMeasure l i` is the convolution θ_{l+i−1} ∗ ⋯ ∗ θ_l.
* `F.IsPairingKernel j k d`: the rules of a correlation k(g, y) = ⟪W g, W (d y)⟫ of a Bessel
  function W, where d commutes with G^(j); `F.partialCorrelation l k`, written k_l, is the average
  of k over the floors from l on.
* `F.depthWeight l g x`, written ℘_l(g, gx): the product of negative powers of the depths of the
  first l frame vectors; `F.weightedSquare l k x g` is ℘_l(g, gx)·|k_{l+1}(g, gx)|².
* `F.weightedSquareSum k x l`, written 𝖻_l: the sum of the integrated weighted squares over the
  floors from l on; `F.weightedSquareIntegral l k x` is its integral over the floors below l.
* `F.IsNear l g`: the coset R^(l) g meets `F.boxSet`, where R^(l) = `partialUnitriangularGroup l`.

modules.title: Two frames: separation and the gains at one position
modules.note:
A weight made of depths separates the two frames. At a fixed position the form then gains from a
frequency, from two different heads, or from a deep vector. Throughout, θ_l is `F.floorMeasure l`,
and w_p is the Weyl element `weylElem j p` of a head `p` of length `j`.

Notions from other files:
* `PlaceData.IsNear`: `g` is near at `j` if `partialUnitriangularGroup j` moves it into the box
  `F.boxSet`.
* `PlaceData.partialCorrelation`, `PlaceData.pivotL1Norm`: the correlation of a kernel from floor
  `j` on, and the integral over floor `j` (the pivot) of the modulus of the correlation from floor
  `j + 1` on.
* `PlaceData.depthWeight`, `PlaceData.weightedSquareSum`: the product of the powers depth^(-s) over
  the first `j` vectors, and the sum over the floors from `j` on of the weighted squared
  correlations.
* `Gauge.weightedSquareProduct`: the product of the second moments `F.weightedSquareIntegral` of the
  two correlations, times a constant that depends on the gauge and on the head `p`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.Gauge.sq_lintegral_le_mul_lintegral`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.sq_lintegral_mul_comp_weylElem_inv_le_of_section`: separating the frames, also
  with a pivot on a section.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.formIntegrandL1Norm_sq_le_of_char`: the gain from a frequency.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.partialCorrelation_mul_eq_integral_sectionPoint`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.formIntegrandL1Norm_sq_le_of_heads`: the phase of the lifts and the gain from
  two heads.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsPairingKernel.pivotL1Norm_le_sum_deepModulus`: the cut at the first deep
  vector.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.pivotL1Norm_sq_le_of_deep`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.formMajorant_sq_le_of_hasDeepVector`,
  `New.Floors.Gauge.formMajorant_zero_sq_le_of_hasDeepVector`: the gains from a deep vector.

modules.title: The sum over the shells
modules.note:
The positions are cut into shells by their height. On one shell the bound for one frame loses a
power of the height. Below a threshold this loss is affordable. Above it every position has a deep
vector, whose gain pays for the loss. The argument is the same at a real place and at the finite
places; the shells that are summed have the powers of 2 as heights.

Notions from other files:
* A `PlaceData` `F` at the place is its data: a unit `F.levelUnit`, the positions, a compact box and
  measures.
* A gauge `Γ` is a notion of size at the place, with a scale `Γ.loss ≥ 2` that bounds volumes.
* `F.formMajorant` is the integral of the moduli of the two correlations of `W` at a position, and
  `Γ.weightedSquareProduct` is the product of their second moments, with a constant.
* `F.FloorMassLe j V 1` says that the mass of floor `j` near the next floor is at most `V`.

Contents of this file:
* `New.Floors.Gauge.IsShell`: a set of positions with a finite height at least 1. It is covered by
  few position balls (`New.Floors.Gauge.positionsOfSize`, each for its own gauge).
* `New.Floors.Gauge.IsShell.setLIntegral_le`: one shell.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.IsShell.setLIntegral_formMajorant_le`: the gain on a remote shell.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.IsShell.setLIntegral_le_inv_height`: a few factors of the gain pay for the
  growth in the height.
* `New.Floors.Gauge.lintegral_le_of_shells`: the sum over the shells. The integral over a shell is
  at most a common bound times the inverse of the height, and `∑ 2⁻¹ ^ i = 2`.

modules.title: Floor measures at the complex place: Haar measure, place datum and gauge
modules.note:
The group `New.Shape.G₁` is the unitary group of the complex form with basis `e_a`, `x_i` (`i : κ`),
`z`, `e*_a`. Here the `e_a, e*_a` are `ϱ` hyperbolic pairs, the `x_i` are orthonormal and
`h(z, z) = -1`. The filling argument at a place needs a place datum (`New.Floors.PlaceData`) and a
gauge (`New.Floors.Gauge`). A place datum consists of measures on the floors of a tower of
subgroups, a set of close pairs of vectors and a box; a gauge consists of sizes in which volumes are
bounded by powers of one constant. The place `ℂ` lies over a real place of the totally real field,
and the docstrings call it a real place.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.ascConv_heisenbergMeasure_eq_besselHaar`: the convolution of the measures
  `New.Floors.Place.heisenbergMeasure` on the Heisenberg groups of the floors is
  `New.Shape.besselHaar`, Lebesgue measure in the free entries of the unipotent group
  `New.Shape.Form.besselU`. Both are invariant, and the Gaussian `New.Floors.dualColumnGaussian`
  fixes the constant.
* `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.complexData`, `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.gauge`: the place datum and
  the gauge at `ℂ`.
* `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.haarRatio`,
  `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.haarRatio_ne_zero_and_groupMeasure_eq_smul`: the product measure
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.groupMeasure` over all floors is a finite positive multiple of the Haar
  measure, and the multiple is bounded by a ratio of volumes `New.volU` of compact unitary groups.
  The bound (`New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.inv_groupMeasure_le`) compares two descriptions of the fibre
  measure of the Gram map on tuples `(y_0, y*_0, …, y_(ϱ-1), y*_(ϱ-1), y_ϱ)`: by Haar measure, and
  by choosing the vectors in turn.
* `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.exists_orthonormal_mul_eq_zero_and_fixed`: common subspaces of two
  points at `ℂ`, orthogonal to `n` given vectors, of each rank up to the free rank less `3 n`.
* `New.Floors.lengthAt`, `New.Floors.inducedLength`, `New.Floors.realDepth`: the Euclidean length at
  a point of `G₁`, the induced length on a quotient along the frame, and the depth of a frame vector
  as the infimum of |ζ|_g² + |ζ|_g'² over its duals ζ.
* `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.stableProducts_eq`, `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.depth_eq`: the set 𝔡_a
  (`New.Floors.PlaceData.stableProducts`) is a disc, and its inverse area
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.depth` is `New.Floors.realDepth` divided by π.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.complexPlace`: The place `ℂ`: `τ = 1/2`, `δ = i/2`, `ν` the image of Lebesgue measure
  under `r ↦ r i`, modulus `‖x‖ ^ 2`, character `x ↦ exp (x - x̄)` and constant
  `kernelBound = π ^ 2`.
* `New.Floors.cellChart`: The chart of floor `l`: if `l = ϱ` and `c ≠ 0`, the boost with parameter
  `c / min 1 ‖c‖`; otherwise the Weyl element `floorWeyl l c`, which is `1` if `l ≥ ϱ` or `c = 0`.
* `New.Floors.cellLaw`: for floor l, the image of the measure with density `cellDensity 𝔰 l` on ℂ
  under `c ↦ (cellChart 𝔰 l c)⁻¹`; the chart is a Weyl element below the top floor ϱ.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorMeasure`: the measure θ_l of floor l of place data; `groupMeasure` is
  𝖬 = (η_{ϱ+1} ∗ θ_{ϱ+1}) ∗ ⋯ ∗ (η₀ ∗ θ₀), with η_l = `Place.heisenbergMeasure l`.
* `New.LeGramFibre J E m`: the law of `g E` under `m` is at most the fibre measure of the Gram map
  on the tuples with the Gram matrix of `E`.

modules.title: Cut Bessel functions at ℂ: integration of the local estimates over shells
modules.note:
This file integrates pointwise local estimates for Bessel functions at the place ℂ over the group.
Every position lies in a dyadic shell, and the positions outside the position ball at a scale are
the remote positions. The place ℂ lies over a real place of the totally real subfield, and the
docstrings call it a real place. The results are the absolute convergence of the forms, an
integrated bound, and a bound for the form of each floor.

Throughout k = card κ and n = ϱ + 1 (`New.Shape.n`), as in the exponents.
`New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.complexData` is the place datum at ℂ: box ‖x‖ ≤ ρ, Haar measure
`New.Floors.PlaceData.groupMeasure`. `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes.gauge` measures sizes by powers of
L. A list p is a head of length j (`New.Floors.Size.IsHead`) if the inverses of p₀ ⋯ p_{l-1}, l ≤ j,
have modulus at most L. `New.Floors.PlaceData.floorForm` is the form of floor j.
`New.Floors.PlaceData.formIntegrandL1Norm` and `New.Floors.PlaceData.formMajorant` bound its
integrand at a position x. `New.Floors.Gauge.weightedSquareProduct` is the weighted product of norms
that their squares are compared to.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel`: the cut, at size ρ, of a normalised Bessel function (`New.IsCutPair`) of
  irreducible type, with the numerical constraints.
* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.lintegral_formMajorant_ne_top`: the forms converge absolutely.
* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.norm_floorForm_le`: a local bound with gain (π / |y|) ^ (2 (k - 5)) gives
  a bound for the form.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.complexPlace`: The place `ℂ`: `τ = 1/2`, `δ = i/2`, `ν` the image of Lebesgue measure
  under `r ↦ r i`, modulus `‖x‖ ^ 2`, character `x ↦ exp (x - x̄)` and constant
  `kernelBound = π ^ 2`.
* `New.IsCutPair`: Two Bessel functions, full and cut (`New.FullOrCut.select`), with base b and
  degree f. The cut one vanishes where `New.besselLength` exceeds b ^ (6 n + 2), n = ϱ + 1. Their L²
  distance is at most b ^ (-r³ f) √(card I), and f also sets their decay.
* `New.Floors.RealPlaceSizes`: The box radius is ρ = b ^ (6 n + 2) ≥ 8 r with b ≥ 2, the exponent
  s > 10⁹ n³ is fixed by k = s + 3 n + 6, and k ≥ n⁷, ϱ ≥ 10⁸.
* `New.headWeight`: The product of max(1, |δ|⁻¹) ^ K over the products δ = p₀ ⋯ p_l, l < j, if these
  have modulus at most R, and 0 otherwise. `New.dampedPower`: The gain r ^ K min(1, r)⁶.
* `weylElem j p`: The Weyl element w_p, with e_a ↦ p_a e*_a and e*_a ↦ e_a / p̄_a for a < j.
  `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsNear`: g is near at j if the coset `partialUnitriangularGroup j` · g meets
  the box. The frame is (e₀, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z), where e_a, e*_a are the hyperbolic pairs of basis
  vectors, and `New.Shape.top` is the position of z. `New.realFrameGram` x is the matrix of the
  products h(f_a, x f_b) of the frame vectors f_a; its entries are the frame entries of x.
* `New.Shape.scaledVolumeRatio`: The constant π ^ ((2ϱ + 1) k) · vol U(k) / vol U(r), where k = card
  κ and r is the rank of G₁. `New.Floors.PlaceData.headDensity`: A product of powers of |p_a q_a|,
  a < j. A normalised integral is an integral over G₁ times this density and
  `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.formConst`.

modules.title: The normalized cell integral Ξ and the local bounds at ℂ for cut Bessel functions
modules.note:
This file defines the normalized cell integral Ξ at the chart of the top floor, proves that it is
continuous, and gives the descent from each floor to the one below. It bounds the mass on the bottom
floor by the position ball and remote positions, and proves decay in the frequency and for unequal
last entries. At the end, a cut Bessel function `F` of a Bessel function `W` satisfies the local
bounds `New.HasLocalBounds` read by the sieve, given bounds on the matrix coefficient of `W` and on
volumes of balls. The place ℂ lies over a real place of the totally real subfield, and the
docstrings call it a real place.

`New.HasLocalBounds` asks for a system of forms `New.SieveSystem` on floors `0, …, ϱ + 1`, each
below the top an integral of the next one.

Throughout `F` is the cut of the Bessel function `W`, n = ϱ + 1, k = card κ and r is the rank of G₁.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.norm_floorForm_zero_le`: the mass at a real place, by the position ball
  and remote positions.
* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.norm_floorForm_wave_le`, `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.norm_floorForm_heads_le`:
  decay in the frequency and for unequal last entries.
* `New.Floors.exists_hasLocalBounds_of_isCutBessel`: the local bounds.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.G₁`: The unitary group of the complex hermitian form made of ϱ hyperbolic planes, the
  standard positive form on κ, and one vector z with h(z, z) = −1. `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: The
  unipotent group 𝖴 of block upper unitriangular elements with middle block 1.
  `New.besselQuotMeasure` computes integrals over 𝖴∖G₁. The frame is (e₀, …, e_{ϱ-1}, z), where e_a,
  e*_a are the hyperbolic pairs of basis vectors, and `New.Shape.top` is the position of z.
  `New.realFrameGram` x is the matrix of the products h(f_a, x f_b) of the frame vectors f_a; its
  entries are the frame entries of x.
* `weylElem j p`: The Weyl element w_p, with e_a ↦ p_a e*_a and e*_a ↦ e_a / p̄_a for a < j.
  `New.wave`: The character c ↦ exp (c - c̄) of ℂ. `New.unitOrOne`: c as a unit if c ≠ 0, and 1
  otherwise.
* `New.Shape.scaledVolumeRatio`: The constant π ^ ((2ϱ + 1) k) · vol U(k) / vol U(r), where k = card
  κ and r is the rank of G₁. `New.dampedPower`: The gain r ^ K min(1, r)⁶.
* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel` (in `New.Spanning.Frames.RealShells`): the cut, at size ρ, of a
  normalised Bessel function of irreducible type, with the numerical constraints.
* `New.Floors.IsCutBessel.formConst` (in `New.Spanning.Frames.RealShells`): the normalising constant
  vol U(k) / vol U(r) / (λ · card I)² of the forms.

The estimates supply the local bounds of the Bessel systems built in
`New.Spanning.Bessel.FillingData`.

modules.title: Place data and gauges at a finite place from the lattice of integral vectors
modules.note:
The estimates on the tower of unitary groups are proved for an abstract place `A` (a
`New.Floors.Place`) with a place datum (`New.Floors.PlaceData`) and a gauge (`New.Floors.Gauge`).
This file supplies these data at a finite place `New.Floors.IntegralPlace`, whose ring of integers
is `integers`, from the lattice of integral vectors. A finite place in this sense may be a finite
set of finite places read as one ring.

* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLatticeData`, `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.exists_isLatticeData`: the
  lattice datum, and its existence.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.gauge`: such a datum with rank bounds, a character
  trivial on traces and a unimodular group, and its gauges.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.heisenbergMeasure_eq_floorModulus`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.ascConv_mconv_unitaryLevel_coset`: masses of the
  congruence subgroup `K(g)` and its cosets.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.groupMeasure_boxSet_le`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.le_partialGroupMeasure_boxSet`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.isHaarMeasure_groupMeasure`: bounds for the mass of
  the group of integral isometries, and the fact that `F.groupMeasure` is a Haar measure.

The form `h` has Gram matrix `T.splitGram`: `ϱ` hyperbolic planes and a middle block `T`. The number
`ϱ` comes from the shape `𝔰`. `New.unitaryLevel integers g J` is the congruence subgroup `K(g)` of
the unitary group (integral elements congruent to `1` modulo `g`), `P.modulus u` is the factor by
which a unit `u` scales the volume, and `z` is the last vector of the frame e_0, …, e_(ϱ-1), z.

Notions from other files:
* `New.latticeMiddleGram`: The Gram matrix of X₀ ⊕ Az in the basis x_i (i ≠ k₀), v, z, where
  v = x_{k₀}/p̄ + z/N and N = p p̄.
* `New.idealZeta`: The ideal zeta sum ∑ [R : I]^(−s) over the ideals I of finite index in R, for a
  natural number s, with values in [0, ∞].
* `New.Floors.HyperbolicBasis`: A basis of the middle block made of a first hyperbolic pair, `m`
  more pairs and an orthonormal part indexed by `ι`.
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`, `New.Shape.Form.besselH`: The block upper unitriangular isometries, and
  the isometries that fix all basis vectors outside X₀.

modules.title: The Bessel vector at the finite places
modules.note:
Let `A` collect finitely many finite places, with integers `R` and character `ψ`, and let `F` be a
large lattice datum of modulus `g` for the unitary group `T.G`. Write `𝖴 = T.besselU`, `K(g)` for
the principal congruence subgroup and `K = K(1)`, and let `K(g) ≤ Z ≤ K`. This file constructs a cut
Bessel function from the translates of the Bessel character by the cosets of `K(g)` in `Z`, and
computes its correlations and norms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar`: the Bessel character of `𝖴`, extended to `𝖴 K(g)`
  and by zero outside it.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup.besselVector`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.isCut_besselVector`: the vector of its translates by
  the cosets of `K(g)` in `Z`; it is a cut Bessel function.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.unipotentMass_mul_inner_besselVector`: its
  correlations as integrals over `𝖴` of the extended character, cut off by `Z`.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.lintegral_enorm_sq_besselVector`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.pairingNormSq_mul_le_massRatio`: its norms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Shape.Form.besselU`: the Bessel unipotent group `𝖴` of the block upper unitriangular
  isometries of `T.splitGram`.
* `New.simpleRootSum`: the sum `σ(s)` of the entries of `s` just above the diagonal of its block on
  the frame vectors.
* `New.unitaryLevel`: `unitaryLevel R g J` is the group `K(g)` of integral isometries of `J` that
  are congruent to `1` modulo the unit `g`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData`: the data `F` of a place, among them the modulus `F.levelUnit`, the compact
  set `F.boxSet` and the measures whose product over all floors is `F.groupMeasure`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsCut`: a Bessel function of frequency `F.levelUnit⁻¹` that vanishes off the
  translates of `F.boxSet` by `𝖴`.

modules.title: Depth, heads and far positions at the finite places
modules.note:
This file proves the facts about a large lattice datum at the finite places that bound the local
Bessel kernels: the sets 𝔡_a are fractional ideals, the heads of a nonvanishing form have integral
leading products, and a position far from the identity forces a small ideal. Here `R = integers` is
the ring of integers of `A`, K is the group of integral points of the unitary group (in statements,
`K : ℕ` is an exponent), K(g) is its principal congruence subgroup of level `g = F.levelUnit`, and
`n = 𝔰.n = ϱ + 1`. In the gauge `Γ` of scale `α` an element `a` has size `i` if `α ^ i * a ∈ R`, and
losses are powers of `Γ.loss = 2 / modulus α`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.exists_ideal_depth_eq`: at a near point the products
  with the stable vectors form an ideal of `R`, and the depth is its index.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.prod_mem_of_formMajorant_ne_zero`: the forms vanish
  unless the leading products of both heads are integral.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.exists_gauge_of_formMajorant_ne_zero`: a scale
  adapted to two heads.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.exists_volume_stableProducts_le`: a large denominator
  of `(x - 1) / g` forces a deep vector.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData`: the place data is given by a lattice, in a
  unimodular unitary group of large rank; its box `F.boxSet` is K.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.stableProducts`: the set 𝔡_a of the products of e_a with the vectors that
  are stable at two points `x` and `x * y`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IsNear`: `x` is near at `j` if a translate of `x` by
  `T.partialUnitriangularGroup j` lies in the box.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup.besselVector`: for a group `Z` with K(g) ≤ Z ≤ K, the
  vector whose coordinate at the coset K(g) z is `extendedBesselChar F.levelUnit (y * z⁻¹)`.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.formMajorant`: an integral of moduli of orbital integrals that bounds the
  form of two heads.

modules.title: Shells, decay and mass at the finite places
modules.note:
The positions `x` are sorted by the ideal of the denominators of `(x - 1) / g`, and into dyadic
shells by its index. The sum over the shells gives the decay of the forms in the frequency and the
mass. Here `R = P.integers` is the ring of integers of `A`, `g = F.levelUnit` is the level unit of
the place datum `F`, `ϱ = 𝔰.ϱ`, `n = 𝔰.n = ϱ + 1` and `k = 𝔰.k`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.gauge`: the gauge of scale `α`, for a unit `α` of `A`
  that is integral and fixed by the involution; size `j` means `α ^ j * x ∈ R`, and the loss is
  `2 / modulus α`.
* `New.Floors.Size.IsHead`: `p` is a head of length `j` if the inverses of the products
  `p 0 ⋯ p (l - 1)`, `l ≤ j`, have size 1.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.HasDeepVector`: at a given position, every active point has a vector after
  the head of at least the given depth.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.formIntegrandL1Norm`, `New.Floors.PlaceData.formMajorant`: the modulus of
  the integrand of the form of floor `j` at a position, and a majorant of it that does not depend on
  the weight.
* `New.Floors.PlaceData.IntermediateGroup`: an integral group `Z` that contains the congruence group
  `K(g) = F.congruenceSubgroup`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.PlaceData.dyadicShell`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.isShell_dyadicShell`: the shells; each collects few
  ideals.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.lintegral_shells_le`: the sum over the shells.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.enorm_floorForm_le`: the decay in the frequency.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.setLIntegral_compl_congruenceSubgroup_le`,
  `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.massIntegral_le_main_add_error`: the positions
  outside `K(g)` contribute little to the mass.

modules.title: Fiber measures of the standard form, and the top quadric by its last entry
modules.note:
At a finite place and in rank at least two, the volume of `κ → A` disintegrates along `ω ↦ ω* ω`
into the fiber measures `Place.normFiberMeasure`. The main result,
`HyperbolicBasis.integral_floorQuadricMeasure_top`, writes the measure of the quadric of vectors of
norm `-N` in `X₀ ⊕ A z` as an integral, over the last entry `t = ⟨z, y⟩` of a vector `y`, of the
fiber measures of the spheres `ω* ω = t t̄ / N - N` in `X₀`.

Notions from other files:

* `Place A`: a locally compact star ring with Haar volume, a multiplicative `modulus`, skew unit
  `δ = skewUnit` and Haar measure `skewMeasure` on the skew elements; `IntegralPlace A` is a finite
  place, or a finite set of finite places read as one ring.
* `P.IsDisintegration μ J l`: the measures `l b`, for skew `b`, are the fiber measures of `μ` on the
  quadrics `x* J x = δ⁻¹ b` and depend continuously on `b`.
* `flatChart S b`, `P.quadricMeasure S b`: coordinates and measure on the quadric of norm `δ⁻¹ b`
  for `planeSumGram S`, the Gram matrix of a hyperbolic plane plus `S`.
* `latticeMiddleGram 𝔰 N`: the Gram matrix of `X₀ ⊕ A z`, where `X₀` has an orthonormal basis `x_i`
  indexed by `𝔰.κ` and `z` has norm `-N`, `N = π π̄`, in the lattice basis `x_i` (`i ≠ k₀`),
  `v = x_{k₀} / π̄ + z / N`, `z`. For such a Gram matrix `T : 𝔰.Form A`, the matrix `T.splitGram`
  is that of the whole space, with hyperbolic planes added.
* `vectorOfLastEntry π t x`: the vector `y = x - (π π̄)⁻¹ t z` of `X₀ ⊕ A z`, in the lattice basis
  of the whole space. Its pairing `⟨z, y⟩` with the last frame vector `z`, called its last entry, is
  `t`.

modules.title: Scaled orbital integrals of the finite Bessel vector on the floor group
modules.note:
A finite set of finite places is read as one ring (`IntegralPlace`); the docstrings call it a finite
place. This file defines the scaled orbital integrals `PlaceData.scaledOrbitalIntegral`. These are
normalized orbital integrals of the finite Bessel vector at the elements `w_p l⁻¹` with head `p` and
link `l⁻¹`. It also defines the integrand `PlaceData.unfoldedPairing` of their pairing. At a large
lattice datum it shows three things. The scaled orbital integrals are locally constant in the head
and on the floor group G^(ϱ). They vanish off a compact set. Their pairings are integrable over
`besselH`. It also writes the form `F.floorForm 𝔰.ϱ`, with a weight on the last diagonal entry of
`T.frameGram`, as an integral of these pairings. General lemmas give compactly supported step
extensions of locally constant functions and the nonnegativity of sums of integrals against a
matrix.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.exists_isCompact_scaledOrbitalIntegral_support`: Let
  `F` be a large lattice datum. The scaled orbital integral `scaledOrbitalIntegral Z p l`, a density
  times `∫ W y ⊗ (W (l w_p⁻¹ y))^*` over the unitary group, with `W` the finite Bessel vector of `Z`
  and `w_p` the Weyl element of the head `p`, vanishes for the `l` in the floor group G^(ϱ) outside
  some compact set.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.inner_scaledOrbitalIntegral`: At a large lattice
  datum `F` and for `l` in the floor group G^(ϱ), the pairing of the scaled orbital integrals with
  heads `p`, `q` at `l` is the density `F.headDensity 𝔰.ϱ p q` of the two heads times the integral
  of the integrand `unfoldedPairing Z p q l` over two copies of the group.

Notions from other files:
* `T.floorGroup l`, written G^(l), fixes the basis vectors of the floors below `l` in the unitary
  group `T.G`; `besselH` is `T.floorGroup 𝔰.n` with `𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1`, which also fixes the last frame
  vector `z`, in position `𝔰.top`; `orbitPoint 𝔰.top l` is `l⁻¹ z`.
* Place data `F` gives measures on these groups (`F.measureH` on `besselH`) and a congruence
  subgroup `F.congruenceSubgroup`; `P.IsLargeLatticeData F` says that it is large lattice data at a
  finite place `P`.
* `Z` is a group between `F.congruenceSubgroup` and the integral unitary group, and `Z.besselVector`
  is the vector of the finite Bessel functions of the cosets of `F.congruenceSubgroup` in `Z`.
* `weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p` is the Weyl element of a sequence `p` of units. An element `w_p l⁻¹` with `l` in
  the floor group has head `p` and link `l⁻¹`. The sequence is a head for a gauge `Γ` (a family of
  compact bounds on entries) if its inverse partial products are bounded by the gauge.

modules.title: The density at the last entry
modules.note:
A finite set of finite places is read as one ring (`IntegralPlace`); the docstrings call it a finite
place. This file defines the pairing over a fibre and the density at the last entry. The pairing of
the scaled orbital integrals over the fixer of `z` in G^(ϱ), `PlaceData.fiberPairing`, is a function
of `e = l⁻¹ z` on the last vector quadric. At a large lattice datum it agrees there with a step
function. Its integral over the vectors `e` with a given pairing `⟨z, e⟩` is the density
`PlaceData.lastEntryDensity`. The file proves four things. This density is continuous. Its sums
against positive semidefinite matrices, over heads with one common last entry, are nonnegative. Its
Fourier transform in the last entry is the form of floor `𝔰.ϱ`. Finally, the file bounds, by the
fiber pairing at a point, the sums of the pairings of scaled orbital integrals over the congruence
cosets of the links that lie over that point.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.sum_fiberPairing_nonneg`: At a large lattice datum
  `F` and at every vector `e`, the sum of the fiber pairings of the heads `ω a` against a positive
  semidefinite matrix `R` is a nonnegative real.
* `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.IsLargeLatticeData.floorForm_top_eq_integral_floorQuadric`: At a large
  lattice datum `F`, the form `F.floorForm 𝔰.ϱ` with the weight `ψ (ξ θ)` on the last diagonal entry
  `θ` of the frame Gram matrix is the integral, over the points `e` of the last vector quadric, of
  `ψ (ξ ⟨z, e⟩)` (`z` the last frame vector) times any continuous function `Φ` that extends the
  fiber pairing.

Notions from other files:
* `T.floorGroup l`, written G^(l), fixes the basis vectors of the floors below `l` in the unitary
  group `T.G`; `besselH` is `T.floorGroup 𝔰.n` with `𝔰.n = 𝔰.ϱ + 1`, which also fixes the last frame
  vector `z`, in position `𝔰.top`; `orbitPoint 𝔰.top l` is `l⁻¹ z`.
* Place data `F` give measures on these groups (`F.measureH` on `besselH`) and a congruence subgroup
  `F.congruenceSubgroup`; `P.IsLargeLatticeData F` says that they are large lattice data at a finite
  place `P`.
* `Z` is a group between `F.congruenceSubgroup` and the integral unitary group, and `Z.besselVector`
  is the vector of the finite Bessel functions of the cosets of `F.congruenceSubgroup` in `Z`.
* `weylElem 𝔰.ϱ p` is the Weyl element of a sequence `p` of units. An element `w_p l⁻¹` with `l` in
  the floor group has head `p` and link `l⁻¹`. The sequence is a head for a gauge `Γ` (a family of
  compact bounds on entries) if its inverse partial products are bounded by the gauge.
* `PlaceData.scaledOrbitalIntegral` (in `New.Spanning.Frames.TopCorrelation`) is the normalized
  orbital integral of the finite Bessel vector of `Z` at `w_p l⁻¹`, indexed by pairs of cosets.

modules.title: Groups that fix given vectors at chosen places have a small mass integral
modules.note:
Let `S` be an admissible filling with base `b = S.b`, and `T` a finite set of finite places of `E`
stable under conjugation. The product `LocProd T` of the completions at `T` is read as one ring,
with integers `R` (`New.Floors.IntegralPlace`), and `F` is a filling datum on it, of modulus
`g = F.levelUnit`. An `F.IntermediateGroup` is a group `Z` with `K(g) ≤ Z ≤ K`, for the integral
unitary group `K` and its congruence subgroup `K(g)` (both `New.unitaryLevel`). `F.groupMeasure` is
a Haar measure on the unitary group, and `F.massIntegral Z` is the mass integral, the number ∫ |∫_Z
χ_g(y x y⁻¹) dy|² dx, where χ_g is `New.Floors.IntegralPlace.extendedBesselChar g`.

* `New.Filling.volume_integers_diff_intUnits_le`: at the chosen places and their conjugates
  (`New.Filling.chosenPlacesAndConj`), few integers are not units.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_one_place`: for one place `w`, some group `Z`
  contains the elements that fix the given vectors, and `F.massIntegral Z / F.groupMeasure Z` is
  smaller than `F.massIntegral K / F.groupMeasure K` by at least the factor `b ^ (6 * 𝔰.k)` (for no
  place, the factor is `1`). Here `𝔰.k` is the rank of the block `X₀` of the shape `𝔰`. The proof
  takes the stabiliser of the vector at `w`, which has large index in `K`.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData.exists_intermediateGroup_places`: for several places, take the product;
  the factors multiply. The places of `T` are cut into the fibres `New.Filling.placeFiber` of a map
  `blk`; `New.Filling.evalFiber` and `New.Filling.toFibers` restrict elements of `LocProd T` and
  unitary matrices to the fibres.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Filling`: `S.levelPrime 0` and `S.levelPrime 1` are the level primes `p₀` and `p₁`,
  `S.chosenPlaces i` is the finite set of chosen places of norm `pᵢ`, and `S.ideleM` is the level
  `M = p₀ p₁` as a finite idele.
* `New.Filling.IsFillingData`: `F` is a large lattice datum on `LocProd T` whose modulus is the
  component of `M` at `T` and whose character is `S.charOnPlaces T`.
* `New.Filling.latticeStabilizer`: the integral elements of the finite adelic unitary group;
  `S.reduction` reduces them modulo the chosen places, `S.toPlaces T` takes components at `T`.
* `New.Filling.vectorFixer`: for a chosen place `w` and `d = (ε, v)`, the elements of `S.ResidueGL`
  (the product of the general linear groups over the residue fields) that fix the vector of the span
  of the frame with coordinates `v ≠ 0`, modulo `w` if `ε` is false and modulo its conjugate if `ε`
  is true; `S.fixer Sg d` is the intersection of these groups over `w ∈ Sg`.
